candidates/opt-adcirc.title: ADCIRC regional hydraulics
candidates/opt-adcirc.content:
ADCIRC
v56.2.1 commit 5d4dfad3a35c6384a6d9548a03d0b649ab315748; repository. Core LICENSE LGPL-3.0-or-later; evaluate obligations and all linked dependencies before embedding. VEWs and condensed nodes avoid the narrow-channel cross-width CFL limit, support paired wall nodes and channel/floodplain flow, and require lumped explicit mode. Subgrid lookup preprocessing is separate. Native build includes shared/static library, ADCIRC_Run(NTIME_STP) advances bounded steps but uses module-global state and invokes writeOutput2D. It is not demonstrated reentrant, C-ABI or editable-topology API. Neither combined VEW+subgrid qualification, finite local conservation and dry rainfall, dynamic geometry repair, nor target-machine cost is established. 2025 resolution study finds inadequate channel/barrier resolution degrades results even with subgrid. First screen with actual unmodified upstream regional fixtures, including the VEW test, then check finite inventory, terrain repair and runtime budgets. Not an approved dependency. See evidence.

candidates/opt-davudk-terrain.title: Procedural World Generation
candidates/opt-davudk-terrain.content:
Procedural World Generation refinement
Source-screened 25 November 2026 at f7b1daa7a61af3ce9bf7e06fa77dfc4fcf89296c. MIT license, manifest, CPU terrain and carve routines, analytic height and channel profile, streamed globe tiles, globe sampling, network extraction, graph storage.
Promising permissive full formation alternative and geometry-realization donor. extractNetwork groups thresholded drainage cells into reaches and represents lake outlets and terminal lakes; GraphBuilder finalizes typed arrays. riverSegments and carveSegmentCpu rasterize channel/valley caps from segment geometry, with a parabolic profile in carveProfile. buildTileCpu combines coarse samples, deterministic noise, supplied river segments, bed/shore bounds and local thermal relaxation. These are specific existing routines that can be exercised independently of WebGL rendering, with narrow integration/port work. Reuse the tested parts with required notices, not the whole browser app.
Limitations: the macro network consumes coarse routing. Additional source inspection identified a real deterministic local creek generator, described below; it is not yet qualified as authoritative fine hydraulic topology. Streamed spherical tiles use margins and residency-dependent blends/fallbacks. The current sphere segment lookup iterates all tile buckets, so do not inherit that hot-path complexity. Flat detail is a dense 2048/4096 map; GPU and CPU paths differ. The profile uses supplied water levels and visual shoreline bounds, so separate immutable bank/bed geometry from live water stage before use. Its thermal pass clamps terrain and is not a conservative live sediment solver. Avoid a minimum channel width tied to coarse render texels. No finite water inventory, edited volumetric terrain or qualified Godot integration. No target-hardware measurement.
Qualification: compare source CPU routines against their native C++/Rust integration on a two-region anchored drainage fixture; preserve bankfull geometry and explicit terminal basins; test cold adjacent pages in opposite orders, partial residency, boundary samples and actual voxel/analytic profile agreement. Separately close regional tributary/outlet construction. No code has been incorporated.
Full generator and creek review
Pipeline order, erosion stages, stream-power solver, configuration, landforms, arid, karst, sea cliffs, hydrology. The actual pipeline builds plates, base relief, stamps, landscape evolution, macro refinement, climate, glacial landforms, other landforms, hydrology, biomes and landmarks. It explicitly generates terraced mesas/buttes/escarpments, coastal cliffs and sea stacks, dolines, towers and cenotes, volcanism, glacial/coastal formations and water features. The stream-power solver advances uplift/incision/diffusion over iterations with dt in years (250,000 years per iteration at the inspected stage). The top-level geologicAge is a 0–1 parameter influencing terrain characteristics and iteration settings. This is genuine numerical landscape evolution during staged generation, but not the same as GeoGenesis’s persistent multi-process geological time loop. Hydrology and climate are generation-time diagnostics, not a verified live finite weather/water cycle.
Correction to the initial refinement screen: creekGen.ts already supplies seeded D8 trunks and per-cell creek growth against a heightAt callback, an indexed segment representation, runoff-derived width/depth and connections to other channels, water or sinks. tests/creeks.test.ts contains order/batch consistency, terminal, monotonicity, no-crossing and performance assertions. These are source-inspected tests, not independently executed results. The manager selects visible cells/tier and caches ribbon graphs; the generator recomputes D8 receivers from macro elevations, permits sinks and has fallback joins. Its actual fine-path sampling depends on the supplied rendered height callback. For Breachborn replace that callback with stable authoritative geometry, test parent routing/closed-basin agreement and finite water ownership, and make the feature recipe independent of the camera. The existing local creek algorithm materially reduces the earlier presumed custom refinement gap but does not close it.
The headless benchmark harness directly invokes the pipeline without the viewer. Use that entry point for a bounded comparison before porting large TypeScript components. Existing demo quality and test assertions do not establish 4,000 km runtime performance or native integration. See formation comparison.
Creek quality and scale correction (user review, 25 November 2026)
The user finds the demo’s small streams unusually narrow/odd, likes its explicit landform and terracing algorithms, and considers missing wind erosion and mineral deposits important. This is aesthetic feedback, not a measured failure of all PWG waterways.

Creek geometry hardcodes width = clamp(4  sqrt(Q)  aridFactor, 1, 8) m and depth = clamp(0.35 * Q^0.4, 0.1, 1.5) m. Q is a mean annual runoff-derived discharge in m³/s, aridFactor 1.5 below 100 mm/year runoff, otherwise 1. These are render-tributary limits, not universal river limits. Creek source area 0.2 km², head count 1–64 and step length 20–40 m are source constants, with climate modulation of source area.
Main river geometry uses 4  sqrt(Q), arid multiplier 1.5 and steep-slope multiplier 0.4; no 8 m maximum in that width calculation. Main-river depth uses 0.35  Q^0.4 with 0.1 m minimum. Macro hydro derives channel-head area threshold as max(8 / riverDensity², 2.5 * cellKm²); minimum node spacing 250 m. Controls expose density, meander, lakes and landform controls; documented expert process constants are not proof creek caps are exposed in the demo. At 4 km cells, macro threshold floor is 40 km²; a render-tier split must not impose physical channel size or lose tributaries.
Creek growth confines fine tributaries to a cell, chooses seeded separated heads, follows sampled slopes, mixes meander noise, heading momentum and nearest-channel attraction (stronger near borders/on flats) and uses forced joins when stuck. These can explain odd paths; they are plausible causes, not proof of the user’s exact observed artifact. The renderer-driven callback and fixed visual cell boundaries are inappropriate as final authority.
Arid landforms classify sand seas and dune orientation using aridity, topography and wind belts. Useful initial morphology/visual prior; no verified finite sediment deflation/transport/deposition kernel. Do not credit dune appearance as wind erosion. No qualified mineral prospectivity/3D deposit model in PWG.

Prefer existing main reach extraction, terraces and landform functions as donors. Treat creek growth as optional candidate requiring physical quality qualification; no blanket port. Use continuous configurable geometry across stream orders, with reference/bankfull geometry distinct from transient wetted width/stage. Test catchment continuity, natural planform, confluence area accounting, bed continuity, small/medium/large channel coverage and view-independent geometry. Preserve numerical bounds for valid configuration, not the 8 m cap. See formation comparison.
V1 selects the standalone channel shape, meander and profile algorithms for bounded refinement of GeoGenesis terrain. The first terrain package established the aged source. The scoped PWG curve and profile port now supplies a shared carved bed and measured sections in a display-backed terrain scene. Persistent material, edits and fully connected basin outlets are still open. V1 technical plan
The adopted sources are the pinned meander and channel geometry routines and the carve profile in the height function. The first test uses a bounded D8 corridor, existing endpoints and upstream discharge as a channel sizing prior. V1 implementation evidence

candidates/opt-geogenesis.title: GeoGenesis
candidates/opt-geogenesis.content:
GeoGenesis
Repository: github.com/nico2525nn/geogenesis ; prior research pin aa898282cbddc71a515deb58a0aa41f649e00147. Prior source inspection: flat fields and Simulation::new/step, no supplied C ABI. Single-shot age; tiled initial relief only. Export final original elevation, soil/geology/climate/receiver fields; refresh after aging. Diagnostic filled depth/discharge is not finite water. Author 256² 105 ms, 512² 420 ms, 1024² 1.82 s; 512² aging 65 ms per 10,000 modeled years; no Breachborn benchmark. Qualify on target hardware and actual geography. Core pilot, not mature turnkey engine.
Comparative formation review
Initial landforms, stratigraphy, chemical erosion, minerals, simulation driver. Initial relief contains plateaus, mesas, rifts, ranges, trenches, peaks and calderas; age advances coupled surface processes in physical years. Stratigraphic columns include rock properties, layer thickness, dip, fault displacement and age, potentially useful for native material queries. Mineral outputs score prospectivity and illustrative inventory, not 3D ore-body formation. Karst dissolution modifies surface elevations, not an underground tunnel network. Both initial and aged terrain are heightfields, not fully volumetric terrain.
The user finds the Procedural World Generation demo more compelling aesthetically. Reopen the surface-formation selection as a bounded comparison with OPT-DAVUDK-TERRAIN; GeoGenesis remains the existing provisional choice until selection evidence is obtained. See formation comparison. No source or runtime benchmark was executed.
Wind erosion and geological-material reuse
The user specifically values wind erosion and mineral deposits. The existing aeolian process takes mutable World, Params, Climate and geological dt in years. It removes loose cover using wind threshold, vegetation shielding, aridity and sediment/soil supply, sends saltation downwind to nearby cells, deposits finer loess and reports residual export. It uses one parameter wind vector snapped to D8, one-to-three-cell transport and full-grid scratch; not local variable wind, a resolved dust atmosphere, or resolution-independent physical transport. It computes residual export from erosion/deposition, not an independently measured finite dust receiver. Qualify actual mass/volume transfers, cell area and interval mapping; for runtime adapt to actual wind/moisture and sediment owner rather than periodically running the full geological world. Minerals provides deterministic prospectivity and illustrative endowment from geology and climate; physical ore bodies, finite mining/depletion and 3D strata remain separate realization work. Geology is a relevant rock/strata donor. These reinforce GeoGenesis’s provisional advantage as age/material backbone. Port only tested PWG morphology/feature kernels if that wins; alternatively qualify a contained GeoGenesis process/material adapter if PWG wins. No whole second mutable formation world.
Source-confirmed process extension boundary
At the prior pin, ProcessPlugin and plugin documentation provide a native compile-time Rust extension mechanism. Simulation::with_plugins registers deterministic Send + Sync processes; the context exposes mutable World, read-only parameters/climate/hydrology/geology, grid, dt and elapsed years. apply returns a MassBalance that the driver adds to its ledger. The example impact process excavates a crater and deposits part of the ejecta. Driver invokes plugins after the built-in process chain and updates exposed geological surface afterward. A plugin cannot assume its read-only hydrology/climate snapshots already reflect the latest terrain mutation or earlier plugin in that step. Recompute dependent data at appropriate barriers and before final export. This is not a dynamic hot-load feature, automatic plugin parameter UI, proof of material conservation, or an existing live-game terrain-edit API. Use configured generation-time processes or explicit formation stages with measured cost; do not add a redundant plugin runtime. Port selected PWG landform functions only after verifying inputs, units, material effects and deterministic geometry. Source confirmed; not built or benchmarked.
Discharge-driven aging qualification (26 November 2026)
Rechecked the original pin. Hydrology estimates annual local runoff from precipitation, parameterized infiltration, evapotranspiration and baseflow, and accumulates discharge in m³/year. Main fluvial laws use drainage area A, slope S, rock erodibility and vegetation; both the detachment-limited and depositional passes use A^m, not accumulated Q directly. Bank erosion does use estimated annual discharge for width and a stream-power proxy. Do not claim full rainfall/discharge-driven incision from the existing implementation. The area surrogate is established for long-term landscape evolution but can underrepresent spatially variable runoff and changes in rainfall intensity.
Qualification recommendation: compare the stock area law with a calibrated discharge-based variant of the existing implicit solver (not a second erosion engine), using accumulated effective runoff and compatible units/thresholds. Reference discharge-based incision, discharge variability and incision thresholds, and Landlab SharedStreamPower as independent mathematical/implementation controls. Test matched wet/dry catchments with equal initial geometry/material, actual runoff, and a wet/dry variability case. Compare timestep/resolution convergence, drainage, soil/sediment budget, channel geometry and cost before selecting adaptation. No new port or benchmark performed.
V1 incorporates the unchanged pinned MIT core for formation and geological aging. The scoped build and bounded parcel use completed successfully. Large-world formation, PWG geometry and coupled downstream behavior remain open. First V1 terrain evidence

candidates/opt-libmorton.title: libmorton
candidates/opt-libmorton.content:
libmorton
MIT license, header. Exposes inline 2D/3D 32-bit and 64-bit Morton encode/decode, with compile-time instruction-set branches and portable alternatives. Useful for sorting irregular region/feature work if measured locality improves. It does not provide paging, hierarchy ownership, geometric queries or route graphs. Do not add to initial dense page lookup: row-major arithmetic is simpler and predictable. A 64-bit 3D Morton code cannot represent unlimited full-world metre coordinates; use stable signed coordinates plus range-checked local or 2D encoding. Qualify actual CPU feature dispatch and ARM portability before adoption. No benchmark.

MAIForge regional terrain

Native Rust project builds a chart-wide drainage skeleton constrained to coarse receiver/outlet basins, regional relief windows and fine tiles. The skeleton distinguishes terminal segments, coarse edges and headwater extensions. Its experimental seam module uses fixed drainage/sea/lake seeds rather than treating arbitrary tile edges as outlets, and marks fills or donor dependencies contaminated by the window boundary. This is a directly relevant research question for independently generated regions. The project’s own README says its example fails strict drainage/coast/mean-height quality checks. It is not a finished replacement, and the region crate explicitly uses AGPL-3.0-only. Alternative licensing is mentioned by the project but not granted to us. Do not incorporate its code; evaluate published algorithms independently and use only as a conceptual comparison unless a compatible license is actually obtained. No benchmark performed.

candidates/opt-meanderpy.title: MeanderPy kinematic river migration
candidates/opt-meanderpy.content:
MeanderPy
Apache-2.0 source, inspected 26 November 2026 at commit 0b836b4896ced7e70aab6d81972d81bc72e86d57. README, source, Howard & Knutson. Stock method moves centerline using dimensionless curvature, empirical migration coefficient, exponentially weighted upstream curvature, depth/friction-dependent weight and sinuosity; supports centerline resampling and cutoff records. Flow velocity is explicitly not a direct input; not a water solver or complete material-conserving channel morphodynamic model. Do not import plotting/history/3D reconstruction dependencies by default. Qualify bounded migration in alluvial corridors, actual discharge/erosive exposure modulation, rock/vegetation and reinforced-bank constraints, confluence continuity, sediment/material changes, new water ownership for cutoffs and local topology invalidation. Compare original method and known-answer tests; no engine implementation or visual benchmark.
Source computemigration_rate loops over all upstream nodes for each node (quadratic work). With constant alpha along one reach, exponential weighting is algebraically reducible: A_i=R_i+exp(-alphads[i-1])A(i-1), Bi=1+exp(-alphads[i-1])B(i-1), then omegaR_i+gammaA_i/B_i. Independent NumPy/Python mathematical probe, nonuniform spacing 4–16 m, seeded random rates, alpha=.002, omega=-1, gamma=2.5: direct sum vs recurrence max absolute difference 1.39e-17 (256), 2.08e-17 (2048/8192). Single illustrative process CPU run at 8192 nodes direct 256.11ms vs recurrence 4.34ms (~59x), not a benchmark of upstream complete model, port, cutoffs, terrain edits or target hardware. This only establishes equivalence of one scalar weighting calculation with the fixed-alpha assumption; preserve source boundary/padding behavior. No new bespoke hydraulic solver proposed.

candidates/opt-mizuroute.title: mizuRoute IRF reach routing
candidates/opt-mizuroute.content:
mizuRoute IRF reach routing
Pin 0843ee874d165772bfbfa2368ee4f65f5fdfeac9, GitHub license metadata Apache-2.0 (individual notices/transitive review pending; license fetch disconnected). IRF source, kinematic wave, methods. conv_upsbas_qr uses finite future-weighted discharge queue, reach volume, clamped outflow and shift. Separate volume and forecast queue must NOT be treated as two stocks; source clamps and shifts a release and has a short-reach pass-through branch resetting reach volume. Qualify residual/withdrawal reconciliation and prohibit losing delayed amounts on topology change. Convolution costs scale with queue length; use bounded circular buffer, analytic linear-reservoir control, event-driven/long-horizon scheduling only where verified. Lagrangian wave variant allocates temporary and per-reach wave arrays; not default. Ordinary downhill only: no backwater/reversal/floodplain control, promote before downstream head influence matters. Transfer pending stock and timing conservatively on mode change. No benchmark or adoption.

candidates/opt-overlandflow.title: Landlab OverlandFlow
candidates/opt-overlandflow.content:
Landlab OverlandFlow
Source inspection 25 November 2026. Landlab pin 2e2c16093afb24093b7d75c577dad519423f23d3; component, license, method documentation, validation paper.
Actual capability: de Almeida local-inertial shallow-water approximation. It reads grid node bed/depth, link discharge, Manning roughness and water-surface gradients, computes face discharge and updates depth by rainfall minus flux divergence. Adaptive stability interval depends on grid spacing and maximum depth. Useful bounded fine/reference model for lake-at-rest, backwater, wetting and draining and signed head-driven flows.
Critical qualification: Constructor adds h_init water to node depths; the steep-slope branch floors low depths after updates. These are not acceptable unaccounted sources in a finite game inventory. The Python/NumPy raster grid is not a subgrid storage-curve solver. Need explicit face width/discharge units (documentation and source conventions must be checked), physical boundary conditions, donor limits, and actual accepted volume conservation. No direct runtime adoption or blanket per-metre flood solving. Use as an independent numerical reference or evaluate extraction of narrow MIT kernels only after proof. No candidate benchmark run.

candidates/opt-river-tree.title: Hydrological construction trees
candidates/opt-river-tree.content:
Hydrological construction trees
Primary publication: doi.org/10.1145/2461912.2461996 . The abstract establishes a geometric drainage graph, watershed classification and analytic feature-composition tree with carving/blending and varying visual LOD. This is the relevant shape of an age-preserving refinement method: constrain a region’s outlets and river graph, then synthesize land around those features. It does not establish finite water or runtime edits, and no licensed author implementation has been qualified.
A third-party implementation was inspected at github.com/bmelaiths/terrainHydrology/tree/09366289a002e7b58290b0cbd76c5b241c7cbfe6 . Its src/hydrology.py is a Python raster-export program using NumPy/SciPy, NetworkX, OpenCV, Shapely and Rasterio. README excludes inland lakes and the pinned tree has no root reuse license. Do not copy this implementation. Treat paper methods as research and seek a permissive reusable kernel, not a ready-made dependency. No benchmark run.

candidates/opt-terrain-generator.content:
terrain-generator 0.3.1
Source inspection 25 November 2026. Pin 5a6c0866d773169dcb5be73e006bfb475b31e859; manifest, library API, hydrology, C ABI, builder. Core license declaration Apache-2.0; default-features=false retains noise =0.9.0. Verify transitive licenses before incorporation.
Actual capability: Flat row-major Grid buffers, deterministic D8 accumulation and Priority-Flood with a separate filled height field, ocean connectivity from map boundaries, river/lake masks, optional droplet erosion and basin breaching. The C ABI already exposes an opaque terrain owner, ABI/version/status checks and borrowed read-only layer pointers; useful model for a GeoGenesis adapter.
Limitation: The public builder generates its own normalized dense heightmap, rather than accepting an existing aged coarse field and explicit tile-boundary constraints. Hydrology is a private module; no public receiver graph or elevation-in-metres runtime handoff. The flood-fill assumes finite map boundaries are outlets, ordering of f32 bit patterns assumes nonnegative heights, every cell adds one unit of rainfall, and filled depressions are geometry masks rather than finite lakes. Whole-map sort/heap/arrays and droplet aging do not prove bounded refinement. Do not substitute it for GeoGenesis or call it independently on tiles.
Next: Determine whether its small permissive routing/geometry functions can be isolated with explicit supplied outlet/saddle constraints and original bed preserved; compare against other permissive Priority-Flood donors. Source inspected, not built or benchmarked.

V1 ports the narrow signed local-inertial surface law and selected profile/stability functions. Bounded generated gate flow and reversal passed. contracts/con-lod.title: Spatial levels and ownership transfers
contracts/con-lod.content:
Spatial levels and ownership transfers
Define per domain: stable spatial key, authoritative resolution, summary resolution, detail residency reason, temporal cadence, promotion/restriction, error bounds, cache size and invalidation. Never assume single uniform grid. Parent summaries are not duplicate child owners. For fine terrain, deterministic reconstruction plus edit overlay; for water, conservative partition of finite stores; for entities, retained individual IDs and aggregate event accounting. Camera requests rendering only, simulation can request detail offscreen.
Quantitative pilot
Use DEC-SPATIAL-PILOT to compare shared spatial indexing and separate field authority. Qualification plan defines the discriminating tests. Do not choose a global dense metre/250 m representation just to simplify coupling.
Concrete provisional pilot
Spatial architecture selection: shared metric coordinates, compact 16 km region directory, dense coarse fields, optional domain-specific payloads, persistent geometry features and independent Zylann fine blocks. Region addresses are not solver ownership or simulation cadence. Use stable IDs and revisioned derived data, no universal octree. Record exact partial-cell areas and wrapped seam rules. Coarse geometry/physics continue without voxel viewer admission. Test no fine-world allocation and bounded activity-dependent residency.

contracts/con-nav.title: Navigation truth and abstraction
contracts/con-nav.content:
Navigation truth and abstraction
Regional portals, connectivity and travel costs derived from terrain/material/clearance, access and hazards. Stable spatial IDs and revision dependencies. Long routes are high-level waypoints/segments with bounded refined queries; no dense metre corridor. Distinguish unknown, pending, stale, proven blocked, valid and approximate. On terrain/flood changes invalidate affected routes; broad connectivity changes may propagate. Offscreen travel shares timing/capacity and validates consequential transitions. Exact local motion checks current proof. Measure path error, search/rebuild time, memory and throughput.
Spatial pilot interface
Spatial architecture selection uses common metric region identities, not the render tree. Global and regional passage summaries must not require all descendants’ fine leaves to be resident or generated before planning; mark uncertain paths and refine consequential crossings. Existing exact remote segment proof is a historical implementation rule, not a new target restriction. Preserve edit/flood invalidation, time and capacity. Navigation library selection is separate.

contracts/con-terrain.title: Terrain authority and granularity
contracts/con-terrain.content:
Terrain authority and granularity
Proposed authority: generation produces immutable versioned macro fields and constrained fine recipe; terrain owner resolves current solid geometry/material from that recipe plus committed edits. Zylann provisional owner of current voxel data. A macro field is not a complete fine occupancy truth; a rendered mesh never becomes authority. Coarse summaries derive from actual recipe/edits; dirty bounds/revisions invalidate relevant geometry consumers. Store seed, model version, dimensions, edit overlay; do not allocate dense metre grids. X/Z/Y-up, metre SDF existing convention; exact target lattice open.
Refinement geometry boundary
Spatial architecture selection proposes a single aged baseline with region-crossing constraints, stable channel/bank profiles, terminal basin geometry and deterministic fine evaluation. The MIT donor may help realize geometry but not choose all tributary topology. Current river stage must never recarve the bed by changing the generator input. Current edits override the generated baseline and invalidate dependent summaries; use exact local SDF only where necessary, not as routine coarse hydraulic geometry derivation.
Volumetric geology qualification
Neither formation candidate supplies a complete editable volumetric world. Surface geometry is a heightfield; use the same canonical aged baseline plus sparse deterministic Zylann SDF features and committed edits for caves, overhangs and tunnels. Material identity must be coherent in X/Y/Z (strata, physical properties, finite mineable deposits), not inferred from a rendered biome color. Underground openings, aquifer/cave connectivity and flood barriers require actual shared geometry; ordinary surface queries must not materialize unrelated underground voxels. See Q-VOLUME and formation comparison.
Extensible landforms and downstream geometry
A new landform algorithm must emit deterministic changes/features in physical units against the same baseline/feature recipe, with explicit spatial footprint and material/volume consequences. Formation stages may use long-term climate priors. Freeze or refresh dependent terrain, basin/crest/channel, material, climate boundary and navigation descriptors at the relevant commit boundary; never retain pre-landform drainage as current truth. Once the game starts, actual fluxes drive bounded revisioned terrain/material transactions and downstream repair. Refinement and rendering must not mutate the authoritative terrain simply because a region becomes visible.
Consumers request only the geometry and field granularity they need: stage-volume curves and connectivity/controls for hydraulics; elevation/relief, surface cover, roughness, albedo and thermal/moisture boundary data for atmosphere; underground solid/void geometry and contacts for cave water; support/clearance for navigation. Derived summaries must be consistent with the underlying current geometry and declared precision. Use conservative area/volume mapping between independent field resolutions; avoid dense fine-world expansion. Exceptional landforms (e.g. floating islands, multilevel water passages) may require explicit vertical/volumetric solver support; do not imply a heightfield-only solver covers them. See CON-WATER, CON-ATMOS, Q-VOLUME.
Hydraulic feature-first acceptance interface
For ordinary generation, derive explicit channel centerline/length/bed profile and cross-section, bank crest, floodplain/closed-basin partitions, stage-volume and stage-dependent wet area/conveyance and face/sill curves from the same immutable aged recipe plus revisioned edits. Use analytic feature geometry where demonstrably consistent with generated solids; sample bounded regional terrain where needed. Preserve true meandering length, narrow connections and barriers. Provide deterministic boundary IDs and topology at coarse resolution even where fine SDF is absent. Never scan a world-sized dense metre DEM or materialize rendered chunks to initialize broad hydraulics. Wet edits and erosion alter the authoritative recipe/overrides and repair affected connected geometry; measure the actual footprint and cost, including downstream changes. Gate on known-answer feature geometry, closed basins, generated-solid agreement and solver acceptance; no claim that the current GeoGenesis/PWG implementation already exports this interface. See upstream evidence.
First V1 terrain recipe
The checked recipe is a centered, open rectangle with 1 m, Y-up negative-solid SDF in Zylann. It keeps the original bed, the potential depression-fill surface, and diagnostic routing as distinct fields. Native terrain sampling uses the original bed and returns no sample outside its declared extent. Zylann can change the current voxel without mutating the archived formation input. Current hydraulic geometry, connected coastal inventory, strata and persistent edits remain next integration work. First V1 terrain evidence
The next V1 geometry package derives curving features, junction IDs, carved bed, sampled sections and candidate crests from the same aged recipe. It records a reach contact as unresolved when the solid connection has yet to be established. A basin storage estimate describes capacity at a stage. V1 terrain evidence
A bounded V1 world now uses the existing RegionWorld writer and stream with its own recipe and generator identity. One cold reopen verified current edited SDF and material channels against the independently loaded immutable base recipe. V1 terrain evidence

contracts/con-time.title: Time and interval contracts
contracts/con-time.content:
Time and interval contracts
Every advancing owner states units, integrated amount vs rate, start/end interval, accepted/completed horizon and stable timestep condition. Actual game time cannot be dropped, and old hydraulic timing is not a new obligation. Configurable calendar maps game seconds to seasons; geological age separate. Persist pending transfers and clocks. Measure CPU per completed game second and actual rendered rate.
Pressure-review clock gate
Literal 86400 physical seconds/600 game seconds implies multiplier144. Synthetic 250m/30s storm cost .383678 CPU-ms/physical-s ->55.25 CPU-ms/game-s. Qualify configurable common coupled environment multiplier 1,10,144 and gameplay pacing; 1:1 not accepted final. Calendar/solar and geological years separate. Review.
V1 implementation starting clock
Use a configurable common physical multiplier of 1 physical second per simulated game second for the first connected world. Both sides of water and energy exchange account for the same physical interval. Keep the 600 second day and 60 day year as configurable calendar settings. Geological aging has its own modeled duration. Measure pacing and debt in the connected host before accepting any rate for release. See the V1 technical plan.

contracts/con-water.title: Water inventory and hydraulic scale
contracts/con-water.content:
Water inventory and hydraulic scale
Use physical units: volume m³, stage m, discharge m³/s, velocity m/s, conserved mass/constituent kg or explicit units. Candidate storage relation V(h) monotonic; topology and connection curves revisioned from shared geometry. Finite donors, equal opposite transfers, pending rain/transit, ocean and groundwater inventories. Simultaneous outflows cannot overspend. Coarse/fine promotion partitions water, restriction sums. Local visual queries may approximate depth from connected surface; no independent water plane inventory. Accuracy tests include arrival, level, inundation and conservation, not ledger alone.
Geometry input distinction
Spatial architecture selection proposes deriving most bed, barrier, cross-section and storage descriptors from shared region/feature geometry, rather than repeated SDF scanning. One region may contain multiple disconnected finite stores. Do not use the coarse formation diagnostic lake level, donor’s visual water height or render residency as live volume authority. Topology change can propagate outside a local edited region; keep actual volume and constituent accounting during repair.
Upstream solver integration boundary
Do not assume one numerical solver can handle all scales. Prefer one accepted stock regional surface solver and only necessary local detail, with one active volume owner for each compartment. Boundary exchange is a signed accepted finite debit/credit, including water in transit and pending sources; not duplicated local/parent water, independent open reservoirs or unconstrained corrections. A solver’s positivity clipping, wet/dry correction and external source/sink behavior must be included in the water ledger; no silently added water. Transfer conserved tracer/heat and compatible momentum when replacing local state; enforce geometry revision and advance both regions on common physical intervals. Cave/underground passages are separate connected vertical compartments, not represented by surface depth alone. No candidate has qualified this integration. See upstream evidence.
First V1 geometry inputs
The V1 recipe now supplies reach IDs, linked geometry, true lengths, sampled sections, candidate crests and approximate basin capacity. These values describe the original carved terrain. Water ownership, physically accepted transfers, current-geometry repairs and verified outlet contacts remain pending. V1 terrain evidence
First V1 accepted surface transfers
The finite surface owner holds independent stage-volume curves and accepts simultaneous crest-limited transfers. It moves volume, heat and two passive masses together and refuses a substep outside the ordinary-flow regime. A generated gate exercised seal, opening, reversal and finite withdrawal. This boundary leaves above-bank storage, current terrain repair, coupled persistence and the local rapid solver open. V1 water evidence
A bounded V1 land interval now accounts for the CFE queues, actual ET and pending recharge as finite stocks. The spatial aquifer owns groundwater and exchanges signed parcels with the same surface owner. An internal transfer never enters the combined external ledger twice. V1 water evidence

Documentation precedence
Precedence

Current explicit user instructions and accepted requirements/decisions define desired outcomes.
Proposed contracts and candidate records are hypotheses, not imposed implementation constraints.
Source at a named commit establishes actual implementation; matching executed evidence establishes validation.
Legacy plans, old AGENTS assignments, archived prompts and measurements are historical, not authorization.

New execution requires user-approved scope. No automatic resumption of earlier campaigns. Preserve source and receipts; never reinterpret history. Retain stable IDs and explain supersessions. This refresh changes documentation only.
Scope update, 26 November 2026
The original Brain refresh was documentation-only. The user’s later explicit authorization now permits the Environmental Foundation V1 full replacement in Codex under the current plan and execution protocol. This does not authorize unrelated runtime work, preserve obsolete implementation as a requirement, or imply that any new runtime code is implemented or validated. decisions/dec-env-stack.title: Integrated living-world foundation selection
decisions/dec-env-stack.content:
Integrated living-world foundation selection
Research date: 25 November 2026. This records a design preference and qualification plan, not runtime authorization, implementation status or passed validation. Source review covered the canonical private repository and the generated public Brain mirror. The public mirror is not an authored source. No game code changes or solver benchmarks were performed. The user explicitly soft-locked GeoGenesis plus selected PWG algorithms and retained Zylann; they favor HPA/DHPA and asked to close remaining selections through compatibility research. Other choices below are proposed first candidates, not user approval or production acceptance.
Selected stack and authority









































































































DomainPreferred directionQualification boundaryGeological formation and ageGeoGenesis (MIT), pinned aa898282cbddc71a515deb58a0aa41f649e00147Primary foundation; single aged macro authority; export material, geography, drainage and climate priors, not diagnostic water stocks.Morphology and refinementSelected PWG algorithms (MIT), pinned f7b1daa7a61af3ce9bf7e06fa77dfc4fcf89296cSelected terrace/cliff/channel geometry; no arbitrary small-stream width cap, forced channel joins, or second world generator. Qualify constrained regional drainage with parent outlets and closed basins, stable feature identities and deterministic seams.Solid geometryExisting Zylann pin 75d3c6d996ed2331c80edcd8c3ebc947afc0f041Sparse editable SDF/material blocks; terrain queries independent of rendering, structures and doors compose with solids. Preserve proven narrow edit/deposit operations; do not materialize whole-world fine terrain.Hydraulic routingNative local-inertial face law with finite connected storage; Wflow.jl reference/donor, SFINCS subgrid method referenceStage-volume and face conveyance from physical geometry. Separate disconnected compartments, signed reversible flow, wet/dry, explicit sills/controls, conservative donor-limited exchanges. No equilibrium-only flood routing, no duplicate reach/floodplain storage, no universal fine grid.Exceptional local flowBounded conservative shallow-water solver; Clawpack Riemann kernel candidateOnly when local-inertial approximation cannot represent rapid/strongly supercritical flow. No global SWE or full Clawpack runtime.Soil waterRetain existing NOAA CFE adapter as first candidate (Apache-2.0)Infiltration, actual ET, runoff/recharge; retain necessary queue mass and physical time. Do not duplicate conceptual groundwater and spatial aquifer inventory.Groundwater and cavesExisting native head/conductance and finite exchange kernels; Wflow groundwater referenceDistinct spatial aquifer and connected cave/storage geometry, bounded spring/drain exchanges; cave compartments may be refined where needed, not dense 3D water.AtmosphereReduced hydrostatic layered model; Weather3D coarse primitive-equation core as first source-screened circulation donorQualify native-compatible horizontal winds/pressure, temperature, vertical exchange and moisture/energy transport. Existing conservative face transport as starting point. Do not import full WebGPU CFD or Earth climatology. Benchmark cheap diagnostic wind closure as challenger, retain more robust pressure correction if needed.Condensation and precipitationCliMA CloudMicrophysics 0-moment scalar precipitation scheme and mixed-phase thermodynamics; ERF Kessler warm-rain fallbackPrognostic total water with diagnosed condensed phases or explicitly balanced phase stores. Add finite falling precipitation and evaporation below cloud; no instantaneous ground delivery or negative unaccounted clipping. Use one precipitation scheme, not both. Cold-phase closure and energy transfer need qualification.Surface energyCOARE air-water bulk exchange reference, simplified coefficient kernel; CFE actual ET, land heat capacity, water thermal slabsSame actual liquid debit and vapor credit; account for latent and sensible heat, solar/cloud shading, outgoing radiation, freeze/melt. Calibrate lake/land coefficients; COARE itself is air-sea reference.CurrentsRiver velocity from accepted Q/A; coarse wind-driven surface layer for lakes/oceanFinite coast/edge transport and optional Coriolis, drag/depth; only refine where consequential. Waves are primarily derived rendering.Runtime erosionExisting narrow incision law and GeoGenesis-derived erosion/material algorithmsActual discharge and accumulated shear/runoff; slow bounded terrain transactions; retain sediment mass/deposition. DAG method only where drainage topology fits. Qualify reversal, changed outlets and slope/bank erosion.Second liquidProposed lava, sparse family-specific mobility and cooling; MrLavaLoba2 footprint referenceFinite mass/thermal state, viscous flow law and solidification into editable material; explicit water contact reactions if modeled. No default multiphase CFD or family state in dry regions.ContaminationConserved mass per wet compartment; donor mass transport with accepted water fluxConcentration, dilution and persistent dry deposition where applicable.CloudsOffline baked volumetric shape assets, instancing and feathered geometry/sprite clusters near, view-dependent impostors fartherArt target: discrete sculpted stylized-realistic puffy clouds, soft internal illumination, vertical forms, open sky between formations when physical coverage permits. No default full-screen volume raymarch, global fixed 50% coverage, arbitrary precipitation or clouds owning water. Compare near mesh/sprites and soft/translucent impostors from above, below and through; fallback bounded low-resolution volumetric pass only if measured necessary.Water appearanceExisting renderer where viable; Waterways Godot 4.5 branch and LesusX Water-Shader as MIT donorsClip meshes to actual stage/geometry, use flow and depth-derived foam/normal maps, Gerstner waves; no editor-authored alternative water authority or global FFT requirement.NavigationHPA-style sparse region portal hierarchy; selective DHPA caches for hot routes; Recast/Detour first local candidateRead-only queries and local scratch; multi-level terrain/caves/bridges, explicit door/permission edges, separate hazard costs from topology; shared routes/flow fields where reused. Compare existing native local/hierarchical code, choose one local engine; RVO2/DetourCrowd only for active local crowds. Offscreen travel must respect cost, capacity and changing obstacles without generating every fine voxel along a route.ECS and executionFlecs first candidate, EnTT challenger; enkiTS/Tracy or current proven scheduling/profilingMixed 1k/10k/100k workloads; persistent identities independent of Godot Nodes, batched data, spatial cohorts and explicit structural changes, one scheduling policy with resource budgets and no competing unbounded pools.EcologyCoarse persistent biomass/cohorts plus deterministic individual identities and harvest/regrowth eventsRead actual soil water, temperature, light, contamination and nutrient/material fields; send actual cover/roughness, uptake and ET feedback. Not yet a qualified plant/fauna gameplay model.
Source-screen findings (not benchmarks)

Wflow.jl, MIT, pin c617a12e413e5eaf20b1818a4091f552001910c7: staggered surface routing, floodplain storage, reservoir and groundwater implementations. Wflow FAQ documents instantaneous exchange and potential excessive inundation. Its negative-storage corrections must not become unaccounted mass losses. Use as narrow donor/reference, not whole Julia runtime. SFINCS (GPL-3.0) is mathematical subgrid reference, not a code-embedding choice; Clawpack Riemann (BSD-3-Clause), pin 008d4921ea46878a97a96c8b8daa399a2e7b9078, is exceptional-flow candidate only. Landlab remains independent reference, not a default solver with unaccounted thin film.
Canonical source snapshot c7b4ede9af45a67a6ddd3d65cd5685d3af79c320 includes native hydraulic flux and finite exchange, groundwater head/conductance, conservative face vapor transport, incision and geology deposit operations. This is evidence of available calculations, not validated integrated performance. Reuse isolated operations and known-answer tests, not the rejected legacy graph/preparation architecture. CFE source pin f9182dfb3d81c407c66c5b782114173893c30cf2; requalify adapter/cadence/conservation.
Weather3D MIT, pin ce66920fd9515e3842110b9c2c7340658e289bef: pe.wgsl coarse hydrostatic anelastic C-grid circulation, vertical mass continuity, pressure projection and column physics. Earth-specific channel/boundary assumptions, advection and GPU dependencies require redesign/qualification; no claim of conservative transport or validated performance for Breachborn. Author describes early AI-assisted project; audit source provenance and third-party notices. Full sim.wgsl is not selected. WeatherBox MIT pin 7d6b2d1e5fcde3ea7a365e398664827563a939ce is a 2D thermodynamic/dynamics test reference, not conservative full-world transport. SpeedyWeather EUPL-1.2, VolcanicSkies GPL-2 and scientific models are reference-only under present licensing/runtime preferences.
CliMA CloudMicrophysics 0M, Apache-2.0; inspected blob 3db0f62dbbb8c79a4b5ce519a7bddecf8facfe6f. Threshold/relaxation precipitation removal; instantaneous sedimentation assumption is unsuitable for our travel-time requirement unless adapted. Evaporation tendency explicitly requires timestep limits. Bulk microphysics API documents one-moment rain/snow/melting/sublimation alternatives. ERF pin e215059ffd648ea097f823cfac1869c16e725669, BSD-style license, Kessler scalar warm-rain routines, AMReX wrappers not selected. Audit any transitive source before reuse.
NOAA COARE, MIT pin bd1cac80d2dae454e699f9ef46204dfd88086a71: Fortran COARE3.6 module has wind stress/sensible/latent flux outputs. Reference for bulk approximation; do not assume full iterative calculation is cheap enough everywhere.
Harris and Lastra, Real-Time Cloud Rendering: precomputed light and impostor approach. Godot MultiMesh/instancing and Godot octahedral impostor plugin candidate (MIT, 6e3bb2c6f8ff67c91ae68d56da30334bd48be7e4); geometry-oriented impostors do not establish translucent volume quality. Waterways Godot 4.5.1 branch, MIT, project.godot inspected blob 50699209604ebb79e82b64f1cd15022177cdfd86 confirms 4.5; LesusX MIT shader donor. Validate both against actual Godot version and target visuals.
MOLASSES GPL-3.0 reference only, does not model actual rate/dynamics; MrLavaLoba2 Apache-2.0 inspected license, stochastic elliptical lobe footprint, not a time-dependent lava solver. First lava law remains an independently qualified small kernel.
Recast/Detour, zlib, pin 9f4ce64458dfae86e1239c525ddc219c4e9e06f1. Local tiled navigation and links, not a continent-scale hierarchy. Flecs external tasks and enkiTS support scheduler integration; measure rather than adopt a second pool automatically. Pin all new dependencies and their notices before code adoption.

Compatibility and qualification
Use one spatial addressing/feature identity convention, not a common resolution. Illustrative 4,000 km world: 4 km macro geography; 16 km page directory; 1 km/250 m conditional geographic refinement; 16–32 km atmosphere horizontally, 6–12 vertical layers, 4–8 km regional weather trial. Exact scales are candidates. At eight layers a 32 km square-grid atmosphere contains 125,000 cells, about 3.81 MiB at hypothetical 32 B/cell; 16 km gives 500,000 cells / 15.26 MiB; 8 km gives 2 million / 61.04 MiB. Excludes faces, snapshots, solvers, geometry, scratch and all other systems. Nested regions must replace or partition parent mass, not duplicate it.
Shared geometry describes material, occupancy, bed/crest, stage-volume, connectivity, exposure, passability and feature revisions. Hydraulic graph, atmospheric cells, navigation graph and voxel pages use their own resolution and ownership. Each physical inventory has exactly one owner. Finite rain/ET/recharge transfers commit once; accumulate physical elapsed time across differing update intervals. Use conservative surface overlap mapping, explicit incoming/outgoing amounts and energy balances. Neither rendering nor paging owns physical state.
Proposed qualification order:

Narrow independent known-answer tests for formation/refinement, hydraulic and atmospheric laws; freeze tolerances and realistic workloads first. Compare source references and cheap alternatives. No unbounded rewrite.
A connected small world fixture with hill/rain shadow, small creeks, lake/outlet, protective wall/dam, underground compartment, doors/bridge, soil/aquifer, actual water/vapor and heat cycle, plus save/reload and out-of-view edits. Verify conservation, meaningful travel/arrival times, topology, erosion and visuals. Cloud silhouette and presentation tests with actual weather.
Scale the macro addressing and generation, sparse residency, large storm and navigational long route before production integration. Include 100 x 100 km severe storm; 256 km generation baseline and 4,000 km macro; 800 km route and realistic mixed 1k/10k/100k population workloads. Monitor CPU/game-second, GPU/frame, RAM/VRAM, main-thread handoff, latency, debt, saves and work budgets. Preserve prior targets as evaluation guidance rather than assert passed: reference Ryzen 7 3700X, RTX 2070 SUPER, 32 GB; 25 CPU-ms/game-second historical environment target, 8x rendered goal and 32–64x longer-term aspiration. Explicit 600 s/day, 60 days/year calendar and physical-domain rates; no hidden accelerated-time conversion.
Only after passing the bounded, connected fixture and scale gates, expand environmental integration and colony/ecology. Profile inclusive cost, not isolated empty-kernel benchmarks.

Open risks: regional hydrological topology and geometry construction; conservative reduced atmosphere and wind closure; coupled hydraulic stability and editable barriers; cave volumes; cold precipitation/heat closure; cloud rendering softness/performance; actual large-population throughput. Retain open question records until reproducible evidence. The selections are compatible by design contract, not yet validated together. No runtime work authorized by this documentation change.
Review correction: 25 November 2026
The user explicitly rejected treating this preliminary review as a satisfactory technology lock. Existing native environment calculations have not earned a reuse preference. The previously recorded terrain soft lock stands as a user preference, not validation. Reopen water, atmosphere and cloud implementation selections. Do not treat the table above as an authorized implementation plan. User explicitly requires true volumetric, attractive clouds with distinct realistic-stylized shapes; cheap raymarching is acceptable. Geometry and sprite-only clouds are not the primary target. See independent numerical probes and revised shortlist.
The revised hypothesis is a single conservative water inventory with cheap reach routing in proven ordinary downstream segments, connected subgrid hydraulics for low-Froude backwater/floodplain flow, and full shallow-water momentum transport where the simplified law fails. FluxCell is the leading detailed-flow evaluation candidate, not a selected port. For atmospheric transport, independently tested MC-limited conservative advection outperformed basic upwind in shape retention, but narrow storms still require finer/subgrid treatment. Pressure/wind dynamics, vertical transport, surface heat and phase changes are unqualified. Prototype a reduced CPU circulation and compare against a more complete reference before choosing it. True low-resolution, depth-aware volumetric clouds using reusable bounded density shapes, empty-space skipping and temporal reconstruction are preferred for visual testing. SunshineClouds2 and Godot-Cloud-Worlds are source-screened donors, not performance-accepted.
Complementary pressure review
Integrated pressure review reconciles the latest user correction, sibling dam-break/cloud evidence and complementary cost/clock, topology and transport tests. Adds PyFlwDir geometry, mizuRoute IRF, Wflow subgrid/snow, CliMT/0M/COARE and Clawpack/JCM leads. No preference for existing native mechanisms, no full-stack validation, no new technology lock. Require true volumetric cloud render gate. The initial 144x physical calendar multiplier can exceed budget even on a synthetic 250m storm; qualify clock and accuracy together. Use the research report for next bounded implementation qualification, not authorization.
Independent pressure-test update (25 November 2026)
See executed architecture pressure tests. The architecture is not qualified for production. The tests strengthen shared finite ownership, feature-aware hydraulic geometry, HPA-style multi-layer portals and bounded true volumetric raymarching as directions, but falsify several shortcuts: average elevations, single-reservoir/pure-delay river routing, naive subgrid stability timestep, blanket fine flooding and global 8km atmospheric grid at historical alpha144, fixed cloud lighting. A synthetic 500-step hydraulic comparison diverged by up to 2.10m at the original timestep despite conserved mass; half timestep agreement is not physical acceptance. The actual environmental clock and stability policy are first-order architecture decisions. Retain terrain soft lock only as user-stated preference; no upstream formation/solver, target GPU, integrated simulation or population scale test was executed. Do not promote earlier preferred numerical implementation entries to accepted status. Use the bounded qualification sequence in the evidence record, with actual pinned solver and Godot tests.
Replacement clarification (26 November 2026)
The user explicitly challenged revising the failed water system instead of replacing it with known-good technology. For new worlds, replacement is the objective, consistent with DEC-REUSE. Do not retain the old hydraulic architecture, river preparation, or numerical kernels by default. Standalone experimental kernels in the pressure probes are falsification/reference fixtures, not a proposed new bespoke water implementation. First evaluate actual unmodified upstream numerical implementations and their published validation, then minimally adapt only the selected candidate’s data/geometry/coupling boundaries. Wflow is the first permissive regional river/flood/land-water candidate to execute; SFINCS is a mature independent subgrid reference, not approved for embedding under GPL-3.0; FluxCell is the first detailed shallow-water candidate to execute, not a proven global system. mizuRoute ordinary reach routing is conditional only if the regional engine demonstrably needs cheaper upstream routing. Avoid selecting three simultaneous runtime solvers before evidence establishes the need. Wflow’s instantaneous same-stage river/floodplain exchange and FluxCell’s fixed solid mask are significant integration risks. No external solver is yet validated against the complete mutable 4,000 km game or target hardware. Retain only useful engine integration, geometry/edit interfaces and test evidence, without requiring legacy compatibility. No runtime authorization or final numerical selection follows from this clarification.
26 November: water-first evidence update
See upstream water evidence and Q-FLOOD. User requests continued research until terrain compatibility, scale and gameplay are confirmed. No production lock. FluxCell earns provisional priority for detailed surface qualification only. ADCIRC v56.2.1 enters regional qualification alongside independent SFINCS reference; Wflow remains a land-water candidate but its stock floodplain storage and clipping are blockers for universal use. Establish feature-first hydraulic geometry export before finalizing formation/refinement. Keep existing user-stated GeoGenesis/PWG/Zylann soft lock conditional, not accepted as integrated. No new code, numerical port or license commitment authorized.
Stylized water clarification (26 November 2026)
User prefers fewer meaningful side-streams, curving beautiful realistic-stylized rivers and flow/rainfall-responsive evolution over scientific precision. Re-rank water candidates on cost, physical consistency and gameplay rather than forecast-grade detail; favor testing existing inexpensive 1D reach and connected subgrid storage methods first, with detailed FluxCell only where needed. Keep ADCIRC and SFINCS as regional challengers/references; no new solver lock, Wflow’s shared-stage and negative-clipping issues remain. Generate a sparse physical network from aged geography, aggregate omitted minor runoff conservatively and expose configurable density/shape. Maintain independent geometry/solver sampling, real cross-sections and lengths. For slow morphology investigate MeanderPy with actual accumulated hydraulic forcing; not random visual animation or another whole-world erosion engine. Retain finite mass, connectivity/barriers, meaningful arrival/flooding, persistent edits, atmospheric exchanges and appropriate accuracy. Suggested old precision gates are not user-approved production thresholds; choose gameplay-scaled tolerances before tests, never relax after failures. No target hardware or full integration validation.
Concrete water-first qualification package (26 November 2026)
Water-first integrated qualification plan consolidates the ordered terrain, upstream regional/local hydraulic, atmosphere and real coupled-world gates after the stylized river clarification. Architecture direction and sequence are concrete; regional numerical backend and atmospheric circulation remain unselected. No production lock, new code authorization or benchmark claim.
Implementation-first selection proposal (26 November 2026)
User rejects another prolonged separate experimental campaign and requests evidence-backed open-source technology selection using existing research and calculations. Recommend a single provisional implementation baseline, with ordinary verification and profiling inside bounded implementation rather than broad competing solver projects. This is a recommendation for user approval, not authorization or proof of feasibility.
Retain GeoGenesis/PWG/Zylann soft lock. Prefer Wflow MIT signed local-inertial river numerical kernel for ordinary channels and low-Froude regional connected storage; do not adopt stock shared-stage floodplain model or its negative-volume clipping. SFINCS-style geometry is an algorithm reference; independent disconnected storage, stage-volume and conveyance curves, conservative simultaneous flux allocation and mutable graph repair are required adaptation, not demonstrated features of stock Wflow. If this requires a substantially new hydraulic engine, stop and reconsider the selection rather than conceal the work as glue. CFE Apache-2.0 for soil and runoff; Wflow spatial groundwater candidate must not duplicate CFE conceptual groundwater. FluxCell MIT local detailed solver only on genuinely consequential patches, with actual withdrawal/geometry/parent exchanges; no globally fine grid, no per-view authoritative change. MeanderPy Apache-2.0 slow centerline migration with hydraulic forcing/material constraints. ADCIRC/SFINCS/mizuRoute remain reference/fallback research, not parallel implementation scope. Retain finite ocean, caves, liquid-family support and mass/heat conservation requirements; no stock solution for all these behaviours confirmed.
Atmosphere: Weather3D MIT reduced dynamics donor, NOT wholesale browser/GPU app or accepted runtime; conservative MC/TVD transport, CliMA bulk microphysics candidate, COARE bulk air-water exchange, SunshineClouds2 true volumetric rendering candidate. The circulation donor includes pressure projections and nonconservative/duplicate moisture/land mechanisms; replacing those is substantial unresolved work. Keep independent solver grids, no duplicate physical inventory, realistic-stylized cloud/rain footprints, and explicit boundary/clock policy. No known turnkey complete atmosphere has passed fit.
Arithmetic feasibility scenario only: 4000km square, assumed 50% land, selected channel density 0.1km/km2 of land, mean hydraulic reach length 2km implies 400k reaches, 24.4MiB at hypothetical64B/reach excluding curves/links/scratch. At prior synthetic hydraulic throughput ~29.8ns/cell-step, 400k updates ~11.9ms; normalized at alpha144 and 300 physical s cadence ~5.73 CPU-ms/game-s, at60s ~28.6, before actual routing, transfers, flood, geometry, saves. 300s is not a proven stable/accurate interval. At same assumed counts 1km reach length doubles cost; linear extrapolation from synthetic EPYC probe may fail due to cache and integration. Prior full active 100x100km storm costs ~.76/45.92 CPU-ms/game-s at 1km/250m (synthetic reduced dt) and 32/16km atmosphere transport+column physics .77/4.95 (not dynamic circulation). No additive production budget claim. Need coarse regional computation and detailed physical features; if geometry stability or response time forces denser frequent stepping, baseline may fail. Physical clock unresolved; no silent acceleration change. Historical 25 CPU-ms/game-s whole environment comparator, target 8x/60FPS reference hardware. See SRC-ENV-PRESSURE and SRC-WATER-UPSTREAM for actual scope.
Implementation approach: choose one primary donor per task, pin sources/license, integrate geometry/finite transfers first and measure as ordinary development. Do not build competing complete engines or reproduce every upstream scientific validation. Keep critical barrier, finite-water, real rainfall, erosion/edit, offscreen, combined cost and target GPU checks as implementation acceptance criteria. If a candidate fails a hard requirement, diagnose and change only that dependency. Current docs-only assignment remains unchanged pending explicit implementation authorization. No new test execution, production lock or solver integration in this turn.
Agreed implementation-first direction and continuation plan (26 November 2026)
User agreed to the proposed implementation-first baseline and requested a concrete plan. Environmental Foundation V1 is the operative provisional technical selection and proposed implementation assignment. It consolidates exact donor pins, source reuse boundaries, clock and scale assumptions, six delivery milestones, scope/stop conditions and acceptance. Supersedes separate broad comparative campaign sequencing, not the finite-water, compatibility, licensing or performance requirements. Wflow scalar/storage/groundwater functions and Weather3D reduced circulation inspected further; no target solver integration or full validation. Initial alpha1 physical clock, 32km/eight layers and sparse density/length preset are proposed defaults, not accepted immutable requirements. No runtime authorization from documentation alone; actual Codex task explicitly activates implementation.
User authorization: full replacement, 26 November 2026
The user approves Environmental Foundation V1 as the selected provisional implementation baseline, authorizes Codex to complete M0 and M1–M5 as a continuous full replacement campaign, and prefers minimal targeted testing with maximum implementation. The new environmental architecture must become the normal fresh-world standard; no legacy environmental compatibility requirement or parallel production backend. Ordinary decisions and bounded implementation issues are delegated; escalate only genuine blockers, significant architecture/requirement changes or research needs. Execution protocol defines orchestrator/worker roles, reporting and publication. This supersedes the previous docs-only task restriction for the scoped implementation; see the active assignment. No claim of integrated solver validation, code completion or new hardware performance. Previously proposed clock and resolution defaults remain configurable starting choices, not newly accepted fixed requirements.

decisions/dec-formation.title: Formation and runtime separation
decisions/dec-formation.content:
Formation and runtime separation
GeoGenesis’s single-shot connected world can age; its tiled fast initial-relief path is not an aged-world refinement algorithm. Use coarse formation first; investigate hydrologically constrained refinement. Runtime land/water/atmosphere supply actual fluxes to periodic erosion. Import original final geography and freshly computed drainage, not diagnostic discharge as finite inventory. Exact grid and algorithms remain unresolved.
Formation comparison reopened
Source review shows Procedural World Generation is a genuine alternative for full staged surface formation, not merely a visual detail donor. Recommend testing it first for landform variety, linked drainage and refinement, with GeoGenesis as the existing provisional choice and stronger geological-age/material contender. Neither is a complete volumetric world or live environmental solver. Select exactly one baseline authority after the comparative gate in formation comparison. Borrow independently useful kernels/data adapters from the other only when justified; do not run two complete formation pipelines over the same world. No final change of accepted technology or implementation status.
Extensible landforms and coupled compatibility gate
User asks whether additional landforms can be added and whether the proposed terrain stack is confirmed compatible with the full water, weather and atmosphere. Native GeoGenesis process extensions are source-confirmed; PWG morphology and other reusable landform algorithms may be integrated as bounded deterministic formation stages/processes. No fixed catalog is a target limit. Existing provisional geometry/age choices remain subject to qualification. Use a single final solid/material authority with stable feature geometry and refreshed drainage, basin/crest/storage and climate boundary descriptors. Runtime geological changes use the current terrain/material transaction boundary, not rerunning an independent formation engine over inhabited terrain. Ordinary new terrain shapes must not require replacement of the hydraulic or atmospheric model; exceptional new physics requires an explicit capability review.
Compatibility is designed, not validated. Do not accept final formation/refinement integration solely on surface appearance or export success. Before fixing production terrain interfaces, screen the shortlisted water, groundwater and atmospheric solvers against the actual terrain inputs, scale/residency and edit requirements, then qualify the smallest connected representative case. Subsequent whole-island storms and large-world cost gates remain mandatory. See coupled compatibility gate and spatial qualification. No claim that all runtime numerical kernels are selected or that full coupling has passed.
User-stated soft lock, 25 November 2026
The user selected GeoGenesis as the primary formation foundation, selected PWG algorithms as bounded landform/refinement donors, and retention of existing Zylann terrain infrastructure. This supersedes the earlier preference to evaluate PWG first as the complete formation authority. Comparative evidence remains useful, but do not launch two competing formation pipelines. The selection is provisional pending the coupled qualification gates, not a claim of implementation or performance validation. See integrated foundation selection.
Water and geological aging clarification (26 November 2026)
Keep two timescales with one geological/material authority: initial accelerated formation uses GeoGenesis’s established implicit geological processes and long-term climate-derived runoff/discharge, not a live gameplay hydraulic solve per storm. The selected external water/atmosphere models, once qualified, may calibrate representative climate/runoff distributions at selected formation epochs; they need not run every physical interval in geological history. The current pinned GeoGenesis main incision and depositional laws use drainage area rather than discharge directly; bank erosion uses annual discharge. Compare a minimal calibrated discharge-aware extension against stock GeoGenesis and independent established erosion references (see OPT-GEOGENESIS), including nonlinear high-flow/threshold effects. No final numerical choice.
Run selected PWG morphology/refinement stages coherently before or within geological aging where appropriate, not as a second full erosion simulation; refresh affected drainage and basin/bed/sill geometry after terrain changes. Export final current solids/material, outlet/closed-basin constraints, climate/runoff statistics and storage descriptors. Diagnostic depression-filled lake levels are potential geometry, not actual finite lake volume: initialize the selected runtime water owner from a declared finite inventory and plausible water balance/spin-up. During gameplay, actual accepted hydraulic flux, sediment, rain, wind and other forcing drive localized periodic terrain/material transactions; never re-age the inhabited world using unrelated climate averages. Handle altered dam/cave/river geometry with finite water transfer and navigation invalidation. This is clarification of existing design requirements and proposed qualification, not new implementation authorization or confirmed compatibility.
First V1 implementation boundary
Formation now calls the pinned GeoGenesis core and records a distinct original bed, potential depression surface, geological fields and drainage priors. Selected PWG methods derive shared geometry for Zylann and the next hydraulic owner. The terrain session verifies independent cold continuation on current voxels. Integrated water inventories and runtime geology remain later delivery work. V1 terrain evidence

decisions/dec-spatial-pilot.title: Spatial hierarchy qualification direction
decisions/dec-spatial-pilot.content:
Spatial hierarchy qualification direction
Hypothesis, not final selection
Use one coordinate and spatial identity convention, not a universal physical grid. Test a global coarse macro image and spatial index, sparse or compact regional features/pages, deterministic fine terrain, and domain-specific solvers. Start with 4 km macro candidates for the 4,000 km world and compare 1 km and 250 m land/refinement levels. At 256 km, compare the same physical scales and a denser macro source where worthwhile. Do not prescribe all-domain level sizes until actual kernel qualification.
Memory sizing
Illustrative 64 bytes per horizontal cell across a candidate packed field set. This is not measured implementation memory or a claim every field fits. Counts use ceiling division for complete square coverage. Excludes vertical layers, graph links, caches, edits, topology, scratch, snapshots and saves.




































































Spacing (m)256 km cell count64 B/cell4,000 km cell count64 B/cell40004,096256.00 KiB1,000,00061.04 MiB200016,3841.00 MiB4,000,000244.14 MiB100065,5364.00 MiB16,000,000976.56 MiB500262,14416.00 MiB64,000,0003.81 GiB2501,048,57664.00 MiB256,000,00015.26 GiB1006,553,600400.00 MiB1,600,000,00095.37 GiB10655,360,00039.06 GiB160,000,000,0009.31 TiB165,536,000,0003.81 TiB16,000,000,000,000931.32 TiB
A dense 250 m field set across 4,000 km would exceed 15 GiB before any other systems. Dense 1 km costs about 977 MiB even at only 64 B/cell. A 4 km global field is about 61 MiB. This is the reason to avoid hard-coding one resolution for every process. It does not forbid compact, compressed or sparse finer fields with proven budgets.
A 16 km regional page at 250 m contains 4096 cells, costing 256 KiB at 64 B/cell. 1024 such pages cost 256 MiB for that field set, covering 262,144 km², not the whole 4,000 km world. Pages with permanent edits or active storage must remain durably represented even when not resident. Use these values as workload probes, not fixed allocation targets.
Ownership by domain























































DataCandidate authoritative representationDerived consumersGeological baselineVersioned aged macro fields and deterministic regional recipeTerrain, materials, land hydrology, climate priorsSolid geometryFine procedural recipe constrained by durable features, plus committed edits, including cave and structure topologyMesh/collision, storage/face curves, navigation portalsClimate and weatherCoarse horizontal cells and optional vertical state, with conservative exchangesClouds, runoff, radiation, vegetation, wind effectsSoil/landPacked active land/catchment units; optional subgrid cover/soil partitionsRunoff, recharge, evapotranspiration, agricultureRivers/lakes/floodsConnected finite volume stores and geometry-dependent stage/flux relationships; distinct subgrid channels/basinsLocal level/depth/current, navigation hazards, erosionErosionMaterial and sediment budgets plus accepted terrain transactions; aggregate time-integrated forcingsUpdated geography and derived topologyVegetationPersistent cohorts/coverage and durable individual deltas when relevantHarvest, root effects, ET, habitatNavigationVersioned coarse region/portal connectivity and local refined evidenceRoutes, travel times and crowd motionPeople/itemsECS individual identities, finite item/needs state; shared batched activitiesLocal actors and offscreen outcomes
Coarse geometry is not exact fine solid truth; refinement must agree with explicit drainage and passage constraints. A coarse water store can represent many fine locations, but distinct sealed basins cannot share one undifferentiated water level. Use partitions or connectivity-aware features. An aggregate is not a second owner: promote by partitioning amounts and restrict by summing, with appropriate clocks and deterministic/validated reconstruction.
Clock and work scaling
A full linear pass over 16 million 1 km cells every simulated second costs 0.4 CPU seconds/game-second even at an optimistic 25 ns/cell, already 16x the historical 25 ms environment target. For one million 4 km cells the same hypothetical pass costs 25 ms. These are arithmetic examples, not measured performance. Use process-specific intervals, event/due work, compact field layouts and a complete inclusive budget. A severe island-wide storm must not force a fine-cell update everywhere.
First experiment
Use the qualification plan. Compare candidate costs at both world sizes and demonstrate preserved narrow channels and causal offscreen flooding. Final selection requires a measured connected implementation; no runtime launch is authorized by this document.
Source-screened selection update (25 November 2026)
Spatial architecture selection selects a simple global macro field + 16 km regional directory + sparse feature geometry + existing Zylann fine voxel residency for the pilot. The 1 km (256 km world) and approximately 4 km (4,000 km world) macro levels and 250 m regional resolution are comparison settings, not globally imposed. Prioritize the MIT Procedural World Generation donor for CPU channel/valley realization. Regional tributary topology and closed-basin reconciliation are still unresolved. Do not install a second voxel tree or generic AMR runtime. This is a provisional engineering selection; source inspected, not executed or accepted.
Formation review supplement
The same spatial hierarchy can consume either candidate’s exported geography. Formation comparison reopens the macro generator selection and identifies existing deterministic creek growth in Procedural World Generation. No universal grid or second terrain authority is introduced.

environment-stack-pressure-review.title: Integrated environmental foundation pressure review
environment-stack-pressure-review.content:
Integrated environmental foundation pressure review
25 November 2026. Reconciles formation soft lock, integrated decision, sibling review and negative evidence and complementary independent probes. The current user correction supersedes prior native-reuse preference and mesh/sprite-only cloud assumptions. Provisional selection for qualification; no production compatibility, runtime implementation, source build or target benchmark claimed.
Primary and contingency stack


























































































AreaFirst qualificationContingency / residual riskBirth and ageGeoGenesis MIT core, age and geologyPWG whole generator only if soft lock fails and user revisits. No two full formation worlds.MorphologySelected PWG MIT terracing/cliff/mesa/river profile stages; GeoGenesis ProcessPluginExisting deterministic stamp/noise/SDF, same final geometry. No forced 8m cap or decorative creek joins.Regional drainageExtend GeoGenesis seeded priority flood; compare PyFlwDir explicit outlet/length/subgrid kernelsPreserve closed basins and parent spill levels; unresolved fine topology, not inverse IHU.Volume/materialZylann sparse editable SDF, existing noise and persistence; rock properties/prospectivity from GeoGenesisDeterministic cave/ore realization and finite depletion separate gates.LandExisting NOAA CFE candidate, qualify actual native wrapper and clocksWflow SBM or calibrated cheaper reservoir challenger; no duplicate GW.Ordinary downstream flowmizuRoute Apache IRF narrow donor, bounded delay/response storeCompare analytic reservoir and Lagrangian wave; no backwater or false instantaneous arrival.Low-Froude floodWflow MIT local inertia/subgrid donor, SFINCS scientific reference, PyFlwDir geometrySigned diffusive law compare; separate compartments and explicit actual length/sills. Existing native arithmetic comparator only.Steep/rapid hydraulicFluxCell MIT MUSCL-Hancock/HLLC CPU reference then bounded GPU/CPU adaptationClawpack BSD augmented SWE reference; no global fine-grid requirement.
