If broad fast flows require SWE, qualify coarse shock-capable mode, not suppress them.Aquifers and cave waterSparse finite head/storage, Darcy conductance; Wflow reference and existing native head helpers as comparatorNo CFE conceptual GW double count; bounded sparse implicit solve if stiffness requires. Open caves use connected hydraulic compartments.Atmospheric wind/pressureReduced CPU prognostic hydrostatic/anelastic circulation, Weather3D parent as source leadCompare cheaper diagnostic wind with thermal/pressure forcing (limited fixture) and JCM/SPEEDY reference. No selected validated dynamics; no full browser/GCM runtime.Moisture/cloud/precipMC/TVD conservative transport, CliMA 0M adapted finite cloud and falling phase; CliMT saturation/heatERF Kessler warm rain challenger, not second owner. Snow/ice Wflow HBV solid/liquid stores.Heat/currentsCOARE-informed bulk exchange, cheap slab heat/radiation, wind stress and damped surface velocityRiver Q/A, coastal head partitions if needed; waves visual, no whole ocean CFD.ErosionGeoGenesis implicit stream power, transport-limited/SPACE, hillslope, aeolian donorsActual water/heat/wind/material forcing integrated, bounded edit transactions; no repeated whole age.LiquidsSparse water and second family (lava candidate), distinct mobility/cooling/solidification, basic contaminantViscous shallow flow/reference, not water roughness blind reuse; no full multiphase CFD.Clouds/visualsTrue bounded volumetric raymarch, SunshineClouds2 and Godot-Cloud-Worlds source leadsQuarter-linear resolution, temporal depth-aware reconstruction, shaped density volumes, SDF skip, distant representation only. No stock addon performance claim.Future lifeCohorts/biomass + individual identities; qualify Flecs/EnTT, HPA regional and Recast local, selective DHPA cachesEnvironmental batch queries and hazards; no all-route fine residency or per-tree global simulation.
Formation extensions and current source
GeoGenesis ProcessPlugin receives mutable World, read-only Hydro/Climate/Geology, dt years, returns MassBalance; built-in meteor impact example demonstrates actual extension point. New landforms can be bounded deterministic stages or plugins. Plugins run after built-in chain, so refresh affected hydrology and climate/material descriptors after geometry changes; if intended to age naturally insert initial stage before age. Surface elevation includes sediment (World); do not add loose sediment twice. Fluvial has implicit detachment-limited, transport-limited and SPACE laws; hillslope conservative edge diffusion; aeolian uses simplified prevailing wind. Formation-time drainage estimates not finite runtime flows. At runtime accumulate nonlinear erosion forcing (shear/threshold exposure, not simply mean Q), actual sediment/dust and material removal, commit terrain edits and dirty topology. New caves, overhangs and finite ore require 3D recipe + edited solid state, not surface-height perturbation alone.
GeoGenesis priority flood has seeded/rank-queue and D8/MFD. PyFlwDir provides actual supplied-outlet and unit-catchment routines. Neither magically solves inverse regional refinement. Store parent crossings, outlet and spill elevation, terminal basin identities, feature profiles; resolve cross-window dependencies before claiming exact. Cropping before a remote saddle in independent probe gives false 1m instead of true 5m. Use sparse regional pages/latent constrained features; no all-creek precomputation. 50% land in 4000km square, illustrative drainage density 1km/km² and 100m segments imply 80M segments, 4.77GiB at 64B before links. Aggregate minor headwater response and persist consequential individual feature changes; do not promise exact unseen local state if only aggregate known.
Published implementation c7b4ede9af45a67a6ddd3d65cd5685d3af79c320: native flux already contains local inertia and conservative exchanges; groundwater head/conductance/SPD; air face transport, morphology, soil exchange useful existing evidence but no reuse preference. Historical Flood078 1124 CPU-ms/game-s vs 25 target; earlier SWMM/CaMa failures; no revival of old LandscapeChannels/preparation, no broad legacy API/save compatibility. Compare narrow primitives only under same acceptance gates. Local unpublished code not inspected. Aokana paper’s explicit lack of runtime voxel edits prevents replacement of Zylann based solely on rendering benchmark.
Shared authority and coupling


















































OwnerDurable quantity / geometryInputs and outputsTerrainversioned aged baseline, deterministic recipe, committed solid/material editsbed/crest/profile, slope, roughness, cave void and portal revisions; accepts erosion/structuresSurfaceone water stock per connected partition/reach, constituent, momentum or delayed release representationstage-volume inversion, Q/A and flood duration, actual ET/recharge/withdrawal, sedimentsSoilCFE root-zone, queues/interception, snow and recharge pendingexact areal precipitation, actual ET and runoff/recharge; remove conceptual GW if spatial owner receives rechargeGWfinite aquifer/cave stock, headDarcy exchange, seepage, springs/extraction, geometry revisionsAtmospheredry/moist air mass convention, energy/temp, pressure/wind, vapor/cloud/falling liquid/iceactual vapor/heat and rain transfer, cloud state, solar/season/wind fieldsSediment/materialloose/mobile/deposited solid and dust/sinksactual integrated forcing, bounded solid edits; retain finite material accountEcologyregional biomass/cohort, durable individual deltassoil/radiation/thermal/wetness/hazards; roots/roughness/infiltration/actual ET feedbackECS/nav/renderentity identity/state; derived portals and render buffersbatched field queries and invalidation; never second physical owner
16km page directory, common checked metric coordinates, independent solver lattices. 256km macro 1km; 4000km macro 4km; 250m regional only conditional on actual geometry/accuracy. Use compact SoA, direct page directory, stable IDs, sparse graph; keep no dense 1m world. Overlap area/contacts precomputed once per geometry revision; transfer amounts by actual integrated interval. CFE m per step and timestep_h/time_step_size: convert by catchment area and actual seconds. Its total includes conceptual GW/runoff; partition/replace conceptual GW if external spatial solver. Potential ET is not actual atmospheric credit. Atmospheric mixing ratio not mass; flux-consistent dry-air convention and explicit heat. Transfer water kg or m³ with explicit density, do not reuse same numeric value in different units. f64 or compensated partitioned amounts: f32 ocean 8e15m³ loses 100m³ update, ULP ~537M m³. Local intensive f32 only with measured error.
Scheduler: atmosphere/land supplies ET demand, water donor accepts finite actual quantity and energy, face-advection, saturation/heat, finite cloud removal into falling precipitation, below-cloud evaporation, actual precipitation split by area, snow melt/refreeze, CFE infiltration/runoff/recharge, surface/GW routing, integrated erosion, revisioned terrain transactions. Each owner tracks completed physical horizon and pending amount, no duplicate credits on retries or applying future rain early. Bulk interval arrays not per-face/per-entity messages. Different stable step sizes reconcile one boundary transfer, not global smallest dt. Promotion/restriction moves stock and delayed history, parent summary becomes derived, no duplicate quantity. Terrain edit invalidates geometry and dependent topology; barrier closure effective before next relevant transfer, affected-basin repair may propagate nonlocally. Queries current/coarse/pending/stale explicitly labeled. Save/restart stocks, clocks, topology and pending exchanges.
Hydraulic method limits and pressure results
Ordinary reach IRF uses normalized response weights and finite transit queue; source mizuRoute conv_upsbas_qr has volume and future flow, clamp and shift, short-length branch resetting stock. Qualify exact remaining inventory, cap/withdrawal, delayed release and re-route when topology changes. Do not count queue and reach volume twice or lose capped release. Promote downstream shortcut to signed head mode before backwater/overflow/control matters; do not run both simultaneously over same water. Local inertia Qnew=(Qold+gAdt(etaA-etaB)/L)/(1+gdtn²abs(Qold)/(R^(4/3)*A)). Need monotone connected V(stage), face area/conveyance/sill/actual path length; no bathtub flood. Quasi-steady diffusive signed Manning challenger for slow flows. Use applicable control/rating laws or full shallow-water momentum for rapid falls/dam breaks. Sibling 1m dam-break local inertia normalized L1 ~40%, HLL 2.64% with exact ledger: local inertia not universal. FluxCell actual MIT source has HLLC, hydrostatic reconstruction, scalar and CPU reference; author 610–700M updates/s preprint not peer-reviewed nor local benchmark. Editable bed retains depth, solid mask fixed, GPU batches/readbacks/ownership need qualification; no full-island 1m solver.
Complementary actual independent C++20 O3 single thread virtual EPYC 9V74, 100x100km synthetic all-active rectangle, closed boundaries, 100mm/h x1h, piecewise volume and rectangular face, no true geometry/land/air/save/render. 1km/30s: 0.025300 CPU-ms/physical-s. 250m/30s: 0.383678; 250m/10s: 1.179750; 250m initially 5m/10s: 1.150764. 30.72MB arrays at 250m, max residual relative to initial+rain 3.42e-13. Fixed dt not certified. Tests stage inverse, no incoming below crest, reversal after momentum reset, simultaneous donor cap and gate; deliberately oversized 2-cell step oscillates 1->0 vs equilibrium 0.5 despite conserving water. Need finer actual reference, real geometry and timestep convergence.
Atmosphere and volumetric clouds
Weather3D parent hydrostatic anelastic C-grid 12 layers RK3, pressure projection each stage with DFT/Thomas and iterative terrain correction. Source includes Earth steering and internal moisture/soil clamps; no whole adoption. Compare 32/16km 8-layer reduced prognostic first, 4 layers only if storm/vertical accuracy passes, regional 8km/parameterized narrow convection. Cheap evolving diagnostic wind/heat benchmark control is not full weather. Need evolving pressure/wind, vertical exchange, terrain uplift/rain shadow, saturation and latent heat, seasonal/diurnal forcing, finite moisture. CliMT C-binding column physics is alternative reference with independent condensation/mixing/surface switches, JCM SPEEDY independent 8-level reference, COARE bulk exchange. CliMA 0M threshold relaxation analytic fixed-excess removal, adapt actual phase/fall-delay; ERF Kessler warm rain challenger. HBV snowpack solid/liquid degree-day melt/refreeze with actual stock and liquid retention; ice/heat approximations explicit. Weather and plant fields include wind direction/speed, humidity/temp, radiation, precipitation and wetness. Rivers velocity Q/A, wind-driven damped slab current for lakes/ocean, optional Coriolis; coastal storage/flow if surge impacts gameplay; no separate decorative physical water authority.
Independent constant-wind tracer 4000km 1D periodic, Gaussian sigma64km, 720km translation, CFL.1: 32km first-order L1 82.53% vs MC21.28%; 16km 59.22% vs6.95%; 8km39.06% vs1.91%. Both mass errors <1e-15. Varying velocity ordinary interpolation loses 3.53% in separate toy example, not Weather3D measurement. Sibling tests include narrow sigma12km: even 8km MC inadequate for tested threshold; subgrid convection or refine where needed. Sibling AVX2 four-scalar 16km 8-layer transport median 2.764ms/step only, no pressure/vertical/etc. Prefer MC/TVD, not upwind-only; validate actual multi-D flux-consistent mass and thermal dynamics.
True volumetric clouds mandatory. Sibling record source-reviewed SunshineClouds2 (MIT Godot compositor) and Godot-Cloud-Worlds (MIT SDF skipping). Test actual bounded 3D density shape volumes driven by atmospheric cloud mass/height/coverage and wind, 480x270 at 1080p, 24–48 primary steps, cheap light, empty-space skip, depth-aware temporal history/rejection. 32 primary steps all-screen 4.147M samples vs 132.71M full-HD/64; not GPU benchmark, nested lights and overlapping volumes can dominate. Eight 128³ R8 volumes 16MiB before mips; share cloud shape assets, not per-cloud grids. True local/fly-through density, distant sky cached if consistent, no sprite-only substitution. Weather determines amount/form and motion, visuals do not own moisture. Test above/inside/below, storm/dawn/night, depth edges, motion and time acceleration on RTX2070S. No measured GPU result.
Performance pressure and clocks
4000km: 16km page directory 62,500 x32B=1.91MiB; macro4km 1M x64B=61MiB; 1km 16M x64B=977MiB; 250m 256M x64B=15.26GiB. 32km atmospheric columns 15,625 x8=125k layer cells x64B=7.63MiB; 16km30.52MiB; 8km122.07MiB. Snapshots/face/pressure/geometry/stock/scratch excluded. At 8x, 25 CPU-ms/game-s=.2 CPU core average, ~3.33 CPU-ms/frame across workers at 60fps; at 64x 1.6 cores, ~26.67 CPU-ms/frame total, not main thread. Broad storms must not expand all fine regions. Hypothetical dense 1M surface cells at synthetic probe stride ~192MB before subgrid tables. Do not extrapolate as real performance.
Default day600 game seconds vs literal86400 physical seconds implies factor144. Independent 250m/30s cost becomes55.25 CPU-ms/game-s, 10s169.88, deep165.71 before others. Freeze explicit common coupled environment seconds/game second, qualify 1,10,144 and gameplay pacing. 1:1 is not accepted final time scale (1 physical hour spans 6 game days); calendar/solar forcing and geological years distinct. Don’t speed rain/ET alone or hide time multiplier. CFL includes effective storage/face dimensions and pressure/vertical stability; no arbitrary long step based on cheap mass-only check.
Bounded gate and Codex brief
No final technology lock beyond user’s terrain soft lock. High risks: actual refined topology/geometry without fine-world preprocessing; regime switching and stable subgrid flood accuracy; real reduced circulation plus mixed-phase heat; global physical/game-time pacing; true cloud GPU cost. Full compatibility designed, not validated. Proposed tolerances before tests: topology/closed barriers hard pass, compare stage/arrival and extent with independent finer reference (initial example extent IoU>=.85, arrival within 10% or one coarse step, relevant stage error <=.1m or 10% depth; select scenario thresholds before execution). Normalize conservation by transferred amount/local balance as well as world inventory. 

~1.5h work allocation: pin actual checkout, build GeoGenesis single-shot age/export, explicit original/filled fields, 256km macro and 4000km macro timing separately. No dense fine generation. If build fails, labeled known-answer fixture only, not natural baseline success.
~1.5h: bounded region plus adjacent seam, shared outlet/closed basin, selected PWG landform and Zylann render; compare repeat/reload and exact geometry/cave if possible.
~2h: qualify mizuRoute-type IRF (finite pending/withdrawal/promotion), Wflow-type subgrid head transport and FluxCell CPU reference on known-answer dam/levee/arrival. Do not require successful wholesale port. Compare native only same criteria, no preference. 
~2h: actual CFE donor and finite rain/ET/heat, MC transport, reduced wind/pressure donor or explicit limited control; test downwind rain, cloud phase and snow; no claim full atmosphere if prescribed. 
~1h: normal host connected small natural terrain/water/weather, terrain edit and save/reload, actual visuals (true volumetric cloud smoke test if feasible), offscreen, inclusive costs and exact blockers. Subsequent whole-island actual storm, long-distance travel and population gate, not accepted on toy data.
This is a bounded one-day qualification proposal, not a promise to finish all systems in one day. Codex: read accepted Brain records and pinned source, one writer, separate scratch lineage; retain Godot/Jolt/Zylann, no LandscapeChannels, no whole app transplant, no new scheduler/voxel tree by default. Follow gates, record actual commands/source/binary, CPU/game and physical seconds, GPU/RAM/VRAM, init/prep/rebuild, visual result, failures and remaining uncertainty. User authorization needed for game runtime changes; no main merge here.

environmental-foundation-v1-execution.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — execution protocol
environmental-foundation-v1-execution.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — execution protocol
Authorized 26 November 2026. This operational protocol accompanies the full technical implementation plan and the progress record. It governs the user’s intended Extra High planning/orchestration chat and High implementation/worker chat. Model naming and actual delegation capabilities depend on the available Codex interface; do not pretend to control another chat if the interface does not support it. No new engine code or test execution is claimed here.
Mission
Complete M0 preparation and every delivery milestone M1–M5 of the technical plan as one continuous full replacement. Deliver real integrated functionality, not a report-only pilot. The new implementation is the standard for fresh worlds; remove/disconnect superseded environmental mechanisms and legacy selection paths when the replacement is ready. Do not keep a second production water system, duplicate atmosphere, legacy compatibility layer, or old save conversion merely for continuity. Keep useful gameplay, Godot/Jolt, existing Zylann terrain integration, actual physical contracts, and historical evidence. Protect unrelated local changes, assets, user saves and installations.
M1 aged editable terrain, M2 finite water, M3 actual coupled weather, M4 erosion/migrating rivers and attractive rendering, M5 integrated scale and release evidence. Do not broaden into full ECS/population, complete ecology, all other liquids, new terrain engine or unrelated legacy repair. Keep interfaces compatible with later goals and distinguish deferred scope from complete.
Orchestrator and worker

Orchestrator: owns the end-to-end plan, selected dependency manifest, sequence and integration boundaries. Read latest canonical Brain and actual worker receipts. Give the worker concrete bounded implementation packages with source pin, scope, acceptance, target paths if known, dependency order and commit/report expectations. Use independent implementation judgement, not micromanagement. Review exact diffs and evidence for changed paths, resolve routine issues, adjust reversible tunables, then immediately advance to next package/milestone. No request for approval simply because one package or milestone finishes.
Worker: owns actual code/build/edit work in the assigned checkout. Implement the selected existing algorithms and minimal native adapters; prefer reuse, simple data structures and physical consistency. Make necessary related call-site changes and remove superseded paths rather than preserve old environmental architecture. Perform only the directly useful checks, fix local issues within scope, record actual results and report the exact code commit, changed capabilities, incomplete requirements, checks, costs and any real blocker. Return work that runs where feasible, not pseudocode or fixture-only substitution. Do not invent new solver or change fundamental scope without orchestrator decision.
One writer per checkout. Orchestrator is accountable for canonical documentation and publication; worker supplies evidence and may author assigned docs when ownership is explicitly handed off. Coordinate via commits and the durable progress record, not duplicated work. If the interface supports actual subagents, use them; otherwise deliver a self-contained worker task and consume its returned receipt in the orchestrator chat. A separate chat does not automatically receive messages or keep running merely because another chat has been prompted.
Continue across all milestones within available execution sessions. If a context/session boundary occurs, save a precise continuation with the next executable package, current commit and real open issue; do not claim background execution or completion. Neither agent stops for routine design choices, optimization tradeoffs within the accepted architecture, ordinary builds/fixes or milestones. Do not create automated infinite loops or repeat failed attempts without changing the diagnosis.

Implementation-first verification
Minimum purposeful verification, not zero verification. Use the same small connected world and concise directly relevant checks for changed numerical/geometry behavior. Reuse upstream tests where useful, without reproducing all scientific benchmarks. One normal build/launch and small core behavior check when a coherent milestone is ready; use quick profiling during integration and one representative combined scale run/capture at M5, with enough repeat/diagnostic detail to make measured claims meaningful. Run additional checks only to diagnose a consequential failure. Prefer fixing the feature over writing a large verification framework. Do not run exhaustive old regression suites, full legacy compatibility campaigns, performance matrices for every candidate, or repair unrelated failing tests. Keep Brain’s normal automated validation and safe publication; it is not a competing physics campaign.
Do not waive finite water/heat exchanges, sealed-barrier correctness, meaningful downstream consequences, current geometry, offscreen progression, persistence and actual weather. Preserve honest units/clocks and evidence. A playable approximation is appropriate; scientific forecast precision is not the goal. Do not label performance, scale or unexecuted functionality as passed. Historical targets and proposed acceptance tolerances remain as in the technical plan; choose meaningful local tolerances before checking, not after failure. If target hardware unavailable, say so and continue other implementable work; don’t block every feature on exhaustive target certification.
Stop and escalate only when necessary
Escalate if the primary upstream method is fundamentally unsuitable, a substantial bespoke numerical solver would be required, a hard physical requirement or performance envelope cannot be achieved without a product tradeoff, a material dependency/license change or fundamental clock/gameplay choice needs approval, or real permission/hardware/access/safety constraints make further meaningful work impossible. First make a bounded diagnosis and attempt the smallest compatible fix; do not spend days on circular tuning. Continue independent unblocked work where sensible. Report: exact failure or conflict, evidence, what has been tried, impact on the plan, one recommended path, and the precise decision or research question. Do not stop simply to ask for routine confirmation. Do not suppress the blocker to mark a milestone complete.
Two-repository workflow

Canonical private repo: github.com/caleb-var/godot_aokana. Inspect actual HEAD, nested AGENTS, local ownership and remote state. Create a reviewable implementation branch/worktree from appropriate runtime source head, synchronize the active V1 plan/authorization, commit coherent code changes and push for review. New runtime becomes the default fresh-world implementation on this branch; use normal repository merge controls rather than force-push or overwrite unrelated work.
Canonical authored documentation resides under docs/brain/content/ in the same private repo. The authorized publication ref is docs/breachborn-brain-refresh-20261125. Keep this ref current via a dedicated documentation worktree or controlled small docs-only commits based on its latest head. Reflect relevant records in the implementation branch as needed; do not merge unrelated runtime changes onto the docs branch. Avoid parallel writers and reconcile automatic generated-index commits before each update. Use stable IDs/typed edges, preserve existing records and historical negative evidence. Update affected systems, contracts, candidate selection/status, requirements traceability, and the V1 progress record after each meaningful package/milestone. Keep intent/selected/implemented/verified separate and cite exact source/code revision.
Public generated repo: github.com/caleb-var/breachborn-brain, main; live site caleb-var.github.io/breachborn-brain/. Never manually edit public generated files, copy private code/history/saves, or expose credentials or confidential local details. Author canonical Markdown, run python docs/brain/tools/atlas.py --write, python docs/brain/tools/atlas.py --check and python docs/brain/tools/test_brain.py when available, then commit/push the authorized docs ref. The existing .github/workflows/brain-validation.yml regenerates/checks/builds and publishes only approved generated Brain output. Confirm workflow result and public mirror source revision after each meaningful documentation update when accessible; if it is pending or fails, record status, fix bounded documentation issues, never bypass publication safety. Do not wait on routine asynchronous publication before implementing the next independent package. A failed mirror publication does not erase canonical progress.
Do not expose private source snippets, logs, filesystem details, or sensitive user data in publicly authored records. Keep detailed private runtime evidence outside docs/brain/content/ where necessary and publish safe summaries and reference identities.

Progress and completion
Provide concise progress receipts at integrated packages and every milestone, without waiting for a user reply: completed/working, exact commits, changes from plan, directly relevant checks and measured/estimated distinction, unresolved issue, documentation commit and mirror status, next work. Persist them in the progress record and relevant canonical system records. Use one lightweight status record, not a custom orchestration platform.
Final report: implemented M1–M5 capability status, actual default-path replacement, remaining known limitations, measured scale/CPU/GPU/RAM/debt and visual evidence where available, commits/PRs, dependency notices and canonical Brain publication state. Do not call an unfinished or unmeasured implementation complete. The user wants maximum implementation, not maximum paperwork.

environmental-foundation-v1-progress.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation progress
environmental-foundation-v1-progress.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation progress
Updated 26 November 2026. Technical plan and execution protocol govern this full replacement.








































MilestoneStatusEvidenceM0 Prepare and pinInitial preparation completeInitial pinned build and isolated host reproduced. Later dependency closures will be checked as used.M1 Aged editable terrainFoundation verified on bounded hostGeoGenesis and PWG terrain, material channels, surveyed marine mouth, cold terrain continuation and offline 4,000 km census verified. Visual polish and remaining basin contacts are open.M2 Water replacementIn progressBounded Wflow routing, CFE, finite groundwater and surface exchange verified. The isolated rapid patch matches the pinned FluxCell reference and retains exact state through a separate Godot reopen while water is moving. One above-bank floodplain patch passed connected wetting and current-voxel remapping of wet storage and faces. Bounded terrain and finite land, surface and groundwater restore together. Broad flooding and production saves remain open.M3 Live coupled weatherIn progressMoving eight-layer warm weather with overlapped finite CFE and open-water exchange passed in the bounded native and Godot fixture, including continuation with rain in flight. Bounded mixed phase also passed with falling and ground snow, heat-limited melt and independent continuation. Bounded Forward+ clouds and the solar land heat budget passed. Broader routing and sustained regional forcing remain open.M4 Erosion and visual worldIn progressThe normal Forward+ colony displays accepted V1 clouds and skips out-of-view occupied air. Two accepted-flow wet-bank edits use the same loaded reach and conserve finite water and sediment custody across an independent reopen. Continuous terrain evolution and production visual acceptance remain open.M5 Integrated scaleIn progressA fresh 128 km world ran a 100 km warm weather window, and a fresh 256 km world ran a local weather event. A 4,000 km opening activated two distant water neighborhoods. A display window paced one bounded crop at a requested 8×. The actual colony scene passed a bounded paired V1 clock and save trial. The tested Windows addon makes V1 the normal fresh-world default in the packaged scene. Sustained production scale remains open.
Preparation checkpoint
The reviewable implementation branch starts at canonical revision 67cb525f2a2b, which contains the committed runtime snapshot 38b4dadc in its history. Implementation and canonical publication have separate workspaces. The preceding canonical revision passed Brain validation and publication, and the public site deployed its generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Root license files at the plan pins were checked for GeoGenesis, PWG, Zylann, Wflow, CFE, FluxCell, MeanderPy, Weather3D, CloudMicrophysics, COARE and SunshineClouds2. Each implementation package records the files incorporated, local adaptations and the required notices. At kickoff, downstream dependency closure and native builds were still unverified.
First terrain package
Commit 1b83f78f adds the pinned GeoGenesis formation and age path, the immutable native terrain recipe and the isolated Zylann inspection scene. For seed 713, 40,000 modeled years changed all 3,072 checked bed cells above 0.01 m. The two 234,808-byte exports matched exactly. A display-backed run checked SDF agreement across LOD0/LOD2 and a live voxel edit. It streamed the checked area in 452 ms. This capture shows the provisional macro terrain. A separate offline coarse export covered 4,000×4,000 km at 4 km resolution. It took 3.465 s inside the exporter, including 0.950 s of aging and 0.879 s of export, and peaked at 334 MiB of guard job memory. Full-world runtime performance and normal fresh-world startup remain unmeasured. Terrain evidence
The preceding kickoff update at 3536d4eb passed the canonical workflow and deployed the corresponding public mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Channel and basin geometry
Commit 0c4fa5dd integrates selected PWG curves and channel profiles into the shared native recipe. The live terrain shows a curved dry channel. The fixture contains 69 reaches, including a linked 1 m tributary, and distinguishes marine areas from below-datum inland bodies and priority-flood depressions. Ten unresolved reach contacts remain explicit. The local stream interval was 143 ms in this display-backed run. Geometry evidence
The offline macro update at 54866b3a passed canonical validation and deployed to Pages. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Editable terrain and cold continuation
Commit 419370d7 connects geological material IDs and the V1 recipe to the existing RegionWorld and Zylann current-voxel stream. The write and independent reopen completed in 8.76 s. The new process recovered exact SDF and material channel bytes for one mine edit. An approximately 1.03 m generated marine mouth now has surveyed geometry. Eight links remain unresolved. The capture shows the dry carved channel with geological tones. Terrain continuation evidence
The prior geometry update at c1661edc passed on the second canonical run after the mobile smoke test timed out on its first attempt. The matching generated mirror deployed. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
First finite surface flow
Commit 1bfb9f8c connects the selected Wflow routines to 82 finite stores and 58 measured links in the small V1 parcel. The sealed gate passed with zero transfer. Opening moved 0.637 m³ in 20 physical seconds and the native test verified reverse flow and a finite withdrawal. The actual Godot snapshot matches the ordinary-flow result. The steep marine case requested rapid-flow ownership before accepting any time. V1 water evidence
The terrain continuation update at 619ecca9 passed canonical publication and the matching public Pages deployment. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Runoff and groundwater
Commit d4cb5f9d integrates the pinned CFE land routines and finite Wflow groundwater with the same surface stores. Two generated sites closed volume, heat and passive mass balances. The test observed 19.294 m³ cumulative runoff, 4.769 m³ recharge and 1.200 m³ actual ET over 5,400 s of model time, with delayed runoff retained when the surface receiver was full. Native and headless Godot checks matched in a 4.58 s guarded run. V1 water evidence
The surface update at 19a5da4e passed canonical publication and deployed through Pages. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Bounded rapid water
Commit fd08bba7 integrates the pinned FluxCell MUSCL-Hancock/HLLC CPU path in a 24 × 48, one-metre patch over the seed-713 carved terrain. The sealed gate passed zero water. Opening four cells moved 2.976 m³ downstream in six physical seconds. The native and Godot runs agreed and returned all 36 m³, sensible heat, dissolved mass and suspended mass through a single custody handoff. The corrected native depths and both momentum components match the upstream reference within 1.81 × 10⁻¹⁶ in their respective units. V1 rapid-water evidence
The M2c Brain update at 8a62b216 passed canonical validation and deployed the generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Above-bank floodplain exchange
Commit 42abc99f prepares nine surveyed floodplain compartments beside the generated reach. Separate stage curves and measured bank and lateral faces use the existing Wflow-derived finite transport. An open bank filled the first compartment while the sealed lateral control kept the second dry. Opening the lateral face reached the second compartment at 4.5 s of accepted time. The headless Godot session reproduced the native result. V1 floodplain evidence
The floodplain Brain update at 0e689b3b passed canonical validation and deployed the generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Cold finite water and terrain continuation
Commit ddb8650f records the surface owner’s finite inventories, signed face state and clock, together with the land and groundwater stocks and pending queues. A distinct Godot process restored the same water bytes, 11.558 m³ of held runoff and the exact current channels of a four-block voxel edit. The continued withdrawal and exchange at 5,400 physical seconds matched the uninterrupted control, and the resumed instance saved again. V1 cold continuation evidence
The cold-continuation Brain update at 7a6aef97 passed canonical validation and deployed the generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Current voxel flood-face repair
Commit e991052f binds surveyed lateral flood faces to revisions from the current Zylann stream. Godot placed a temporary earth barrier over a still-open face. Water time and checkpoints paused while its geometry was stale, and after resurvey the higher crest passed zero water. Exact terrain rollback reopened the face and finite flow resumed. V1 face repair evidence
The flood-face Brain update at b5dc2b9b passed canonical validation and deployed the generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Finite warm atmosphere and land exchange
Commit eeb07f99 couples the selected Weather3D warm saturation adjustment and CliMA 0M tendencies to CFE. Two bounded columns delivered 0.1064 m³ of rain, returned 0.1298 m³ of actual ET to the air and routed 0.001742 m³ of accepted runoff. The independent Godot process recovered airborne rain and condensate, then matched the uninterrupted state at 3,600 physical seconds. V1 warm weather evidence
The warm-weather Brain update at d4dad310 passed canonical validation and deployed the generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Finite open-water heat and evaporation
Commit 5bbad4ef couples the pinned COARE neutral coefficients to the covered part of the existing finite reach. It evaporated 3.510 L of open water and transferred 2.672 MJ of sensible heat to the air over 3,600 physical seconds. The full native and Godot balances closed, and the independent continuation matched. V1 open-water evidence
The open-water Brain update at 97c12d73 passed canonical validation and deployed the generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Native pressure projection
Commit 6f8949b2 computes the variable-column-mass pressure correction with a pinned PocketFFT cosine transform and closed boundaries. It preserved a specified circulating field while removing the imposed gradient. The native controls took 6.25 ms on 125² columns and 23.51 ms on 250². The later coupled moving-grid check uses this kernel. V1 pressure evidence
The pressure Brain update at 1a10d3de passed canonical validation and deployed the generated mirror. Canonical workflow · Mirror deployment
Native hydrostatic circulation
Commit e2497325 advances Weather3D hydrostatic forcing, terrain-weighted pressure correction and rigid-lid vertical continuity. A thermal anomaly drove three-dimensional conservative heat, vapor and cloud transport on 3,072 columns with eight layers. The 200 s control took 123.55 ms of native step wall time. V1 circulation evidence
Coupled moving warm weather
Commit 7255aa04 replaces the stationary columns in the connected V1 fixture with 42 terrain-derived columns and eight layers. Native and two headless Godot processes verified wind-driven transport, finite CFE and COARE exchange and byte-matching continuation at 3,600 seconds from falling rain at 60 seconds. The moving fixture delivered 21.38 L of rain, all consumed by CFE rain evapotranspiration. Moving weather evidence
Coupled mixed-phase weather
Commit 9bc119f3 adds cloud ice, finite falling snow, ground snow and heat-limited melt to the same moving owner. The colder fixture advanced 3,600 seconds, with 82.84 m³ water-equivalent ground snow and 4.47 m³ melted. Native and both Godot processes passed, with byte-matching continuation after saving rain and snow in flight at 60 seconds. The warm control also passed. Mixed-phase evidence
Accepted cloud volume and motion
Commit a54c3a46 publishes a world-aligned cut-cell cloud volume from the accepted weather clock. Native and Godot checks verified cloud density and wind. Both headless profiles reproduced the volume after independent recovery and changed its contents as weather advanced. Cloud field evidence
Display-backed volumetric clouds
Commit 96fdc29c connects the accepted V1 cloud field to the pinned SunshineClouds2 compositor. A guarded 1080p Vulkan run captured the same formation below, above and inside, then changed the scene lighting. Sampled compositor GPU p95 was 2.97 ms on RTX 2070 Super. The effect released its resources before the weather owner saved and continued. The generated terrain footprint remains visibly bounded. Volumetric cloud evidence
Current-voxel wet flood storage
Commit 8eb1c621 remaps surveyed wet flood storage and its represented bank and lateral faces from the same Zylann revision. The Godot excavation lowered the occupied cell’s water stage from 1927.7061 m to 1924.6265 m at 2.024 m³, with heat, solute and suspended mass unchanged. A distinct process reopened the edited world and reproduced the next finite state. Wet storage evidence
Current-voxel ordinary reach storage
Commit a1703040 resamples four sections in one eight-metre ordinary reach strip. The existing owner retained 2 m³ while its stage fell below the still-open outlet after excavation. The native owner refused a raised internal saddle that needs separate shelf custody. An independent Godot process reproduced the accepted edit and next water state. Ordinary reach evidence
Flow-driven loose-bed movement
Commit 5042c059 integrates accepted Wflow-derived outlet flow and hydraulic radius into a Shields-informed shear exposure. Selected MeanderPy upstream curvature weighting chooses the bank. The existing V1 session erodes one current loose sample, surveys the changed storage and credits the suspended lane once. The sealed control accumulates no exposure. Independent Godot recovers the edit and sediment. Terrain evolution evidence
Fresh formation through the connected host
Commit 43bce84e moves fresh recipe creation into the V1 Godot session. The packaged exporter generated and admitted the seed-713 parcel in 1.30 s. The same session rendered mixed-phase clouds at 1080p and saved an airborne checkpoint. An independent host recovered from disk and matched the continued water and cloud state. Runtime formation evidence
Land heat and the solar boundary
Commit 156da4cd puts absorbed solar and outgoing longwave on the same accepted wind, precipitation and water clock. A finite land slab exchanges sensible heat and informs evapotranspiration. The dusk fixture recorded no new sunlight after sunset, cooled 0.83 K and continued byte-identically in a distinct Godot process. Radiation evidence
Wider terrain and two active water neighborhoods
Commit 51081a5b exercises fresh 256 km terrain with one 30-column weather event. It also opens a 4,000 km macro recipe, validates current voxel reads in two regions, and advances both finite water routes in one interval. The macro opening generated 2,468 blocks on demand. Wider world evidence
Bounded display pacing
Commit 37cd5f67 advances the live V1 session against a supplied physical horizon in complete 10 s quanta. The paced Forward+ fixture accepted 100 physical seconds in 12.533 wall seconds at a requested 8× and finished with zero debt. Frame p95 was 16.91 ms, and the cloud effect measured 2.94 ms GPU p95. A separate Godot process matched the one-hour continuation. Display pacing evidence
Rapid flow saved in transit
Commit d78a9bbf preserves the active FluxCell grid, gate, accepted time and exclusive parcel ownership in a V1 terrain and water save. Independent Godot reopened with 2.976 m³ downstream, advanced to 4.049 m³ downstream and reconciled the full 36 m³ once. The saved, continued and reconciled bytes matched the uninterrupted run. Rapid continuation evidence
Active rapid bed repair
Commit 25103282 pauses the active fine grid against stale terrain, samples the affected bed from the current Zylann revision and preserves the parcel through the edit. A separate Godot process reproduced the edited in-flight checkpoint and the continued fine state. The edited patch retains custody until a coarse geometry handoff is available. Rapid bed evidence
100 km moving warm weather
Commit 45058453 widens the existing atmosphere to a saved 100 km window on a fresh 128 km terrain. The same eight-layer solver produced rain at 286 columns and routed 33.4 L of accepted runoff through the two small receiving sites. Independent Godot reproduced the one-hour endpoint from rain in flight. Peak accumulated rain was 0.87 mm. Severe regional flooding and recession remain open. Regional weather evidence
Recurrent finite-flow bank cuts
Commit ebd96023 services the watched ordinary reach through bounded accepted intervals and applies a current-voxel edit when accumulated shear permits. The independent Godot process reopened after the first cut and reproduced the second cut’s channels and water state. Two loose samples credited a cumulative 3,200 kg under the declared bulk-density model. Recurrent erosion evidence
Colony clock and selected save
Commit b73b85aa admits the V1 trial through the normal gameplay scene and uses completed actor time for the water and weather horizon. One 16-actor run saved at 64 gameplay seconds with 60 physical environment seconds accepted. A separate process selected the same paired checkpoint and continued to 128 gameplay and 120 accepted environment seconds. The save contains the V1 state in the native checkpoint payload. Colony integration evidence
Packaged fresh default and displayed colony
Commit 388ebe65 stages the verified Windows V1 addon for ordinary fresh launch. The 1080p Forward+ run started the V1 colony without an opt-in, displayed live terrain and 16 actors, and reached 64 gameplay seconds in 8.004 wall seconds. The native player control requested 8×, and a separate process reopened the paired checkpoint. Packaged colony evidence
Accepted clouds in the normal colony scene
Commit 6827168c uses the existing compositor without creating a separate atmosphere. It aligns each accepted volume to the current Zylann render origin and skips an out-of-view volume. The bounded normal start measured 64 simulated seconds in 8.002 wall seconds with 16.82 ms frame p95. A separate view in the same scene displayed the accepted cloud with 2.84 ms compositor GPU p95. The ordinary save still reopened independently. Colony cloud evidence
Current handoff
The colony entry has a bounded 1:1 clock and paired checkpoint trial. The user confirmed 1:1 physical-to-gameplay seconds for initial playable testing, with 8× gameplay speed as the baseline and 32× as a stretch target. The shared clock and checkpoint passed headless and displayed tests from the packaged fresh-world default. The normal scene renders accepted clouds in their represented footprint. Production art and sustained multi-system measurements remain open. Long-run morphodynamics, deposition and reach cutoffs remain open. Sustained weather forcing, broad land and flood routing, atmospheric terrain remapping and production stability remain open. Remaining M2 work includes wider ordinary channel and basin storage remapping, caves, wide-area flooding, moving coarse/fine exchange and return from a surveyed rapid patch to updated coarse geometry. Normal fresh-world adoption and severe-storm performance are unverified.

environmental-foundation-v1.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation-first plan
environmental-foundation-v1.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation-first plan
26 November 2026. The user agreed to the implementation-first direction: choose evidence-backed upstream numerical implementations, stop prolonged standalone comparative campaigns, and create a concrete continuation plan. This is the selected provisional design baseline, not a declaration that an integrated solver or the performance target has passed. It supersedes the research-first sequencing of water-first qualification; preserve that document and pressure-test evidence, upstream water evidence, reuse decision, formation decision, and requirements. No runtime source changed by this document. The user subsequently authorized full replacement implementation in Codex on 26 November 2026; see execution protocol and the current task scope. Actual runtime implementation has not started by virtue of this documentation change.
1. Deliverable and scope
Deliver a normal playable Godot fresh-world foundation with aged realistic-stylized terrain, distinct curved rivers and meaningful tributaries, finite lakes/ocean, land/soil and groundwater, causal rain/evaporation/heat/wind, connected flooding and recession, local interactive water, slow erosion/migration and real attractive volumetric clouds. Include persistent current geometry and edits, cheap native gameplay field queries and navigation-hazard invalidation. Scale by geography and actual work, not camera visibility; a 100×100 km storm, offscreen changes and a 4,000 km macro configuration are required scale evidence, not optional presentation. Full 100k+ population, complete ecology, all liquid families, advanced abilities and final art content are later dependent scopes; retain their contracts, don’t claim them complete or create irreversible limits. Basic groundwater/cave contacts, finite ocean and cold-phase water cycle are required environmental closure cases, not optional infinite sources.
One primary implementation per role. Ordinary small correctness fixtures, source equivalence and profiling occur while delivering features. No parallel full solver implementations, bespoke PDE engine, reimplementation of vendor test catalogs, revival of LandscapeChannels, or reuse preference for failed native environment mechanisms. Existing Godot/Jolt, Zylann, useful terrain editing, coordinates and integration boundaries may be retained. Preserve legacy artifacts and unpublished work; fresh-world policy is not a migration mandate.
2. Dependency and numerical reuse manifest
Pins are previously inspected source snapshots, not necessarily latest releases or a transitive license approval. Preserve notices and independently check selected files/build dependencies before incorporation. Prefer original callable kernels over copying a whole application; native ports must preserve the upstream numerical method. Record the exact upstream files used and deviations. Do not embed unapproved GPL/AGPL code.











































































RolePrimary source and pinReuse / integration boundaryGeneration / ageGeoGenesis, MITRust single-shot simulation and geology/age/erosion. Small C ABI/export if needed; no second full mutable world. Drainage-area incision versus climate-derived actual discharge requires calibrated adaptation, not a claim that existing code already uses Q for all erosion.Landforms/initial river geometryPWG, MITMain river network/geometry, channel profiles, selected landform functions, deterministic constrained refinement. Do not import viewer or forced joins/8m creek cap.Current solidsZylann, existing pinSparse editable SDF/material, streaming and mesh/collision. Verify actual checkout identity; no duplicate voxel engine.Regional hydraulicsWflow, MITSigned local-inertial flow, stage/area/perimeter lookup, suitable reservoir/groundwater methods. Use actual upstream routines, preserving numerical formulation and stable stepping constraints. Adapt topology/geometry and finite transfer boundaries; reject stock common-stage floodplain and negative-stock clipping. Not a stock turnkey Wflow installation.Root zone/runoffNOAA CFE, Apache-2.0Native C infiltration, root-zone storage, realized ET, lateral/runoff delay. Existing adapter only if narrow and correct. Spatial aquifer owns recharge; CFE conceptual groundwater must be removed/reconciled, not duplicated. Preserve all queue masses and correct units.GroundwaterWflow pin aboveUnconfined saturated thickness, harmonic conductance, finite head/storage and river/spring contact. Use source units and suitable stable timestep; no external constant head creating water without a named inventory. Cavities are separate physical compartments, not a duplicate aquifer.Rapid/detail surfaceFluxCell, MITUpstream MUSCL-Hancock/HLLC, CPU reference and bounded GPU or native path. Use exact scoped results in SRC-WATER-UPSTREAM, not a full suite or target GPU pass. GPU bed update keeps depth; solid mask is fixed; negative sparse source rejected. Explicit withdrawal, safe topology changes and finite parent exchange needed. No dense global grid.Channel migrationMeanderPy, Apache-2.0Curvature/upstream weighting, cutoff and resampling, bounded slow evolution in suitable alluvial channels. Actual discharge/shear/material forcing and physical sediment/geometry edits required; stock migration is not directly flow-driven. O(N) exponential recurrence permissible with constant weighting coefficient, preserving original padding/spacing; no plotting/runtime history package.CirculationWeather3D, MIT sourceReduced hydrostatic/anelastic C-grid core, momentum, hydrostatic diagnostics, vertical continuity, barotropic correction. Do not import full WebGPU app, Earth climatology, default moisture sources or its soil model. Actual native port and conservative coupling are significant work.Transport and cloud phaseconservative MC/TVD and CliMA 0M, Apache-2.0Conservative flux-limited horizontal and vertical water/energy transport; scalar bulk condensation/precipitation/evaporation tendencies, cold phase, latent heat. 0M alone is instantaneous precipitation removal; explicitly own falling water/snow and cap evaporation/condensation by available mass and saturation. No Julia runtime by default.Surface energyCOARE 3.6, MITAir-water bulk exchange coefficient/flux calculation; use actual accepted ET/evaporation and heat transfer, appropriate land/lake calibration, finite thermal inventories. No prescribed ocean temperature reset.Cloud renderingSunshineClouds2, MITActual Godot compositor/volumetric rendering. Reduce stock 300 ray/32 lighting step limits; data-driven discrete shapes, multi-altitude forms, depth compositing and temporal history. No duplicated physical weather.NavigationHPA/DHPA and existing local Recast/Detour directionNot a population rewrite in V1. Publish passability, depth/velocity, door/barrier and geometry revisions for later local paths/hierarchical summaries. Do not require world-wide metre occupancy.
Fallbacks are not parallel implementations. SFINCS scientific reference (GPL-3.0, embedding not approved), ADCIRC (LGPL review and topology issues), mizuRoute (ordinary downstream only) remain available only if primary fails a named requirement. ERF warm-rain and other archived atmospheric models are reference/fallback only. A new technology search must be driven by a specific demonstrated blocker, not routine development.
3. Final source-level reuse review
Wflow: surface_process.jl takes prior discharge, two stages, face water depth, area, hydraulic radius, path length, squared Manning roughness, Froude limit and dt. Signed semi-implicit friction law is directly separable. Floodplain profile functions provide depth/flow area/wetted perimeter/storage inversion. Groundwater and river-groundwater contact are narrow donors. Its regional storage update merges river and floodplain to common stage and records negative corrections after clipping; do not preserve these semantics. Stable timestep is a depth/length bound for its discretization, not proof for new subgrid graph. Use existing update loops where compatible; independent compartments, connected face geometry, simultaneous finite transfer acceptance, topology repair and subgrid stability are genuine integration changes. A Froude cap cannot be used to suppress a rapid flood. Earlier independent probe shows dry-dam front error about 54% for simplified local inertia. Keep it for ordinary low-Froude flows; promote or use a qualified shock-capable representation when needed.
Weather3D: pe.wgsl computes hydrostatic and vertical mass continuity; momentum and nonconservative scalar transport are in pe_stage. pe.js projects each of three RK stages, with variable-column-mass iterations using direct DFT/inverse transforms and Thomas solve. For square 125²/250² grid, one direct forward/inverse pair per each of three stages is 6*N³ = 11,718,750 / 93,750,000 inner summation terms per full timestep, excluding iterations and column work. Do not port direct DFT literally. Reuse an established permissively licensed fast transform/linear-algebra backend suitable for the chosen boundary conditions (audit existing dependencies first), and retain variable-coefficient correction and residual control where needed. Do not assume periodic-x/closed-y fits a bounded world; choose saved boundary policy and explicit fluxes, e.g. compatible no-normal-flow boundaries with matching transform/solver, or a deliberately periodic world. Reference profiles, Earth-dependent nudging and independent soil/moisture/SST forcing cannot create water/energy; disable or replace with accounted game forcing. Conservative face transport must use the same dry-air mass flux, include vertical face transfers and consistent latent/sensible energy. This is a reduced-model port, not a turnkey atmosphere. Do not present dropping pressure correction or clamping negative humidity as an optimization pass.
4. Shared physical representation

Whole-world metric coordinates (checked wide integer identity; local float offsets), independent solver lattices. Initial configurable macro geography ~4km for 4,000km; 16km addressing pages, not solver boundaries; 32km atmosphere with 8 layers as initial cost-conscious starting point, local/nested 16km or smaller where justified. Pilot smaller domain with appropriate resolution, not a single uniform 32km cell presented as a storm.
Aged geometry produces persistent feature IDs, channel polylines/splines and true length, bed/bank profiles, cross sections, crest/sill elevations, compartments/outlet connectivity, V(stage), wet area and face conveyance, material/soil/roughness/cover, cave contacts. Fine realization and all derived tables agree with the same recipe+edits. No render-stage-driven recarving, no global metre DEM/SDF scans. Regional fine sampling only where required; keep hydrographic topology correct across page boundaries. Sparse channel density around 0.1 km/km² of land and average 2km hydraulic segments are proposed configurable starting settings, not arbitrary minimum/maximum or user-approved immutable counts. Retain meaningful 1m creeks, unbounded meaningful river widths, natural confluences, beautiful curved planform; omitted minor drainage contributes actual catchment runoff and can produce local wetness.
Surface authoritative quantities: volume, stage derived from current geometry, signed flow/momentum as required by selected method, thermal and relevant constituent mass. Soil owns actual storage and runoff queue; spatial groundwater owns aquifer head/storage; ocean is finite. Air owns dry-air convention, temperature/energy, wind/pressure, vapor/condensate/falling precipitation. Geometry has a revision; each field snapshot has coverage/precision/time, not an alternative physical owner. No per-renderer state as physical truth.
At a common accepted model interval: air supplies integrated precipitation; partition once by receiving area and geometry; soil yields runoff/recharge; surface accepts flow and withdrawals; actual ET/open-water evaporation/heat return once; record finite pending transfers until consumed. Conservative sums, nonnegative donor amounts, and overlap in space/time. Update material only from accumulated real erosion/deposition; refresh affected geometry/navigation and conserve water when volume changes. Refinement replaces parent authority for represented volume, and coarsening reconciles actual stock/tracer/heat and timing; no double counting. Trigger by physical state or interactions, not camera. Renderer reads snapshots only.

5. Clocks and engineering cost envelope
Retain configurable 600s/day, 60 days/year calendar. Do not require 144 physical seconds per game-second for every physical process simply to match an Earth day. Initial playable test setting: common water/atmosphere physical clock of 1 physical second per simulated game-second, with separately saved calendar/solar forcing. Caleb confirmed 1:1 for the initial testing, an 8× wall-clock gameplay baseline and a 32× gameplay stretch target. The tested physical mapping and the gameplay-speed setting are independent. Production acceptance still requires the integrated measurements below. At 8x simulation a 20 physical-second release lasts 2.5 real seconds at alpha1, 0.208s at alpha12, 0.0174s at alpha144. Weather movement, water cycle, runoff queues and season pacing must be coherent under the declared clock; no pretending this is an Earth-time 24h day, no independent camera clock. If pacing is too slow, adjust a declared world/physical policy with measured cost, not silent dt compression. Historical alpha144 remains a sensitivity comparator.
Arithmetic from recorded synthetic EPYC probes and upstream claim, not target performance: 50% land over 16Mkm² ×0.1km/km² /2km =400k reaches; 64B/reach illustrative 24.4MiB before curves, edges, scratch, saves. At 29.8ns/update, one full update is 11.92ms; at hypothetical stable dt300 physical seconds, alpha1/12/144 =0.040/0.477/5.722 aggregate CPU-ms/game-s. At dt60s =0.199/2.384/28.608. This does not establish actual graph or Wflow update cost/stability. A 100x100km storm with 250m cells previously measured synthetic 45.92 CPU-ms/game-s at alpha144 -> .319 at alpha1; 1km .761 ->.0053, not proof of comparable fidelity. 32/16km atmosphere transport+column probes .77/4.95 at alpha144 -> .0053/.0344 at alpha1; dynamics not included. Actual cadence constrained by geometry, dynamics and accuracy. Do not infer combined budget from these estimates. 256² at 1m, dt=.05s, 8x at alpha1 needs 10.49M cell updates/s, nominal .287 GPU-ms/frame at FluxCell’s author-reported 610M/s; at alpha144 41.26ms/frame, before integration. Do not use high-resolution solver everywhere. Budget from actual complete workload and peak service cost, not divided by worker count.
Reference target: Ryzen 7 3700X, RTX2070 SUPER, 32GB, 1080p/60fps, sustained 8x without growing debt (future 32–64x aspiration). No such integrated result is claimed. Historical aggregate environment CPU target 25ms/game-s, 512MiB steady, 768MiB autosave, 1GiB replacement, .5ms water GPU/frame and 32MiB water VRAM are comparison targets, not newly approved rigid subsystem allocations. Broad flood/edits, memory, CPU/GPU/frame, query and publication cost and save debt included. Report peak latency and complete work. Choose coarse connected storage and multirate scheduling consistent with actual transfer clocks, not just arbitrary reduced cadence or fine region caps.
6. One release in six implementation milestones
Proceed to the next milestone when the implemented output is usable and its directly relevant acceptance criteria are met. These are delivery milestones, not a separate exploratory research campaign. Reuse upstream checks and the same one connected world; no endless independent benchmark phase. If a hard failure occurs, record the smallest specific issue, fix the integration when bounded, or stop that component and reconsider the dependency.
M0 — Prepare and pin
Inspect actual worktree, build instructions, existing terrain API, scheduler, saves, branch status and unpublished changes. Create isolated reviewed implementation branch/worktree from appropriate code head and import canonical Brain decisions; don’t base runtime work on docs alone without checking differences. Freeze dependency manifest, source/license notices, units/clock, world seed and scenario/tolerance definitions. Runtime scope is authorized by the user on 26 November 2026; synchronize the active task and instructions into the actual implementation checkout. Don’t delete legacy data or overwrite another writer. Deliver reproducible build and start fresh-world policy.
M1 — One aged editable world
Integrate GeoGenesis core, selected PWG geometry/morphology and existing Zylann. Form macro geography, age at chosen years, export final original bed/material/climate/drainage (not filled diagnostic water stock), build feature-first channel/basin geometry, initialize finite stock later. Generate visible small valley with 1m tributary, curved river, lake, closed depression, mountains and editable land; test adjacent seams and matching hydraulic curves from same solids. Use real authored/generated geometry, not fixture-only solver. Deliver visible terrain, world age/density/shape configuration, finite geometry summaries and macro 4,000km count/bytes/startup census without full fine generation. If fine tributaries do not respect parent outlet, fix recipe before adding water.
M2 — Water replacement (highest priority)
Integrate upstream Wflow numerical routines, connected independently staged subgrid compartments, finite volume exchange; CFE native soil/runoff, finite Wflow-derived groundwater/springs and coastal/ocean inventory. Ordinary reach+flood storage first; use FluxCell only for needed rapid detailed patches and demonstrate conservative authority transfer and actual geometry/withdrawal updates. Do not port full Julia stack or rebuild old graph. Render real stage-clipped water, query depth/current cheaply, include dams/weirs and narrow channel controls. Meter rainfall as a temporary explicit forcing fixture, not production weather. Deliver playable filling, draining, extraction, rainfall/runoff, backwater, protected settlement, gate opening/reversal, wet excavation, caves and save/reload with offscreen progression. No double-stock, infinite source, ghost water across sealed barrier or widespread fine-grid requirement. If geometry/positivity/stability work turns Wflow into a new general-purpose solver, stop and reconsider regional dependency; do not hide it in adapters. If rapid-flow area exceeds FluxCell budget, record missing regional capability, don’t clamp away physically consequential floods.
M3 — Live coupled weather
Implement Weather3D reduced numerical core on CPU-compatible packed fields using established pressure backend, conservative MC/TVD fluxes, selected CliMA bulk phase and finite falling rain/snow, COARE-informed exchange and surface heat capacity. Generate actual wind/rain responses to topography, temperature, humidity, seasons and water; connect CFE/surface/GW, remove temporary rain driver from normal path. Cloud physics snapshot supplies base/top, condensate, types and movement. Require mass and simplified energy accounting of all physical exchanges and explicit boundary/solar energy, stable circulation with meaningful wet/dry and mountain rain-shadow behavior, no arbitrary rainfall source or doubled ET. Drought and rewetting must affect both sides. Provide field queries for gameplay independent of renderer. If the native reduced dynamics port becomes a rewrite or cannot maintain stability/physical finite coupling without large compute, return the specific blocker instead of adding a heavyweight atmosphere.
M4 — Erosion and visual world
Reuse GeoGenesis bed/hillslope/material methods where applicable and MeanderPy slow alluvial migration/cutoffs, driven by actual accumulated flow/shear, sediment, wind, rainfall and material/vegetation resistance; protected hard/engineered banks constrain movement. Separate fast stage/wetted width from slow physical bed/centerline changes. Apply bounded persistent solid edits and repair water/navigation; cutoffs retain finite stock and connectivity, not cosmetic curves. Integrate SunshineClouds2 real volumetric compositor: start quarter-linear resolution 480x270 at 1080p, 24–48 primary samples, low lighting sample count, early-out/empty-space skipping and depth-aware temporal reconstruction. Default stock settings not accepted. Shape driven by persistent meteorological formations, reuse 3D density shapes where supported, dynamic sunlight, beautiful open-sky gaps when weather permits. Do not build second weather simulator or fixed baked sun shading. Deliver attractive normal gameplay view below/above/inside clouds, moving sun/camera, storm, clean curved streams and changing water stage/terrain. Keep measured frame/VRAM costs, not screenshot-only pass.
M5 — Complete release evidence and scale
Use same environment implementation to run normal connected valley and 100x100km severe storm/recession, representative 256km region, and 4,000km macro with multiple simultaneous active regions and sparse terrain/solver residency. Do not equate idle macro load with a fully active world. Include offscreen edits, dams, dry/wet, finite snow/ice and heat, cave/ocean/groundwater exchange, representative gameplay depth/hazard/nav queries, paced save/reload and actual rendered host. Report accepted finite residuals, water levels/arrival/hazard/extent against simple analytical or existing fine reference, no false closed-barrier crossing. Choose gameplay-relevant error thresholds before work; historical 5cm/10%/IoU0.9 are proposed fixture starting tolerances not universal scientific accuracy or new accepted requirements. Record exact source/binary/config and inclusive CPU/GPU/RAM/debt/p95/p99/frame/latency, generation/age separately, actual visible captures. Prove no global scan or full fine promotion. Record actual success/failure and unresolved features; only promote validated capabilities and leave future scale/ECS/ecology/other-liquid work open. Prefer a smaller truthful functioning release with named open failures to falsely labeling 4,000km/8x production-ready.
7. Stop conditions and reporting
No competing full solver builds, blanket dependency upgrades, old water optimization, unapproved license, invented source implementation, or numerical redesign masquerading as integration. Preserve tests as ordinary development, not months of independent qualification. When a hard requirement fails, show exact source/fixture/profile, why reuse cannot solve it cheaply, and the smallest viable replacement/contract change; obtain approval if changing fundamental gameplay, clocks or dependency/license. Do not hide unresolved full hydraulic, pressure, rendering or population costs. No separate repeated paper search unless a concrete blocker. Commit bounded code+evidence on reviewable branch, update canonical Brain systems, candidate dispositions and traceability. Never edit generated website repo; run atlas generation/check/tests and publish through configured workflow. This plan makes actual technology choices provisional, not a claim of new performance or integration validation.
8. User-approved full replacement execution
The user approved the implementation-first design and all M1–M5 delivery work on 26 November 2026. The active work is full replacement, not an optional branch of the old environment system. Follow the execution protocol for orchestration, continuous progress and public Brain publication. No milestone requires another user permission unless it exposes a fundamental decision or real blocker. M0 is preparation, not a further research gate. Minimal targeted verification is required for the changed path only; do not reproduce comprehensive legacy compatibility or vendor validation. Preserve truthful status, hard physical invariants, representative scale evidence and repository safety. Remove or disconnect obsolete environmental paths where the replacement is ready, without deleting unrelated assets, saves or unpublished changes. Proposed tunable settings remain configurable; routine reversible engineering decisions are delegated. No measured performance or runtime implementation is established by this authorization.

formation-comparison.title: World formation comparison and remaining terrain scope
formation-comparison.content:
World formation comparison and remaining terrain scope
Source review: 25 November 2026. Both candidates MIT. Existing provisional GeoGenesis selection remains subject to comparison; recommend Procedural World Generation first in the surface-formation comparison because the user values the demonstrated geographic quality. Neither is validated on target hardware. No engine code modified.
Actual scope























































CapabilityGeoGenesisProcedural World GenerationSurface geographyTectonic relief, crust/isostasy, landform stamps and ageTectonic relief, staged landform passes, LEM and refined terrainGeological timePersistent coupled simulation, age in years, replayIterated uplift/incision/diffusion with time step in years; age-conditioned parameters, staged buildReliefPlateaus, mesas, ranges, rifts, faults, calderas, peaksTerraces, mesas, buttes, escarpments, coastal cliffs, sea stacks, volcanism, karst and glacial/coastal landformsGeology/materialsRock properties, strata, age, dip, fault offset, soil/sediment, mineral prospectivityErodibility, geological provinces, simplified strata/landform and biome layersDrainageD8/MFD, depression fill, climate-derived flow; needs finer realizationExplicit reach graph, lakes, meanders, deltas, local trunk/creek growth and CPU terrain detailOutputHeightfield, maps, 3D surface mesh, geology descriptorsHeightfield, typed-array fields, feature graphs, CDLOD surface and visual effectsTrue volumetric terrainNot suppliedNot suppliedLive finite gameplay hydrology/weatherNot suppliedNot suppliedNative integrationDependency-light Rust core, export/ABI adapter neededTypeScript numerical core and headless benchmark; export/native port of proven functions to qualify
GeoGenesis source: initial formation, age driver, geology, mineral scoring. PWG source: pipeline, LEM, age config, landforms, arid, cliffs, hydrology, creeks, creek tests.
Recommendation: compare whole formation outputs, not stack two full generators. PWG’s explicit landform diversity and local creek implementation may avoid significant custom engineering. GeoGenesis is better aligned with chronological coupled age and material inventories. A beautiful demo does not by itself establish native runtime speed, physically correct finite water, or 3D geology. PWG’s rendering and visual embellishment should not be mistaken for the physical terrain. If PWG wins, consider only needed compatible GeoGenesis rock/stratigraphy and geological-process kernels, not a second world owner. If GeoGenesis wins, borrow PWG’s targeted landform/creek/geometry routines rather than running PWG’s entire macro pipeline afterward.
Bounded selection gate

Run both pinned upstream generators headlessly using the same physical world width and comparable output resolution/land fraction/climate settings. Use a small reproducible seed set representing humid mountainous islands, dry plateau/canyon terrain and volcanic or glacial terrain. Seeds need not map to identical geography across different algorithms. Inspect final exported elevation, not renderer exaggeration, and measure cold macro generation, aging/evolution, refinement/export and peak working memory separately. GeoGenesis’s author timings are not a direct comparison; PWG has a source-inspected benchmark entry point.
Compare actual plateau/cliff profiles, river continuity, lake/outlet connectivity, relief variation, geology/material information, age controls and age-dependent changes. Freeze tolerances and visual evaluation views before testing. Report which landforms are process-driven vs explicit stamps; both are legitimate if coherent and configurable.
Test actual natural fine river/creek realization, including 1 m feature geometry where representable, cross-page continuity, closed basins, deterministic re-generation and no view-dependent physical geometry. Existing creek tests are useful starting evidence, not our validation. A fixed height callback and persistent parent routing/finite inventory contracts are mandatory.
Only after upstream evidence, compare native interop costs and one bounded Godot/Zylann view with true caves and materials. Select one source. Do not start a large port or new framework to make either candidate fit. Probe 4,000 km coarse scaling with no dense fine allocations. Distinguish failed/partial/accepted results.

Additional scope retained from the environmental plan
These items are not made unnecessary by selecting a formation engine. They remain required or explicitly phased in existing records.




























































DomainStill neededCanonical owner/requirementTrue 3D geologyCaves, overhangs, tunnels, coherent underground strata/materials, finite deposits; Zylann SDF and sparse editsQ-VOLUME, REQ-EDITSurface geometryStable channels/banks, lakes, basin capacity, dams, cross-page routing and local editsCON-TERRAIN, Q-REFINESoil and groundwaterActual infiltration, evapotranspiration, soil stores, aquifers, springs and cave exchanges; CFE remains provisional land kernelSYS-LAND, SYS-GW, OPT-CFEDynamic finite hydraulicsRivers/lakes/ocean, local controls, broad flood/recession, accepted volume transportREQ-WATER, REQ-FLOOD, Q-FLOODLiquidsBasic contamination and additional liquid families; sparse transport and meaningful effectsREQ-LIQUID, REQ-CONTAMWeatherWind/temperature/moisture circulation, actual evaporation, cloud transport and precipitation, seasonal forcing; ERF Kessler only a cloud donorQ-ATMOS, OPT-ERFLive erosion and sedimentActual runoff/discharge/wind/material activity causes later terrain evolution, including deposition and soil fertility; not wholesale regenerating an inhabited worldSYS-EROSION, CON-SEDIMENT, Q-EROSIONEcologyPersistent vegetation, succession, fauna, feedback to infiltration/ET/erosion, farming and resourcesREQ-ECOCurrents and visualsRiver velocities, wind-driven water currents, waves, atmosphere/cloud presentation, coherent material/foliage renderingSYS-CURRENTS, REQ-VISUALGameplay and scaleECS, hierarchical travel and crowd movement, offscreen work, mining, cultivation edits, common time/scheduling, save/reload and measurementsREQ-PEOPLE, REQ-NAV, REQ-FANTASY, REQ-PERSIST, REQ-BUDGET
Do not conflate deferred qualification with deleted requirements. The next experiment chooses a formation source and establishes its geometry handoff; subsequent finite water, weather, ecology and entity qualification remain unchanged.
User review: stream scale, landforms and geology
User finds PWG’s small-stream appearance unconvincing, particularly the 8 m cap, but values explicit landform/terracing algorithms and the absence of equivalent wind erosion and mineral deposit support is a concern. Source follow-up: the 8 m cap is only in small-stream geometry, not macro river sizing. River density and meandering controls exist; creek width/depth caps and several growth rules are hardcoded. At 4 km macro spacing the existing channel-head area floor is 40 km². The existing split is a rendering-oriented approximation; Breachborn needs one coherent feature hierarchy with configurable hydraulic geometry, catchment/mean or bankfull discharge, local slope/material and physical units. Do not infer live water volume from carved width. A fixed minimum or maximum is not a physical stream-order rule. Do not accept forced joins/cell-boundary artifacts or visual-only creek ribbons as physical topology.
Provisional engineering preference: retain GeoGenesis as the age/material baseline, qualify PWG’s strongest explicit terracing/landform and main-network/geometry kernels as targeted donors, and keep PWG full formation as the comparison challenger. This reflects the user’s newly expressed priorities and the source-confirmed richer geological process model. If PWG’s headless geometry, costs and coherent age/material adapter win the existing gate, choose PWG instead. Avoid both full formation pipelines in one world and avoid duplicating existing erosion. Prefer a single geology/terrain owner with optional generation-time landform processes and runtime forcing-driven material changes.
Add to the comparative acceptance gate: (1) creek/trunk/river scale continuity across macro spacing and density, natural morphology without inappropriate forced junctions, configurable widths/depths, and reference bankfull dimensions distinct from dynamic wetted dimensions; (2) bare versus vegetated/arid wind erosion, finite loose-material budget, downwind deposition and recorded dust/export; test physical scale and actual wind fields rather than accepting the donor’s cell-count transport; (3) reproducible rock strata and resource prospectivity, with finite local 3D mineable resource realization a separate Q-VOLUME gate; (4) cliffs/terraces/canyons rendered from the same final solid geometry as hydraulics and navigation, with natural drainage preserved after landform passes. See candidate records for exact pinned source evidence. No benchmark or user-approved final selection.
Coupled compatibility gate
Status: proposed gate, not passed. The current source review confirms extensible formation processes and useful surface geometry algorithms. No full live hydraulic, groundwater or atmosphere implementation has been qualified against either formation candidate.
