Keep the formation comparison open until the following interface and coupled checks have evidence:

































BoundaryRequired contract and discriminating checkFormation / added landformVersioned metric terrain/material recipe, stable deterministic feature identities; add a terrace/cliff, depression or crater; refresh drainage/outlets, geological properties and terrain summaries after mutation.Surface waterGeometry-derived connected storage partitions, stage-volume/area, bed/bank/saddle/face/control geometry, finite ocean/lake/river inventories, signed accepted fluxes. A natural river, two basins, barrier and dam edit show conserved transfer, correct spill, arrival and recession.Soil / groundwaterFinite soil/recharge/spring/underground exchanges and actual cave contacts; no duplicate groundwater store when using a conceptual land kernel.AtmosphereGeometry and surface properties mapped conservatively to the selected coarse atmospheric grid, wind/thermal gradients, vapor/cloud transport and precipitation. Compare mountain rain shadow, wet/dry land and ocean exchange; not a static climate map.Coupled live evolutionActual terrestrial evaporation removes water, credits vapor, transports it downwind, condenses and rains; rainfall partitions once to land/open water, runoff moves downstream and changes storage; erosion/deposition uses accepted forcing and commits geometry changes. Test water and material closure, causal timing and geometry changes.Scale / visualAll above remain meaningful offscreen and after save/reload/promotion. No whole-map fine terrain admission. Measure inclusive CPU/GPU/memory and debt with actual Godot presentation, 100 x 100 km severe storm, and 4,000 km logical-domain scale probes. Freeze error/performance criteria before tests.
The first gate is deliberately a small connected case, not full production integration or literal molecular/3D CFD. Independent solver resolution and cadence remain allowed if conservation, meaningful outcomes, feedback and local refinement are established. Additional liquid families, contamination, currents, ecology, seasonal/weather range and full scale still require subsequent qualification under existing requirements. If a shortlisted solver requires incompatible geometry or unbounded fine work, change that solver/representation before locking the stack; do not discard required water or weather behavior.

questions/q-atmos.title: Which lightweight atmosphere and transport?
questions/q-atmos.content:
Which lightweight atmosphere and transport?
Compare reduced atmosphere methods and permissive numerical donors. Demonstrate wind/thermal gradients, downwind moisture, condensation/rain, actual ET, seasons and large storm under budget. Verify cloud rendering consumes same fields and later snow/currents/vegetation interfaces.
Complementary pressure review
Weather3D reduced dynamics lead, CliMT and JCM independent physics, CliMA 0M finite phase adaptation, COARE bulk coupling. MC/TVD preferred over upwind-only in independent 720km tracer probe; dynamic atmosphere remains unqualified. True volumetric clouds mandatory per REQ-VISUAL. Review.
Implementation-first selection (26 November 2026)
Use reduced Weather3D hydrostatic/anelastic C-grid dynamics as primary donor, with compatible established pressure solver, conservative MC/TVD finite transports, CliMA bulk phase and COARE-derived exchanges. Environmental Foundation V1 records exact source pin and adaptation boundaries. No stock atmosphere or full validation claimed; this question stays open for implementation evidence. No new competing atmosphere campaigns.

questions/q-erosion.title: Which erosion methods can run during play?
questions/q-erosion.content:
Which erosion methods can run during play?
Compare stream-power/hillslope methods and suitable sediment accounting. Feed actual runoff/discharge, soil/material properties and vegetation; test erosion/deposition and terrain revision without erasing player construction or rebuilding entire map.
Formation/runtime forcing comparison (26 November 2026)
See GeoGenesis source correction and formation clarification. First verify the upstream implicit area-based and discharge-aware geological laws under wet/dry and varying-discharge controls, including threshold effects. A representative statistical climate/runoff forcing is appropriate for prehistory; live erosion must use actual accepted flows/erosive exposure and material resistance. Reuse established erosion/deposition implementations (GeoGenesis, Wflow sediment candidate where appropriate, Landlab as reference) rather than duplicate overlapping erosion laws. Validate sustained erosion/deposition, local sediment accounting, altered channels and dam/cave geometry, navigation revision and no removal of construction by whole-world regeneration. Scope each physical process and timescale separately.
Stylized dynamic channel migration (26 November 2026)
MeanderPy is a newly source-screened permissive kinematic channel-migration donor. Evaluate its curvature/upstream-weighted law and cutoff/centerline resampling before new implementation. Stock migration does not directly include flow velocity/discharge and is not a finite hydraulic or terrain/material solver; qualify modulation by actual accumulated flow/shear, material and vegetation resistance, coherent erosion/deposition and topology updates. Restrict to suitable alluvial reaches; canyon/bedrock channels should not wander unrealistically. Preserve construction and water custody during migration/cutoffs. No runtime adoption.

questions/q-flood.title: Which scalable hydraulic algorithm?
questions/q-flood.content:
Which scalable hydraulic algorithm?
Qualify signed head law, wet/dry, backwater, control/levee, downstream arrival, storage curves and dynamic geometry. Compare whole-island storm and two-basin/levee cases against finer reference with declared error and memory/throughput. No wholesale local refinement. Use historical SWMM/CaMa failures as negative evidence.
Numerical source screen
Landlab OverlandFlow is an independently implemented local-inertial raster reference. NOAA t-route diffusive routing exposes a C binding and cross-section preparation; the whole solver has module-global state. Neither qualifies as a turnkey sparse subgrid engine. Compare two practical coarse algorithms: a signed quasi-steady diffusive-wave head law using stage-dependent conductance versus a local-inertial face-discharge update retaining prior momentum. Use SFINCS/CaMa as algorithm references and independent fine Landlab controls. Start with one conservative stage-volume store per connected partition and explicit saddle/face geometry; both alternatives must handle closed barriers and exact accepted-volume debit/credit. Reject equilibrium-only flow for travel-time tests, unaccounted thin films/floors, or a requirement to promote an entire storm region to metre cells. See spatial qualification. This is a shortlist for tests, not a selected production solver.
Complementary pressure review
Compare mizuRoute IRF ordinary reach delayed flow, Wflow connected low-Froude and FluxCell rapid-flow reference. No old native reuse preference. Independent large-step oscillation despite perfect ledger and 250m storm time-cost probe in review.
Upstream-first replacement gate (26 November 2026)
The next comparison must execute existing upstream implementations before undertaking a new hydraulic port or implementation. Start with Wflow as the broad permissive candidate, SFINCS as independent mature subgrid reference, and FluxCell as rapid-flow candidate. Wflow documentation and floodplain limitations; 2026 SFINCS global flood validation (extent validation, not depth/game performance); FluxCell (MIT, CPU references and GPU implementation). Independently measure actual regional model and detailed solver using identical frozen geometries, inflows, physical clock, accuracy and inclusive cost criteria. Test narrow creeks, closed basins, dam/backwater/reversal, storm/recession, dynamic solid edits and transfers. mizuRoute only if separate ordinary reach routing earns its additional integration complexity. The old integration is negative evidence, not a required implementation baseline. No new solver is accepted by this record.
26 November upstream execution and regional rescreen
New evidence: bounded pinned FluxCell CPU analytical and gate/edit tests passed, but a full suite attempt timed out and GPU performance, mutable masks, withdrawals and multiscale coupling remain open. FluxCell is the provisional first detailed candidate, not the regional answer. Wflow’s actual same-stage storage code, negative-stock clipping and static network initialization mean a direct stock regional flood integration is not accepted. Retain Wflow for land-water evaluation. Add ADCIRC as a leading regional contender against SFINCS; test actual upstream before deciding whether either is usable, including license compatibility and mesh/lookup repair. Do not infer that subgrid or quasi-1D support resolves all scale, conservation or cave problems. Terrain-to-water export and clock selection are architecture gates, not follow-up polish.
Implementation-first selection (26 November 2026)
Use Wflow signed local-inertial and storage/profile numerical methods as primary ordinary regional implementation with independent connected compartments and finite donor transfers; FluxCell for genuinely necessary rapid details. Environmental Foundation V1 describes source reuse and implementation boundaries. Do not develop parallel regional backends. If required adaptation becomes a bespoke engine or fails a hard requirement, report the blocker. Regional solver remains unvalidated; this question stays open for implementation evidence.

questions/q-refine.title: How to refine aged geography?
questions/q-refine.content:
How to refine aged geography?
Smallest decisive experiment: age a coarse seed, generate adjacent fine regions and a shared creek/lake; compare drainage/outlet continuity, slope/section geometry, seam determinism, memory and startup. Inspect reusable hydrological terrain generation, graph/drainage algorithms and licenses. Tiled initial relief is not sufficient.
Narrowed research
Hydrological construction trees and procedural planet refinement are promising methods, not qualified licensed implementations. Tiled Priority-Flood addresses geometry reconciliation, not finite runtime water. flowing-terrain is a small permissive candidate with a closed-basin limitation. Neural Earth provides corroborating architecture, not a selected dependency. Test a constrained coarse/fine seam before committing to one method. See qualification plan.
Additional native donor screen
terrain-generator exposes a compact Apache-2.0 Rust/C interface and deterministic dense-map hydrology. Its bounded-map border-outlet policy, normalized heights, private flow functions and absent parent-boundary refinement prevent selection as an aged refinement engine. Investigate narrow geometry primitives only if they materially reduce new integration code.
Preferred source-screened geometry donor
Procedural World Generation is a promising MIT CPU routine donor for constrained channel and valley geometry from coarse fields. Qualify supplied-feature realization first. It cannot yet be called an aged geographic refinement engine because it does not guarantee new tributary/outlet topology; the remaining question is regional drainage construction and cross-window reconciliation. MAIForge has relevant pinned-outlet/window methods but AGPL and its own failed strict quality checks; reference only. Spatial architecture selection describes the bounded pilot.
Correction and comparative gate
Additional pinned source inspection located the deterministic per-cell trunk/creek generator and its tests within Procedural World Generation. It supplies an actual reusable topology lead, not only carving. It currently feeds visible river ribbons and samples a supplied rendered height callback, so the authoritative, camera-independent topology/bed and finite-store handoff still need qualification. See candidate record and formation comparison.
Small-stream quality gate
User review rejects assuming PWG’s current small-stream scale/shape is suitable. See PWG candidate for hardcoded 1–8 m creek limits, fixed per-cell growth and forced joins; main river widths have no corresponding 8 m maximum. Treat fine creek code as an optional donor only. Qualify natural coherent stream-to-river geometry, configurable continuous widths/depths, closed basins and cross-page connectivity against the same canonical surface and actual catchment. No visual-only terrain or mandatory arbitrary maximum channel width. Main network/landform algorithms may still be valuable independently.
Complementary pressure review
PyFlwDir accepts explicit outlets and geometry profiles; GeoGenesis seeded priority flood is alternative. Crop probe falsifies arbitrary boundary outlet (1m vs 5m true spill). Preserve parent crossing/spill constraints. Integrated review.
Stylized network direction (26 November 2026)
Prioritize selected meaningful channels rather than maximum stream density. Investigate climate/runoff/slope-conditioned channel initiation thresholds, drainage-area or stream-order pruning with conservative catchment aggregation, and PWG main-channel morphology. Keep metre-scale channels when selected, do not force tiny tributaries into every cell, preserve outlet/closed-basin identity and finite runoff after pruning. Separate curve control-point spacing from hydraulic segment spacing and voxel detail; preserve actual lengths, confluences, valley bounds and bed geometry. User requires good-looking curving channels, not perfectly reproduced dendritic geography. No fixed density selected.

questions/q-volume.title: How to generate coherent volumetric geology?
questions/q-volume.content:
How to generate coherent volumetric geology?
Separate procedural surface generation from volumetric detail. Zylann’s existing VoxelGeneratorGraph supports SDF composition and caves (documentation, generators). Use age/geology and material features to control cave topology, cliff overhangs, fractures and ore placement, not random unrelated noise everywhere. GeoGenesis stratigraphic/prospectivity outputs may be useful inputs, not proven 3D resource deposits. Investigate existing reusable volumetric generation examples/kernels and retain only relevant proven features. Test a connected cave and surface entrance, a true overhang, stratigraphic section and finite mineable deposit across neighboring blocks and restart; demonstrate that an edit changes both liquid storage/connectivity and navigation summaries without dense volume initialization. No implementation selected for these geological semantics. See formation comparison.

requirements/req-visual.title: Real visible and interactive world
requirements/req-visual.content:
Real visible and interactive world
Launch the normal Godot host, inspect actual terrain, streams, flooding, clouds and vegetation. Prioritize a useful playable baseline and actual interaction; distinguish cosmetic smoothing from authoritative physics. Preserve aesthetic direction from historical art as a reference, not a locked tiny scene scale.
User clarification, 25 November 2026
Clouds must be genuinely volumetric, pleasant realistic-stylized forms with recognizable shapes, soft shading, and clear gaps between individual formations when atmospheric conditions permit. The attached art reference was provided for aesthetic direction, not publication. Cheap raymarching is explicitly acceptable. Mesh/sprite-only representations do not satisfy the near/interactive cloud target; derived distant representations are permissible if visually consistent. Select the cheapest method that meets the appearance and performance requirements through measured Godot tests. No new fixed GPU allocation is accepted.
User clarification, 26 November 2026: stylized waterways
Prefer attractive, realistic-stylized river networks: visually meaningful tributaries rather than exhaustive natural drainage density, smooth curving main rivers, varied width and channel forms, and meaningful gradual shape changes influenced by flow/rainfall. Preserve small streams where useful, but do not require every minor runoff path to be an explicit permanent river. A stylized generated channel is still physical terrain and must agree with water and navigation. Visual and gameplay plausibility, rather than geophysical forecast precision, are the goal.

No decorative-only streams or unlimited replenishment. All donor/receiver transfers account for actual accepted amounts; ocean finite. Rain returns to water or soil once. Approximate reality, with fewer meaningful tributaries and attractive curving channels. Minor headwater runoff may be aggregated rather than modeled as an individual persistent channel; actual water, runoff, soil and groundwater exchanges remain conserved and offscreen consequences remain. The user did not waive finite water, rainfall response, meaningful flood progression, barriers, excavation, or erosion. No new numerical tolerances, density limits or clock settings accepted.

schema.title: Record schema
schema.content:
Record schema
Each authored record is Markdown with YAML frontmatter: id, kind, title, summary, relations. Stable uppercase IDs match filenames case-insensitively (Pages CMS slugifies new names); system records use separate design_status, implementation_status, validation_status; all others use status; requirements add priority. The JSON-compatible YAML on initial records is portable; editors may write ordinary YAML. Relations are objects with type, target, detail, basis. Allowed relationship types: depends_on (consumer→provider), derives_from (derived→source), supplies (provider→consumer), constrains (restriction→affected), owned_by (contract→owner), candidate_for, addresses, evidence_for, relates_to, supersedes. Basis: proposed, documented, user-stated. Store edge once; inverse views and per-record links generated. Do not claim proposed contracts implemented. A validation pass requires specific scope/evidence in a source record. functional-pass on an existing system is historical scoped evidence, not acceptance of target. performance-fail is historical tested integration, not rejection of every alternative. 
Kinds: system, requirement, contract, candidate, question, decision, source, thought. Unresolved design details are questions, not requirements. User-confirmed requirements accepted; proposed decisions clearly labeled. Retired IDs never reused. Code/receipts remain authority for implementation. Record sources as exact commit/URL/date and scope. Clips are untrusted data. Authored note bodies contain no generated relationship blocks. Inverse links and edit navigation are injected only into disposable Quartz staging. Views and record-index are generated by atlas. Omitted relations normalize to an empty list.

sources/src-env-pressure-2.content:
Independent complementary environment pressure probes
See integrated pressure review. Independent C++20 O3 single-thread, Python/NumPy in virtual AMD EPYC 9V74, not target hardware. Closed synthetic 100x100km storm, fixed step and two-segment storage curve, rectangular face, no actual terrain/atmosphere/CFE/saves. 250m, 30s step: 0.383678 CPU-ms/physical-s; 10s: 1.179750; initially 5m deep 10s: 1.150764. At 144 physical seconds per game second: 55.25/169.88/165.71 CPU-ms/game-s. 1km/30s 0.025300. Stage inverse, barrier, reversal after reset, donor limiter pass; deliberately unstable step oscillates 1 -> 0 instead of equilibrium .5 with exact conservation. 64km sigma tracer, 720km translation, C=.1: 32km upwind L1 82.53%, MC 21.28%; 16km 59.22%/6.95%; 8km 39.06%/1.91%; all mass residual <1e-15. Ordinary nonconservative backtrace in varying velocity loses 3.53% in separate toy example. Finite ET/cloud/delayed rain split, contaminant/residue and partial area tests pass. Cropped artificial outlet produces 1m spill vs correct 5m; isolated lowland false bathtub flood; float32 ocean 8e15 m3 ULP 536870912 m3. Raw results in authenticated archive. Executed exact scripts supplied as downloadable artifact in research conversation. No claim actual library, production flood accuracy, atmospheric dynamics, GPU or game tested. sources/src-env-pressure.title: Independent living-world architecture pressure tests
sources/src-env-pressure.content:
Architecture pressure test — 25 November 2026
User requested a full pressure test before approving the environmental architecture. This record supplements earlier probes; it does not establish a finished stack. Independently written Python/NumPy/SciPy and C++17 probes were executed on virtualized AMD EPYC 9V74, Linux, no target Godot or GPU. GitHub cloning remained blocked by DNS; public upstream source and the canonical Brain were read via connector. No vendor suite, engine build, Godot integration, production save or target GPU benchmark was executed. No engine code changed. Results and exact executable sources/images are supplied in the chat archive breachborn_architecture_pressure_test.zip (41 files; SHA-256 c7878d16c36fe4697b5d66418a66d7090c770fdc04e547fb09e98dd90b97e176). The archive is not checked into this repository; the numerical evidence and limitations are recorded here. Reference targets remain Ryzen 7 3700X, RTX 2070 SUPER, 32 GB, 8x rendered, historical 25 aggregate environment CPU-ms/game-s; 144 physical seconds/game-second is a sensitivity scenario, not accepted universal timing.
Storage, routing and groundwater
Independent analytical fixtures (breachborn_pressure_physics.py):

1km square, 1m wide 1km channel, 2m banks, 1500m3: true stage 1.5m, averaged-bed stage 1.9995m; true wetted area 1000m2 vs 1e6m2. Exact piecewise volume curve preserves shape; averaged terrain fails.
Two 1000m2 basins with 1m wall, 800m3 initially upstream: actual stages .8/0m; lumping yields .4/.4m. Add 500m3, simplified free weir C=1.7 width2m, 1s steps: downstream .1m at 242s, after 3600s stages 1.015824/.284176, residual -1.14e-12m3. Splitting a .6m water compartment then removing 200m3 from side A leaves .4/.6m, exact stock. This is a controlled geometry fixture, not a 2D dynamic inundation proof.
Linear diffusive-wave IRF reference (mizuRoute method): L=10km, c=2m/s, D=100m2/s, 600s 10m3/s pulse, bins20s. Mean transit5000s, SD500s. Reference peak4.558m3/s; pure delay 10m3/s, L1 114.23%; one gamma reservoir 1.131m3/s, L1 160.46%, early volume47.34% before3500s; 4/16/100 stages L1 127.54/79.61/2.105%. No early delivery via a closed dam; held packets need backwater resolution, not just gate check.
Compact shifted-gamma alternative matching mean/variance (breachborn_routing_groundwater.py), D=25/100/400/1600m2/s: shifted 16 stages at D100 delay3000s, L1 4.305%, peak+1.341%; 4 stages D100 L1 15.232%; 16 stages D25/D400 L1 4.567/2.413%; 4 stages D1600 L1 5.117%. This is mathematical screening, not a selected implementation or proof of runtime expense/physical nonlinear routing. Compare actual mizuRoute IRF/kinematic/MC methods; use bounded compressed response only where stage feedback negligible, own transit, refine on edits/high flow.
Two linear finite aquifers each storage derivative 1000m2 and conductance2m2/s, tau250s: exact at dt250s heads .68394/.31606m; explicit .5/.5, backward Euler .75/.25 (-20.9% transferred volume). At dt1000s donor-limited explicit exchanges all initial water, overshoots equilibrium; backward Euler still -18.5% transfer. Exact pair update is useful control; general spatial aquifer/stiff heterogeneous network unqualified. Stable or mass-conserving is not sufficiently accurate.

Native surface cost and critical extended failure
breachborn_pressure_bench.cpp: synthetic 100x100km regular grid, two faces/cell, variable beds and sparse crests, piecewise storage V(h), explicit local-inertia face update, donor limits, exact friction power vs lookup. No terrain scans, real curves, topology repair, local SWE, pollution, transfers or renderer. Median thread CPU five batches. Original illustrative dt=.5dx/sqrt(g2m) is NOT adequate for this subgrid geometry; near-dry small negative roundoff volumes reported. Original timings (pow/table ms/step; table normalized at alpha144): 1km .6268/.3824, .4878ms/game-s; 250m 10.7828/6.5535, 33.4407; 100m 53.4406/27.4966, 350.7687.
breachborn_water_table_check.cpp: 100x100 cells at 1km/250m, 500 steps per row (different physical durations with dt changes). At original dt max stage difference 1.264979m/2.104131m; end volume L1 fraction .001153/.92869; both conserve mass. At half dt max difference 1.485e-8/2.582e-8m; quarter and tenth dt also agree to tiny tolerances. This only checks consistency against the same simplified pow method, NOT physical correctness, convergence or sufficient CFL. Geometry/storage derivative and conveyance can make the naive wave-speed timestep unreliable; fix stability law and geometry consistency before benchmarking candidates. No reuse preference for this prototype.
Reduced-dt workload rerun (breachborn_water_reduced_dt_bench.cpp): 1km 10k cells dt56.44046s, .29835 CPU-ms/step -> .76120 CPU-ms/game-s; 250m 160k cells dt14.11011s, 4.49963 ->45.92075; 100m 1M cells dt5.64405s, 29.26409 ->746.63279. All costs are scoped synthetic CPU, not target benchmarks. Broad 250m or 100m fully active solver is not the default at historical alpha144. Test connectivity-aware variable-resolution storage with actual subgrid face geometry; SFINCS paper supports subgrid method, reports 35–50x on particular 100m vs25m applications but unresolved meanders overestimate flux, bins and fine preprocessing cost real. GPL reference only under current policy.
Rapid local water: FluxCell preprint (24 Nov 2026, not peer reviewed) reports 610–700M cell updates/s on integrated laptop GPU; actual project pin c62d8118839831529399b33815bac52a94738f55 MIT, CPU references and editable bed, fixed solid mask; no independently executed vendor code. Illustrative 256x256 1m patch at physical dt=.05s, 8x game speed: alpha1 needs10.486M updates/s, ideal nominal .2865 GPU-ms/frame at published lower rate and60FPS; alpha144 needs1.510B updates/s, 41.26ms/frame, impossible for a 60FPS budget on that throughput. Even 64x64 alpha144 nominal2.58ms/frame. This is arithmetic, not target timings; includes no GPU integration/copies or actual variable dt. Define physical-clock policy before selecting local simulation; no silent clock changes or camera-dependent flow.
Atmosphere and coupled fixture
Prior known-answer tracer: MC at16km retains95.27% broad sigma64km peak, only48.96% sigma12km. New idealized 256km ridge/transport experiment prescribed 2 layers, wind20m/s, uplift/saturation; 16km MC windward/lee rain21.524/4.933mm, 1km MC17.723/6.159mm; local intensity and distribution differ despite mass conservation. This is not dynamic weather.
Native synthetic atmosphere: four float fields, eight layers, varying signed divergence-free horizontal winds, split AVX2 MC transport, prescribed vertical mixing, saturation LUT, condensed and falling rain, surface actual water and latent/sensible exchanges, no pressure/dynamics or true air/land physics. Median combined per-step CPU on EPYC: 32km (125^2*8) 2.837ms at dt533.333s, .766 CPU-ms/game-s alpha144; 16km 9.175ms dt266.667s,4.955; 8km 33.713ms dt133.333s,36.411. Relative float mass residual max7.28e-8, simplified energy residual relative total max2.92e-8. No claim of physical thermal accuracy, pressure speed, timestep validity or engine overhead. 8km global unsuitable as default at scenario clock, 32/16km coarse candidates.
Independent manufactured horizontal pressure test (breachborn_pressure_circulation.py): scipy single-worker periodic constant 5-point Laplacian FFT at side125/250/500 median .1695/.5763/3.3069ms; heterogeneous positive open-area coefficient (minimum near .1) same simple solver relative residual .09468, preconditioned CG correction 19/20/20 iterations,7.942/27.607/138.133 CPU-ms, relative residual below1e-6. Python/scipy timings not optimized native pressure solver; not a true terrain-following 3D atmosphere. Illustrative explicit c=100m/s, dx16km, Courant .5 ->80s instead of266.7s; trapezoidal oscillator phase error -11.45% for wavelength128km at266.7s. c300m/s ->26.67s, -43.99% phase error for128km. No universal dt from wind alone; semi-implicit stability does not guarantee propagation accuracy. Prioritize reduced pressure/wind closure and parameterized uplift with actual causal weather tests; do not port Weather3D wholesale or assume diagnostic wind is sufficient. Compare dry/wet moist shallow-water, reduced hydrostatic and low-cost diagnostic variants; actual circulation remains unresolved.
Independent connected accounting fixture (breachborn_connected_fixture.py): eight 1000m horizontal columns of artificial area10000m2, prescribed two-layer wind/mixing and simplified heat balance, finite surface soil/aquifer and two 100m2 basins, gate opens43200s. Dry case produces no rain. Explicitly cooled humid case at dt20s: 1,006,476.176kg rain,397,331.051kg actual evaporation,1114.457m3 runoff,671,024.420kg recharge; no-evap control625,207.253kg rain (difference381,268.923kg). Protected basin remains dry, hazard crosses at43220s; dt10s crosses43210s and rain1,006,228.840kg (0.0246% difference), end basin stage .308156 vs .308076m. No negative stocks, water and simplified sensible/latent energy ledger close to roundoff with explicit external forcing. Raw pickle bytes differ after restart; canonical arrays/scalars digest exactly equal. Not game persistence, full thermodynamics, real circulation or forecast accuracy. Initial atmospheric water contributes to rain; not all rain is new evaporation. Preserve successful accounting boundary; no solver chosen.
Clouds
Executed standalone CPU real 3D density raymarch (breachborn_cloud_pressure.py, breachborn_cloud_sculpted.py), deliberately sculpted ellipsoid union plus surface detail, 96^3 quantized density/light, directional optical depth precompute, no nested light march, bounding volume and transmittance early-out. 640x360 96-step same-asset reference vs160x90 32-step bilinear upscale. Sculpted below:7,892,748 vs164,520 primary samples,47.97x, cloud-mask sRGB RMSE2.428/255; close18,874,912 vs394,715,47.82x, RMSE1.624; softer inside22,118,400 vs460,800,48x, RMSE .041. Static single smooth volume, mask reference transmittance<.98, no overlapping clouds, GPU, temporal reconstruction, actual terrain composition or art acceptance. Changed sun direction and stale baked lighting yields cloud-mask RMSE46.267/255 sculpted,25.355 softer. Reject fixed directional lighting for day/night. Candidate bounded true 3D density raymarch with live directional light approximation/directional caches, compare existing SunshineClouds2 (not validated), SDF skipping and temporal reconstruction; Nubis cubed method evidence, not performance guarantee. User reference art remains higher quality. Require below/above/inside, multiple formations, storm overcast, changing sun, camera/time motion, correct opaque geometry clipping and GPU timing on target. No CPU software-render time extrapolation to GPU.
Navigation and terrain
breachborn_hpa_pressure.cpp: independently authored HPA-style two-floor256x256 synthetic walk grids with 16x16 clusters, explicit stair portals, sampled entrances, exact local BFS and abstract A, intercluster door as dynamic link. 2912 abstract nodes,19344 directed edges,13.939ms build,243776B raw node-position/edge payload excludes mapping/scratch/capacity. 400 sampled paths: open grid A183.049ms vs hierarchical16.028ms (11.42x), mean stretch2.396%, p95 11.881%, max37.5%; closed214.382 vs15.402ms (13.92x), mean2.486%, same p95/max. No false blocked/false path in sampled cases, not universal reachability proof. Door fixture exact and abstract path8->138; no graph rebuild for this explicitly represented intercluster link. No actual path refinement, 3D terrain, crowd, library, capability-policy or 100k acceptance. Shared macro fields in separate benchmark: 250^2 unweighted graph, 500 fresh A87.524ms, 20 reverse fields6.348ms, 100k cached cost lookups .558ms; cache5,000,000B, 0 mismatches on500 sampled searches. Shared queries promising, lookup is not movement or per-agent planning. [HPA](webdocs.cs.ualberta.ca/~jonathan/publications/ai_publications/jogd.pdf) and DHPA/SHPA literature supports qualification; selective caches, no universal cached all-pairs. Door inside a local cluster requires explicit conditional link or local repair. Population/ECS remains unqualified.
Terrain: pinned GeoGenesis author benchmark 1024^2 generation1.82s, approximate .4s/10k-year step, 200 steps ~80s rough extrapolation; tiled4096^2 initial-only3.4–3.8s vs single shot37.5s/3.1GB, not proof of aged fine world. No actual GeoGenesis, PWG or Zylann upstream execution. Retain user terrain soft lock conditional on natural drainage, deterministic seams, latent channel topology, cave/door/structure geometry and offscreen edits without global fine sampling. A render-only generated tributary cannot participate in physical drainage before its connectivity is known. Preserve topology as a compact feature constraint, not as independent fine resident solver state.
Decision status and next qualification
Do not claim full compatibility or lock production implementations. Retain only design-level shared ownership, independent domain scales, user soft-locked terrain, hierarchical navigation direction and true volumetric clouds. Reject blanket fine grids, unqualified native water retention, single reservoir routing, average-elevation storage, global fine atmospheric grid, fixed cloud lighting, all-agent per-frame path search and arbitrary clock compression. Candidate gates:

Freeze common clock policy and response/travel semantics, actual target budgets and accuracy tolerances. At historical alpha144 local visible dynamics and even one detailed patch can exceed budget. Do not solve by silently slowing water or weather, or dropping elapsed time.
Qualify actual GeoGenesis/PWG/Zylann geometry and topology before large integration; compile/run pinned tools on target. Determine whole-world feature counts, curve bytes, dirty edits and conservative promotion/restriction.
Run independent upstream hydraulic CPU controls and target FluxCell GPU; low-Froude connected subgrid vs reference, dry-bed dam, broad storm, backwater, edited dam, coarse/fine seam flux/time/mass, physically meaningful stage/arrival plus inclusive costs; geometry-derived stable timestep. Avoid automatic 1km as accuracy choice.
Test reduced atmosphere with actual wind circulation, thermal feedback and terrain-driven rain, high/low pressure/frontal propagation, local storm footprint and offscreen refinement, independent reference. Include soil/groundwater, sediment, liquid families, cold phase and heat closure. Provisional reduced geometry and accounting probes support the test, not production.
Test actual volumetric Godot renderer and moving sun/camera against user art reference; include full GPU frame and VRAM. Prove native multi-layer route construction and dynamic edits with HPA-style local paths, shared destinations, real 1k/10k/100k mixed agents and ECS. No benchmark substitution.
Integrate bounded playable slice; then 100x100km storm, 4,000km macro and 800km route with increasing simultaneous active areas, save/reload, measured complete CPU/GPU/RAM/debt. If failure, stop at the discriminating issue; no new blanket framework.

Evidence source hashes: pressurephysics.py e222f832f8bff0f7b19d76f9c2b6d245e8ade8dcd38e91320104ac3decb8d38a; pressure_bench.cpp 1d76daaac9516cd8f95600881b5706ac412f2ff4f03d6405690dd576dc222869; pressure_circulation.py fabbe2e2764dad98349cd80d22e52498c4447b7edcc484dfa84d5a83c2984eea; connected_fixture.py 2dae8332272e418bef6d15dbc7667acec9c531284cb9bcf8bfd3a669e7044bdb; cloud_sculpted.py 92cdcc8ab1a0df2057a65092918467220f53a0cece7437f932ee26dc4c3233d6; hpa_pressure.cpp 0f423b99e1ee69bc57d64cea9e01d3e9aa8bf2a586786c5de6c4957bcdf3b9e0; water_table_check.cpp 147c983430172fbf26a400d7487b10963ed4fcc122009944fe732106b01bf42a; water_reduced_dt_bench.cpp 289e4c06a16e3e5098ef840e1e4da877c118cc6e801d532a4d410ec72e58cef8; routing_groundwater.py 8d412ce53132a946739a34d3699fd76905dc1426be67e39d3a26c29a281e154d. sources/src-env-probes.content:
Environmental numerical probes and revised efficiency shortlist
25 November 2026. The user was not satisfied with source-only technology selection and requested concrete calculations and true attractive volumetric clouds. These independently authored probes were executed in a Linux virtualized AMD EPYC 9V74 environment, not the target Ryzen 7 3700X / RTX 2070 SUPER. No Godot executable or target GPU was available; GitHub checkout was blocked by DNS in the execution container. The Python/NumPy and C++17 probe scripts and results were supplied separately in the research conversation; SHA-256 of Python: 9fb7f46ca22efaf721e485a6e61d0e6bc6b6352a780ae2224989fa30ec87ce47; C++: 67c1c4decf6bc7e5d323a97a1d0a2bc890adce8199c110abd3b631cb03edc5f5. No canonical engine code was executed or changed.
Existing negative evidence
Historical water/weather review: optimized Flood078 sealed-bank 256 km headless diagnostic advanced 3.254 seconds at 0.889x, 1,124 inclusive CPU-ms/game-second versus 25 target (44.96x). Reference 1,104. Native air 589 to 558 ms over interval, receiver settlement 332 to 352 ms, maximum full diagnostic service 782 to 797 ms. No successful full natural flood, wet edit, or rendered acceptance. Earlier CFE/CaMa 16,384-reach 512 km prototype: 4.59 CPU-ms/game-second but 190.11 ms maximum service and failed terrain boundary convergence. Earlier aggregation improved 66.015625 to 60.052083 CPU-ms/game-second with 7.33% local water/35.21 cm stage divergence. See prior migration archive outside public content. Reuse interfaces/semantics selectively, not failed architecture or unqualified numerical implementations.
Independent dam-break experiment
Frictionless one-dimensional 1,000 m channel, unit width, reservoir depth 1 m left of x=0, dry right, reflective boundaries beyond wave reach, g=9.81 m/s2; t=20 physical s. Local-inertial test omits advective momentum, uses max adjacent depth for staggered face depth and donor-limited explicit flux; HLL finite-volume comparison evolves depth and momentum with dry-bed wave-speed estimates. CFL coefficient 0.35. Neither is a copy or execution of Wflow/SFINCS/FluxCell/legacy code. Ritter exact depth in fan: (2sqrt(g h0)-x/t)^2/(9g). At 1 cm depth, analytic front 106.4911 m. Report cell-center threshold front, and L1 depth integral divided by h0 sqrt(g h0) t; not a standard relative domain RMSE.

Conservation is necessary, not adequate accuracy. Local-inertia failure here is expected for an extreme dry-bed dam break, not proof against low-Froude use or all production implementations. de Almeida and Bates, 2013 reports slower unsteady wave propagation and generally good agreement at Fr below 0.5 in tested flows. SFINCS subgrid paper 2025 reports 35–50x speed at 100 m subgrid vs comparable 25 m regular configurations; 500 m hurricane application lost skill, coarse unresolved meanders overestimated flux. Not evidence for a universal 1 km mesh.
Tracer experiment and native transport cost
4,000 km periodic 1D domain; 384 km translation at 20 m/s; Courant 0.5; Gaussian cell averages with 16-point quadrature, center 1,600 km, exact translated initial profile. Compare conservative first-order upwind and MUSCL-style MC-limited flux (minmod of 2 left/right differences and centered difference). Relative L1 normalized by exact scalar integral. Total mass residual at most 4.73e-16 for all tested schemes, nonnegative. Results:

Synthetic native CPU probe: four float passive fields, eight vertical layers, horizontal dimension-split passes with fixed positive Courant values 0.3 and 0.2; contiguous array layout, ping-pong, no dynamic wind, pressure, vertical flow, phase changes, synchronization, coupling, saves or rendering. g++ -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 -std=c++17; explicit AVX2 finite-input MC stencil (no fast-math), branchy build -DBRANCHY. Median thread CPU time from five batches after warmup, 8 steps/batch for 125/250 sides and 3 for 500. Latest run:

Upwind column from AVX2 build. Maximum relative scalar sum residual across latest runs 4.18e-8; finite input only, not complete numerical validation. At hypothetical combined horizontal wind 30 m/s, C=0.5, dx=16 km, step 266.67 physical s; applying illustrative historical alpha=144 physical seconds per game second yields 1.49 CPU-ms/game-second for four-scalar AVX2 transport only. At 8 km this becomes 10.73 ms. Alpha is not automatically an accepted atmosphere clock; vertical motion/pressure may force shorter steps. A broad field can be cheap and accurate at 16 km, small storms cannot be justified at that grid from this evidence. Conservative semi-Lagrangian split remapping (UK Met Office SLICE) is an alternative to investigate if explicit stability/dispersion limits dominate. Do not select Weather3D wholesale; historical source review found global mass rescaling and nonfinite evaporation. Moist shallow-water models are a useful reduced-dynamics reference, not independently qualified circulation. Benchmark diagnostic terrain/thermal wind versus reduced prognostic circulation with real evaporation, cloud/rain and heat feedback.
Detailed water and geometry
FluxCell pin c62d8118839831529399b33815bac52a94738f55, MIT code (license; data separately licensed), API, verification. Preprint 24 Nov 2026 reports 610–700M cell updates/s on an integrated laptop GPU for fused second-order MUSCL-Hancock/HLLC. Upstream author measurement, not independently reproduced, preprint not peer reviewed. CPU reference available; mutable bed keeps water depth, solid mask fixed, batch readbacks and ownership require qualification. Do not import full global grid or confuse CFL update throughput with simulated time. Clawpack BSD Riemann kernels/reference remain alternatives. mizuRoute IRF/Lagrangian kinematic/diffusive methods (documentation) motivate cheap ordinary downstream routing, not universal backwater or mutable topology. Verify license and source pin before code reuse. Prior Wflow/SFINCS references remain valid for low-Froude subgrid geometry; no preferred old native flux implementation.
At historical alpha=144, hypothetical 100x100 km region, h=2 m, gravity-wave C=0.5 and two faces/cell: 250 m requires ~1.63M face updates/game-s, 1 km ~25.5k (64x less). An illustrative 8 CPU-ms/game-s surface budget allows ~4.9 vs 314 ns/face; actual stability, graph structure and memory change this. Scaling historical reach density 102,321/512^2 km2 across 4,000^2 km2 gives ~6.245M reaches, ~381 MiB at 64B/reach before links/curves, not a required density. Use catchment-scale summaries with finite water and geometry-consistent narrow streams, admit consequential details independent of camera. Do not generate all fine terrain to derive geometry. Geometry/accuracy remains an unresolved risk.
True volumetric clouds
SunshineClouds2, MIT, source-inspected Godot compositor. Supports 3D noise textures, painted mask, depth-aware reduced resolution, temporal reprojection, point effectors, directional lights; current Godot project advertises 4.5 Forward+. Its defaults 300 ray steps, 32 lighting max, half resolution; nested light loops and point-effector loop in density sampling make stock configuration unsuitable to assume cheap. Global floor/ceiling and noise/mask structure do not establish independently shaped vertical formations. Godot-Cloud-Worlds, MIT, source-inspected pre-baked SDF skipping and single light-march per pixel, but stochastic density mask and transparency/shadow limitations. Clayjohn sky demo v2 spreads hemisphere updates over 64 frames; useful distant sky concept, not local fly-through solution. Guerrilla Nubis Evolved reports under 2 ms PS4 sky clouds and Nubis Cubed describes voxel density, SDF skipping and cached lighting; commercial engine performance not transferable.
Preferred first render comparison: real bounded 3D density raymarch with pre-generated reusable shaped volumes, projected tile bounds/scene depth, quarter linear resolution (480x270 at 1080p), 24–48 primary steps, cheap single scattering/precomputed approximate optical depth or 1–2 shadow samples, early termination, depth-aware temporal reconstruction and history rejection on motion. Compare configured Sunshine addon to narrow bounded density renderer and pre-baked SDF approach. True volumetric near, distant sky representations optional. No expensive simulation or random noise as shape authority. At 32 primary steps quarter resolution all-screen ceiling 4.147M samples vs full HD 64 steps 132.71M, 32x fewer; 25% projected covered rays 1.037M if actually culled, not guaranteed. Eight 128^3 R8 volumes consume 16 MiB excluding mipmaps and cache/light data. No GPU timing or art quality validation performed. Proposed normal cloud target <=1 ms and adverse <=2 ms at reference 1080p only for experiment; not approved budget. Measure below/inside/above, sunrise/night, overcast, storm, fast time, camera movement, scene-depth compositing and shadows. Do not adopt a second heavyweight weather simulator for rendering.
Status
This is a falsification and screening record, not a new technology lock. No complete hydraulic, atmospheric, cloud-rendering or ECS benchmark ran. Require existing independent solver known answers, coherent terrain/storage and edit gate, measured end-to-end CPU/GPU/RAM including rebuilds/copies, and connected visual slice. Canonical terrain soft-lock remains provisional; user has not approved the rest.
Connections

→ Outgoing evidence_for DEC-ENV-STACK · Integrated living-world foundation selection: Reopen unqualified selections after user review. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for Q-FLOOD · Which scalable hydraulic algorithm?: Independent dam-break test and upstream solver screen. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for Q-ATMOS · Which lightweight atmosphere and transport?: Independent tracer accuracy and synthetic throughput. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for REQ-VISUAL · Real visible and interactive world: True volumetric cloud implementation candidates. (documented)

sources/src-env-v1-m1.title: V1 aged terrain integration evidence
sources/src-env-v1-m1.content:
First terrain integration, 26 November 2026
Implementation commit 1b83f78f. Built the unchanged GeoGenesis MIT core aa898282cbdd with pinned Rust 1.82.0 and called its formation, age and final geology/climate/D8 routing functions. A versioned immutable native archive supplies the original bed to the Zylann generator and retains geological and climate fields for downstream consumers. It carries depression-filled elevation and annual discharge as diagnostics. Zylann retains current voxels and applies edits.
The fixed parcel is 64×48 km with 1 km macro samples and seed 713. Four 10,000-year steps changed all 3,072 bed cells by more than 0.01 m with zero reported numerical repairs. Two exports produced the same 234,808-byte archive. Birth, age and final refresh took 9.94 and 10.17 ms together. Including serialization and file synchronization, exports took 67.39 and 75.79 ms. Thirty-three cells had more than 0.01 m of potential depression fill. The corrected native reader accepted the upstream three-class river mask.
Display-backed Godot 4.5.1 and the pinned patched Zylann extension ran on an RTX 2070 SUPER with the OpenGL renderer. In the checked cell, original bed was 634.399 m and filled diagnostic elevation was 677.239 m. LOD0, LOD2 and the streamed current voxel agreed within the preset 0.02 m SDF tolerance. Editing the voxel changed its SDF from −2.396 to +1.999 m while the immutable source remained −2.399 m. The 452 ms local streaming interval reported 3,935 generator calls and 326 mesh blocks. The captured frame showed a plain coarse surface with visible creases. The guarded build and display run completed in 19.78 s and 5.83 s respectively.
Verification covers this parcel and an in-session edit in the terrain inspection scene. Geological textures and fine geometry, PWG river realization, cold save continuation, default gameplay adoption and live scale remain open.
Offline 4,000 km macro census
The same pinned exporter and seed 713 formed a 4,000×4,000 km bounded world on 1,000×1,000 samples at 4 km. Birth took 1.384 s, four age steps totaling 40,000 years took 0.950 s, final geology/climate/drainage refresh took 0.252 s and export took 0.879 s. Total inside the exporter was 3.465 s. The guard reported 349,958,144 bytes peak job memory. The macro recipe was 76,001,336 bytes with SHA-256 21ccda8e33eb7abb4a7e1c8bc58ea74f5ded10decc0a9de290e75e43191edda5. It had 929,284 bed changes over 0.01 m, 101,725 cells with more than 0.01 m of potential depression fill and zero reported numerical repairs.
This run generated coarse formation data. It leaves world admission, fine streaming, connected simulation, multiple active regions and severe storm performance for the integrated checks.
Shared channel and basin geometry
Implementation 0c4fa5dd applies selected PWG meander, channel width/depth and carve-profile methods from f7b1daa7. The native terrain recipe carries stable reach and junction identities and distinguishes marine edge-connected areas, below-datum inland bodies and priority-flood depressions. Channel sections are sampled from the same carved bed that Zylann generates. Unresolved channel contacts remain explicit.
The same seed and parcel produced 69 reaches, including 56 with linked downstream reaches and 10 unresolved contacts. It found five marine areas, three below-datum inland bodies and nine priority-flood depressions. A curved example measured 1,414.214 m on its straight axis and 1,431.403 m along the feature. The linked 1.000 m tributary had a sampled wet section of 0.08475 m² at its measured crest. The shared section and candidate spill location agreed with the final native sampler within 0.000001 m. One depression’s macro capacity was approximately 52.15 million m³ at its sampled candidate crest. The value describes geometry, with the final outlet and finite storage still to be established.
The isolated live preview completed in 5.88 s on the same RTX 2070 SUPER. The local stream interval was 143 ms with 4,402 generator calls and 280 mesh blocks. The capture shows the curved dry channel in actual meshed terrain. Material mapping, restart, connected basin exchange, geometry at larger scales and normal gameplay admission remain open.
Material, current voxels and independent reopen
Commit 419370d7 adds a bounded V1 terrain session through RegionWorld and the existing Zylann SQLite terrain stream. The V1 world manifest identifies the immutable recipe, generator geometry and material versions. The native generator fills the SDF and Mixel4 channels with palette IDs derived from the GeoGenesis soil, sediment and rock fields.
The guarded build completed in 22.38 s. The display-backed writer and separate headless cold reader completed in 8.76 s together. The writer streamed 200 mesh blocks and observed 1,358 generator callbacks. The local stream took 1.933 s. All 1,536 checked plugin samples matched native material and weight queries, including 960 solid igneous samples and 12 solid soil samples. A mine edit changed the current SDF from −2.045 to +0.183 m. The base recipe value was −2.057 m, within the prior quantization tolerance. The verified one-block write took 97.268 ms. A new process started with the save path alone and recovered the exact combined SDF and material channel digest and identical recipe, generator and world identities. Local stream on the cold reader took 132 ms.
The same run checked a generated 1.029 m marine mouth with 34 centerline samples. Its highest sampled receiving floor was 19.450 m against a marine datum of 38.042 m. Two previously unresolved contacts gained bounded surveyed geometry and eight remain pending. The capture shows a dry carved channel with distinct material tones. Broader geological visual quality, fully surveyed lake outlets, integrated water and normal fresh-world adoption remain open. All timings are from this terrain fixture.
Formation from the running V1 session
Commit 43bce84e launches the packaged GeoGenesis exporter using formation settings supplied to the V1 Godot session. A new scratch target isolates the bake. World admission uses the existing persistent recipe and Zylann identity checks. It refuses an existing world target.
Guarded birth001 used native build040. Godot produced the same seed-713 recipe digest as the native control, from 64 by 48 cells of 1 km aged to 40,000 years. Bake-through-admission elapsed was 1.301 s. The mixed-phase weather render and headless reopen reached the same saved and continued checksums. At 1080p the renderer p95 was 1.096 ms over 62 dispatch-to-composite samples in this run. The guarded process tree took 23.03 s and peaked at 1,253 MiB. This is runtime formation for the connected V1 session. The separate colony entry and larger production resource case remain open.
Wider terrain and sparse active regions
Commit 51081a5b exposes formation dimensions in the connected V1 preview. Guarded build042 and region256a used a fresh 256 × 256 km world at 1 km spacing. A 30-column weather crop ran from daylight through dusk for 3,600 seconds. The distinct Godot process reproduced the continued state. The local storm delivered 37.79 L into the connected CFE footprint. Recipe bytes were 4,982,072, fresh Godot formation and admission took 1.061 s, and the guard took 11.50 s with 153.6 MiB peak job memory.
Guarded macro004 used 250 × 250 cells at 16 km spacing. The 4,000 km rectangle opened from a 4,751,336-byte recipe and initialized 1,438 coarse stores and 494 links. Two read leases 5,264 km apart matched the generated SDF and kept their local water routes open simultaneously. Their receivers gained 15.162 and 75.741 m³ during the same 20-second accepted interval. The two terrain demands caused 2,468 generated blocks, with 29,584 resident data blocks and 356 mesh blocks reported at the snapshot. The guard took 7.30 s and peaked at 213.4 MiB. The macro case used two active coarse water neighborhoods without regional weather or actors and wrote a combined terrain-water save.
Colony clock and selected save
Commit b73b85aa admits the V1 world through the ordinary colony scene. Its existing RegionWorld remains the terrain owner. V1 cold startup uses the selected recipe and current terrain for sixteen natural embark poses and ordinary native depot creation. The cycle services water and weather at ten-second physical boundaries of completed gameplay time. The native selected checkpoint binds the V1 payload, recipe identity and clock to the actor, terrain and resource cohort. Saved V1 terrain routes back through the same environment without a launch opt-in. Slot packaging copies the immutable recipe.
Guarded colony004 ran Godot 4.5.1 with the installed gameplay binding, build046’s V1 extension, a 1,000 km square generated world and one 25-column mixed-phase crop. At requested 8×, the fresh eight-second runtime window reached tick 640 and 64 simulated seconds. It saved 60 accepted physical environment seconds in checkpoint 3. The separate process restored checkpoint 3 without the fresh opt-in and advanced to tick 1,280, 128 simulated seconds and 120 accepted environment seconds in another eight-second window. Both reports accounted for the remainder to the next ten-second boundary. The complete guard took 37.41 s and peaked at 1,139.5 MiB. Item conservation and the native save verified. No separate water checkpoint file was created.
The 1,000 km square fits the retained native binding while it is in use. The smaller 64 km trial reached terrain admission and its bound gameplay build refused that domain size. The exact gameplay source rebuild stopped at an existing incomplete native manifest. The accepted run leaves that build issue, production defaults, normal rendered V1 weather and sustained scale open.
Packaged fresh default and displayed colony
Commit 388ebe65 packages the pinned V1 exporter and Windows extension from a verified build receipt. The ordinary colony entry selects V1 for fresh starts with this addon. Persisted worlds dispatch by their terrain identity. The V1 colony uses the shared terrain material and a surface starting view. The normal speed control now offers 8× and reports the native request. The legacy plane and weather display do not run in the V1 scene.
Guarded build046 and colony006 used the ordinary Godot 4.5.1 entry at 1920 × 1080, Vulkan Forward+ and RTX 2070 Super. The fresh launch supplied no V1 selection flag. Sixteen actors and a 25-column mixed atmosphere advanced 64 gameplay seconds and 60 accepted physical environment seconds over the 8.004 s trial. The display had 338 measured frames with 16.879 ms p95 and 19.757 ms p99. The colony displayed terrain and 200 resident mesh blocks. The snapshot shows the native 8× request. The whole guard took 29.78 s and peaked at 1,911 MiB. Separate headless Godot reopened the paired save and reached a second accepted weather boundary. The earlier colony005b had a functional clock and save, but the cutaway obscured terrain and its host-only speed override displayed the wrong request. The accepted build corrected both.
This verifies the staged Windows bundle and a short connected displayed trial. The package leaves sustained 60 FPS, normal volumetric weather and water views, exact modern gameplay build recovery and larger coupled workloads open.
Connections

→ Outgoing evidence_for SYS-AGE · Geological aging: Pinned upstream aging and original-bed export executed for one deterministic parcel. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for SYS-WORLD · World formation: Bounded macro formation and native recipe loading demonstrated. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for SYS-TERRAIN · Editable volumetric terrain: Zylann streamed and edited terrain from the native V1 recipe. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for REQ-AGE · Natural configurable geological aging: 40,000 modeled years and observed bed changes on the first parcel. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for REQ-EDIT · Interactive volumetric world: A current voxel edit and exact cold continuation passed in the V1 terrain session. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for SYS-REFINE · Geographic refinement and drainage: Shared carved voxel bed and sampled hydraulic geometry were verified in the small parcel. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for REQ-SCALE · Large configurable worlds and metre interactions: Offline 4,000 km formation ran at 4 km spacing. Integrated scale is open. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for SYS-PERSIST · Persistence and identity: Independent reopen verified a V1 terrain edit and its source identity. (documented)
→ Outgoing evidence_for REQ-PERSIST · Fresh coherent save and reload: Exact cold continuation checked for terrain SDF and material channels only. (documented)

sources/src-env-v1-m2.title: V1 finite water implementation evidence
sources/src-env-v1-m2.content:
First finite surface water integration
Commit 1bfb9f8c ports the signed local-inertial momentum and friction calculation, stage/storage interpolation and depth/length timestep bound from Wflow c617a12e. It prepares independent stores and crest-clipped face profiles from the V1 terrain recipe. The transfer adapter uses simultaneous finite donor and receiver budgets to move water volume, heat, solute and suspended mass. It reports out-of-regime requests before accepting that substep.
The generated seed-713 parcel provided 82 finite stores and 58 prepared links. A sealed gate passed with zero transfer. Opening the same link moved 0.637189 m³ in 20 physical seconds, with signed flow +0.031859 m³/s at Froude 0.02943. A separate native reverse case reached −0.025317 m³/s. The transfer carried 765.14 MJ, 0.127438 kg solute and 0.031859 kg suspended mass. The finite withdrawal and water, heat and constituent ledger checks passed. The surveyed steep marine link reached proposed Froude 31.986, returning a rapid-flow request with 0 s accepted and unchanged inventories.
The guarded build completed in 25.43 s. The matching native and Godot inspection run completed in 7.70 s with about 296 MiB peak job memory. The display reproduces the native ordinary-flow result and shows a diagnostic stage-clipped ribbon between rendered Zylann banks. These elapsed times include setup and do not establish steady simulation or GPU cost.
The pilot uses prismatic channel storage through bank crest and scans its local prepared graph each step. Edges begin closed for deliberate opening in the fixture. Above-bank routing, rapid-flow ownership, soil and groundwater coupling, normal control policy, save continuation and scale remain open.
Finite runoff and groundwater
Commit d4cb5f9d calls the pinned CFE Schaake infiltration, actual ET, soil outlet, GIUH and Nash C routines through a checked source-file lock. The Windows build adapts the original GCC scalar statements and makes Nash scratch local per call. CFE exports recharge for a finite Wflow-derived unconfined aquifer that supplies and receives water through signed river contacts. The surface, soil, delayed queues and groundwater balance at the common accepted interval.
The native check and a separate headless Godot session used the same generated pair and two declared 400 m² land patches. Measured rain input was 26 m³. It remained pending after a 60 s accepted surface slice. By the first 1,800 s land interval, the code recorded 0.400 m³ actual ET, 2.902 m³ infiltration, 1.362 m³ surface runoff, 1.727 m³ recharge, 0.115 m³ spring release, 0.062 m³ reverse river seepage and 0.00106 m³ lateral groundwater flow. The GIUH delay held 21.337 m³.
At full surface capacity the land owner retained 11.558 m³ of delayed runoff. Releasing a metered finite extraction allowed further delivery. At 5,400 s accepted time, 19.294 m³ cumulative runoff had reached the surface, 4.769 m³ cumulative recharge had reached groundwater and actual ET was 1.200 m³. Native and Godot results matched. Volume, heat, solute and suspended mass passed the 0.000000001 relative balance tolerance. The build took 26.15 s and the coupled check took 4.58 s end to end.
The fixture establishes two calibrated sites, signed groundwater-to-stream coupling and delayed runoff acceptance. Regional soil maps, cave contacts, actual atmosphere, broad groundwater or flood performance and cold continuation of water quantities remain open.
Bounded rapid flow and custody
Commit fd08bba7 ports the pinned MIT FluxCell CPU MUSCL-Hancock/HLLC kernel at c62d8118839831529399b33815bac52a94738f55. The 24 × 48 patch uses one-metre cells, wall boundaries and the seed-713 generated bed. The parent releases 36 m³ into the patch and refuses concurrent additions, extractions and opening of its coarse gates. A one-substep request reports the unaccepted time. A sealed row passed zero water for two physical seconds. Opening four cells moved 2.976 m³ downstream in six more seconds. Reconciliation returned 36 m³, 43.229 GJ of sensible heat relative to 0 K, 7.20 kg dissolved mass and 1.80 kg suspended mass to the parent and retired the patch.
The first reference comparison found as much as 0.333 m of depth deviation after opening. The native port had used bed slope where FluxCell uses free-surface slope after subtracting the face pressures. With that correction, comparisons at the first step, sealed endpoint and opened endpoint passed. The maximum absolute discrepancies were 1.12 × 10⁻¹⁶ m in depth and 1.81 × 10⁻¹⁶ m²/s in momentum per unit width. The corrected case ran 165 native steps in 73.5 ms of wall time. The linked pilot, pinned Node.js reference, generated terrain and display-backed Godot run completed in 8.75 s with 311 MiB peak guard job memory. Godot matched native arrival, returned stocks and accepted time and captured its depth grid and opened diagnostic gate. The capture has incomplete surrounding terrain coverage.
This control uses a whole-parcel transfer with all parent links sealed during fine custody. The gate is a pilot solid mask over generated elevations. Independent overlapping patches, finite boundary exchange with moving coarse reaches, repair from edited voxel geometry, rapid patch persistence and GPU throughput remain open.
Above-bank and lateral floodplain exchange
Commit 42abc99f derives a 24 × 24 m survey from the seed-713 geometry. The patch has nine independent 8 × 8 m compartments. Equal-area floor samples define monotone storage knots. Sampled shared faces define bank and lateral crests and the wet area and perimeter entering the existing Wflow local-inertial update. The in-bank channel curve is preserved and extended over the same channel footprint. The surveyed patch excludes other channel and basin footprints.
The 2,765.581 m³ finite seed stayed in its channel while the bank was sealed. After four physical seconds with the bank open, the first compartment held 11.209 m³. Its lateral neighbor stayed dry while the connecting gate was sealed and received 0.0198 m³ by 4.5 s of total accepted time after the gate opened. Channel and overbank stages stayed distinct. Native and headless Godot balances matched for volume, sensible heat, solute and suspended mass. The guarded run took 5.89 s with 132 MiB peak job memory.
This fixture uses one surveyed bank corridor and a prescribed 0.125 s step. It does not establish large-area flooding, flow through edited barriers, general automatic floodplain placement, rapid overbank behavior or broad recession. The next checkpoint adds cold persistence and checks continued flow from restored state.
Cold finite water and current voxel continuation
Commit ddb8650f adds a checked versioned record for surface inventory, signed face state and accepted time. It also records CFE soil, GIUH and Nash queues, pending rain, evapotranspiration demand, finite aquifer stock, transfer outboxes and interval phase. The V1 session pairs it with the verified current terrain database and world identity under the same directory writer lease. A pending save marker or an outstanding database journal prevents cold admission.
The native control re-encoded the restored state byte for byte, rejected truncation and repeated the pending runoff release. Godot saved at 3,600 physical seconds with 11.558 m³ retained. The fresh process read the saved recipe without an external recipe input. It restored the water bytes and exact current SDF and material channels from a four-block mine edit away from the surveyed hydrology. The same 20 m³ withdrawal and further water interval reached 5,400 s with the same continuation bytes. The reopened owner successfully published a second checkpoint. The guarded run took 5.93 s and peaked at 134 MiB of job memory. The final water file was 6,672 bytes.
This check uses a bounded generated reach pair and a remote voxel edit. Hydraulic geometry repair from edited voxels, an active rapid patch in the save, recovery of an interrupted cross-file transaction, comparable wide-area checkpoint costs and whole-game saves remain open.
Edited lateral flood face
Commit e991052f uses current RegionWorld read leases to repair sampled lateral face profiles. A Zylann fill edit crosses a surveyed compartment face. The surface owner detects the revision, declines time without changing stock and refuses save publication. Godot bilinearly interpolates the horizontal SDF samples and locates the upper solid-to-air crossing for each point. Accepted repair rebuilds the Wflow face curve, clears stale face momentum and leaves finite stock in its existing owners.
The open diagnostic face rose from 1,927.656 m to a 1,930.500 m crest and passed zero water. The original voxel channels were restored with the terrain writer’s exact rollback receipt. The measured current crest returned to 1,927.657 m and passed 0.00424 m³ on the next 0.125 s step. Volume, heat, solute and suspended mass remained balanced. The rebuilt profile round-tripped through the versioned water codec, and the combined terrain and water checkpoint verified. The guarded run took 5.88 s with 134 MiB peak job memory.
This repair covers the represented lateral profiles. It does not resurvey the compartment storage curves or infer cave connectivity from the upper surface. Bank, channel, basin and rapid-patch geometry repair remain separate work.
Current-voxel wet flood storage
Commit 8eb1c621 uses the existing 16 equal-area floor samples per represented flood cell and the bank and lateral cross-sections. An intersecting edit invalidates affected surveys. Before replacing curves, a current lease must complete the revision batch and establish that each stored parcel still fits. Time and checkpoints withhold publication while geometry is pending.
Guarded build036 and wetgeom002 kept the native flood arrival control and the prior temporary barrier test. A second live terrain edit excavated a wet cell. The minimum sampled bed dropped from 1927.6615 m to 1924.5000 m and stage from 1927.7061 m to 1924.6265 m. The same cell retained 2.024027 m³ and its original heat, solute and suspended stock. Independent Godot re-open matched the edited capacity and the checkpoint and next state bytes. The observed workload took 5.96 s and peaked at 136.2 MiB. The warm weather codec regression moving010 also passed.
The represented flood compartments retain one finite owner each. This proof leaves out-of-capacity displacement, ordinary reach remapping, basin/cave contacts, broad floodplain routing and autonomous bed migration open.
Current-voxel ordinary reach storage
Commit a1703040 replaces only a watched eight-metre strip of the coarse reach capacity with four current-voxel cross-sections. The remaining prismatic section and surveyed endpoint links stay in the same owner. A raised internal saddle is refused because this representation has one stock. Capacity conflicts stay pending.
Guarded build038 and channel002 excavated the loaded ordinary reach in Zylann. Two cubic metres and the thermal and passive lanes stayed with the same owner. Stage moved from 1927.2180 m to 1924.6241 m below the 1927.1951 m outlet crest. The open outlet transferred no water after the edit. A separate Godot process recovered the same state and reproduced the next accepted interval byte for byte. The guard took 6.19 s with 137.5 MiB peak job memory. The represented strip is bounded. Larger cuts, internal barrier division, arbitrary deposits, full-reach adaptive geometry and autonomous migration remain open.
Flow-driven loose-bed movement
Commit 5042c059 consumes the accepted outlet velocity and hydraulic radius of the watched strip. A fixed Shields threshold for loose fine sand bounds bed exposure. A selected exponential upstream curvature weighting from MeanderPy guides bank preference. The V1 session reads current Zylann materials and validates the erodible sample before changing SDF. It updates the same occupied storage and accounts for one removed metre-grid sample at declared dry bulk density in the suspended lane. Pinned MeanderPy
Guarded build040 and erosion001 began with a sealed gate that produced zero exposure. After opening, 10.931 m³ passed in 115 s and the highest estimated shear was 0.490 Pa. The edit increased capacity while retaining 671.625 m³ with stage lowered by about 0.67 mm. The one credited 1,600 kg sample equivalent matched retained suspended mass, and duplicate credit was refused. A distinct Godot process reopened the terrain, exposure and sediment and reproduced the next state. Guarded runtime was 6.19 s with 137.7 MiB peak job memory.
The outlet shear serves as a local proxy. This test covers one threshold-driven edit and a sample-based sediment estimate. It leaves calibrated erosion, repeated centerline migration, deposition, vegetated and engineered bank campaign checks, cutoffs and normal gameplay scheduling open.
Rapid flow saved in transit
Commit d78a9bbf records the gate state, fine depth, two momenta, three constituent lanes and accepted time during exclusive delegation. A restored reach remains empty while the grid holds the parcel. The receipt checks the parcel’s finite volume and constituent balances. The ordinary surface and weather format is unchanged.
Guarded build043 and rapidresume001 repeated the native comparison against the pinned FluxCell implementation, with maximum absolute depth or momentum error 1.81 × 10⁻¹⁶. Godot captured the open gate after eight physical seconds, with 2.976 m³ downstream. A distinct Godot process loaded the saved terrain and water without the original recipe path. Both continuations reached 4.049 m³ downstream at ten seconds and returned 36 m³, 43.229088 GJ heat, 7.2 kg solute and 1.8 kg suspended material to the parent once. The active checkpoint, continued fine fields and reconciled checkpoint were byte-identical across processes. The complete guarded run took 10.63 s.
The parcel is isolated while the fine patch is active, the coarse links are closed, and the diagnostic gate overlies the generated bed. Moving coarse/fine exchange, edited rapid bed repair and overlapping fine ownership remain open.
Active rapid bed repair
Commit 25103282 tracks the fine cells touched by current terrain edits. The pending revision holds advancement, gate changes, reconciliation and water checkpoint publication. A complete batch uses current Zylann samples, retaining the existing fine depth, momentum, gate mask, heat, solute and suspended mass. The FluxCell step subsequently resolves the new surface slope. The water checkpoint stores the accepted bed with the current terrain database.
Guarded build044 and rapidterrain002 passed with a live cut, 35 resurveyed cells and a selected wet floor change from 1927.216 m to 1924.500 m at 0.410 m depth. The patch kept all 36 m³ in exclusive custody and the two independent processes reached matching checkpoint and continued bytes. The display check produced the edited wet-grid capture. The full run took 10.20 s and peaked at 407.9 MiB of kernel job memory. Unedited rapidresume002 again matched the pinned numerical reference, independent continuation and one coarse return. The initial rapidterrain001 stopped when the fixture tried to release the voxel lease before flushing its edit. The accepted fixture released it after the verified combined save.
The repair covers the represented free surface in one isolated patch. Edited fine stock stays in the patch until the coarse geometry can admit a measured handoff. Mobile boundaries, multi-patch exchange and cave topology remain open.
Recurrent finite-flow bank cuts
Commit ebd96023 services the watched ordinary reach at five-second hydraulic intervals inside an explicit physical horizon and bounded service budget. After each accepted interval it can consume the shear exposure for one current loose-bed change. The voxel lease is placed on the measured reach independently of a camera. Each edit follows the same current-voxel material and storage checks and credits the suspended lane exactly once.
Guarded build045 and erosioncycle001 used the same seeded reach as the single-cut control. The sealed 30 seconds produced zero exposure. The first cut occurred after 115 open seconds and 10.931 m³ of cumulative throughflow. The second occurred 50 seconds later at a neighboring solid sample, with 17.775 m³ of cumulative throughflow. Both processes matched the second terrain channel digest and exact native state, with two events and 3,200 kg of accumulated declared sediment. The guard took 6.14 s and peaked at 140.7 MiB. The first event remains on disk as the shared checkpoint, while the second is the continued state in each process.
This is a bounded repeated bank erosion check with the same finite water. Centerline migration, wider material feedback, deposition, coupled weather-driven erosion and cutoffs remain open.
