sources/src-env-v1-m3.title: V1 finite warm weather implementation evidence
sources/src-env-v1-m3.content:
Finite warm atmosphere and land exchange
Commit eeb07f99 ports Weather3D ce66920fd’s warm qsat and saturation adjustment with latent feedback. It applies CliMA CloudMicrophysics at f7e038e26c for fixed-threshold removal and bounded below-cloud evaporation. Finite vapor, liquid cloud, falling rain and the ground outbox own their respective water. Precipitation retains sensible heat, CFE takes it once, and actual ET returns its water and energy to its air column. The latent cost of CFE evaporation comes from the receiving column’s enthalpy. Both sides use the surface owner’s accepted physical time.
In the seed-713 test, a 60 s accepted slice formed 27.095 kg of cloud condensate in the upper layer and no rain reached land yet. At 3,600 s, 0.106371 m³ of rain had been accepted, 0.129784 m³ of actual ET returned to air and 0.001742 m³ of runoff reached surface water. The combined water residual was zero to the reported precision and the energy residual was −0.000122 J. The guarded native plus two Godot-process run completed in 5.89 s with 135 MiB peak job memory. The second process read in-flight rain and condensate from the saved world and matched the uninterrupted state byte for byte at both the checkpoint and the continued endpoint.
This is a closed warm-column case over two existing CFE footprints. Initial humidity, column geometry, fall speed and the humidity-derived ET demand are declared pilot settings. Circulation, rain shadows, cold phases, COARE open-water transfer, rendered clouds and measured production workload remain open.
Finite open-water heat and evaporation
Commit 5bbad4ef uses NOAA COARE 3.6 at bd1cac80 for the neutral freshwater roughness and transfer coefficients. The fixture supplies a declared 6 m/s reference wind. The open-water area comes from the local length of the prismatic wetted reach within the CFE footprint. Before crediting the air, the surface owner bounds both the sensible loss and evaporation by available water and thermal energy. Evaporation carries liquid sensible heat and latent energy. Solute and suspended mass stay in the water owners.
At 3,600 physical seconds, open water evaporated 0.003510 m³ and transferred 2.672 MJ of sensible heat to air. Rain delivery was 0.106371 m³ and actual soil ET was 0.129607 m³. Combined water, heat and passive mass checks passed. The native and two Godot-process check completed in 5.94 s with 136 MiB peak job memory. In-flight and continued saved states matched. This covers neutral open-water exchange with explicit wind. Stability, skin, salinity, dew and prognostic wind remain dependent work.
Native variable-mass pressure projection
Commit 6f8949b2 applies the Weather3D variable-column-mass correction on closed rectangular grids. Pinned BSD-licensed PocketFFT cosine transforms invert a flat Neumann reference operator for preconditioning. The iterative solve uses the actual terrain-weighted face masses. It withholds the corrected flux on nonconvergence and verifies divergence again from the accepted face field. Pinned PocketFFT
The generated seed-713 control removed a manufactured gradient and retained a known circulation. The first 250² control met the initial relative divergence test but exceeded its independent face-error tolerance. Tightening the residual target preserved the same face-error threshold. The accepted 125² result took 6.25 ms for 15 iterations, with relative divergence 1.44 × 10⁻¹³. The accepted 250² result took 23.51 ms for 14 iterations, with relative divergence 7.56 × 10⁻¹³ and maximum face error 2.49 × 10⁻⁸ kg/(m s). Both used the same 48 km resampled terrain crop. A forced one-iteration failure left the input flux unchanged.
These are single native pressure-kernel controls. They exclude layered momentum, moisture advection, coupled physical response, Godot and the cost of multiple stages per atmospheric step.
Hydrostatic circulation and conservative transport
Commit e2497325 ports the Weather3D downward hydrostatic diagnostic and pressure-gradient predictor into a native closed rectangular C-grid. It corrects horizontal dry-air face fluxes over terrain, derives the vertical mass flux from continuity and gives all carried scalars that same transport. A monotonized central limiter respects the donor dry-air Courant bound. The interval publishes all wind and scalar fields together. An oversized test step refused publication and preserved the initial fields.
The generated 64 × 48 km, 1 km grid used eight air layers over real land and sea elevations. A finite warm anomaly drove 5.31 m/s maximum horizontal wind and 2.48 kg/(m² s) maximum vertical dry-air flux at the 200 s endpoint. Relative pressure residual was 4.78 × 10⁻¹³. Relative energy conservation error was 1.78 × 10⁻¹⁴, vapor 8.81 × 10⁻¹⁶ and cloud water 5.41 × 10⁻¹⁶. Twenty 10 s steps took 123.55 ms in the native control, excluding startup and rendering. The scalar fields changed without external water sources.
This is the hydrostatic pressure and conservative transport path, ahead of nonlinear momentum, multi-stage time integration and rainfall over overlapping land footprints. At that checkpoint the bounded Godot warm-physics and rainfall path still used stationary columns. Weather-driven terrain response, cold phases, atmospheric grid continuation and large integrated performance remain open.
Coupled moving warm weather
Commit 7255aa04 combines the eight-layer circulation, finite warm phase transfer, CFE and neutral COARE in the same advancing session. Face fluxes carry heat, vapor, cloud liquid and falling rain with its heat. Rain is partitioned by rectangle overlap with surveyed CFE patches. Pending delivery retains weather custody. Uncovered rain is retained separately. CFE returns actual ET by receiving area, and COARE takes the local simulated wind and apportions the active wetted area by the channel centerline within each overlap.
The guarded build032 and moving006 used the seed-713 generated parcel and a 42-column crop. At one simulated hour the peak wind was 18.6729 m/s and cumulative horizontal rain transfer was 205.29 m³, counting repeat crossings. The connected footprints received 21.38 L of rain, fully consumed by CFE rain evaporation. Total actual CFE ET was 114.52 L. Finite open water returned 6.732 L of vapor and 5.101 MJ of sensible heat. Ground rain in columns with no receiver reached 67.18 m³. Native combined water residual was −8.99 × 10⁻¹¹ m³ and combined energy residual was −26.21 J. Peak job memory was 137.3 MiB for the native and two sequential headless Godot processes. Both saved the same endpoint from a checkpoint taken at 60 seconds with rain in flight.
The fixture has a finite initial anomaly, a closed crop and static atmospheric terrain. It verifies offscreen progression and local thermal and moisture exchange. It leaves rain-driven runoff in the moving fixture, mixed-phase physics, broader routing, nonlinear momentum, seasonal forcing, visual weather, normal gameplay adoption and large coupled resource measurements open.
Coupled mixed-phase weather
Commit 9bc119f3 uses Weather3D’s mixed water/ice saturation with a reduced bulk phase partition and finite falling snow. Four cloud/air lanes use limited transport. Falling rain and snow retain their own volume and energy pairs. Snow adds to a ground column reservoir and can melt only by drawing finite local sensible heat. Only liquid is offered to CFE.
Guarded build033 and mixed001 used the same seed-713 crop with a colder profile. At 60 seconds the air contained 124,878 kg of cloud ice and 3.133 m³ water-equivalent of falling snow. At 3,600 seconds the peak horizontal wind was 30.63 m/s, 82.84 m³ water-equivalent snow remained on the ground and 4.471 m³ had melted. Repeated snow volume transport summed to 1,760 m³ across horizontal faces. CFE received 24.44 L total liquid rain and accepted 20.79 L infiltration and 0.047 L runoff. Those totals combine liquid sources. Native combined water and heat residuals were 8.47 × 10⁻¹¹ m³ and −18.21 J. The run used 137.3 MiB peak job memory and 8.61 s of guarded wall time. A distinct Godot process reproduced the saved and continued state bytes. The warm control moving007 matched build032’s measured totals.
This bounded fixture uses bulk ice partition, fixed settling rates and local-air melt. Sublimation, snowpack physics, surface-water ice, seasonal and solar forcing, active atmospheric terrain remap and display-backed weather remain unverified.
Accepted cloud volume and motion
Commit a54c3a46 publishes bounded copied view data from the weather owner. World X/Z origin and spacing locate the cut cells. Each open layer carries its altitude interval, liquid and ice density and horizontal wind. Buried cells have zero thickness. The native check reconstructs cloud ice mass from the supplied density and terrain-cut volume.
Guarded build035, moving009 and mixed003 passed. Both Godot profiles matched their independently reopened cloud snapshots at 60 and 3,600 physical seconds. The digest covers geometry and field contents independently of time. The warm transient can clear by the endpoint. The snapshot is a rendering and gameplay input. The next check uses it in the display host.
Display-backed volumetric clouds
Commit 96fdc29c adapts the MIT SunshineClouds2 runtime at a73a80b0. It uploads the accepted liquid and ice field and cut-cell altitudes to a 3D raymarch. Presentation noise changes extinction inside occupied air. The compute path skips rays outside the weather volume, clips against opaque depth and reprojects the quarter-linear history. The scene supplies the current light direction and radiance. Pinned upstream
Guarded cloud007 used build035, Godot 4.5.1 Forward+, Vulkan and the RTX 2070 Super at 1920 × 1080. The 480 × 270 march used 40 primary and four lighting steps. Captures show below, above and inside views. At the fixed inside camera, changing the sun altered 21,881 sampled pixels at stride eight. The compositor’s dispatch-to-composite p95 was 2.966 ms over 62 GPU timestamps. Its nominal render textures totalled 28.18 MiB. Kernel job memory peaked at 1,240 MiB across the run. Clean teardown and a separate weather reopen passed. Earlier display setup never registered the effect because the Godot compositor getter returns a copy. The first registered capture exposed shutdown RID leaks, which the accepted run corrected.
The pictures show a small streamed patch and a finite layered cloud event. They do not establish production art quality, continuous severe weather, inclusive target frame time or fresh-world gameplay adoption.
Land heat and the solar boundary
Commit 156da4cd introduces optional cloud-attenuated shortwave, gray-sky longwave and a finite land slab in the moving atmosphere. The calendar uses specified latitude, season day and solar time. The thermal area excludes the represented water corridor. Sensible heat passes between the surface and the lowest open air, and surface temperature informs CFE evapotranspiration demand. Absorbed sunlight and emitted radiation appear explicitly in the combined budget.
Guarded build042 and solar001 advanced one hour across an equinox dusk at 35° latitude. Absorbed sunlight totalled 3.124 TJ and stopped after sunset. Longwave loss totalled 20.055 TJ, and land returned 7.468 TJ of sensible heat to the air over the whole hour. Mean land surface temperature fell from 289.589 K at dusk to 288.755 K after 30 dark minutes. Actual CFE evapotranspiration was 306.1 L in the bounded footprint. Combined residuals were 2.65 × 10⁻¹¹ m³ and −25.80 J. Independent Godot saved and continued state bytes matched. The guard took 8.66 s and peaked at 140.9 MiB.
This case uses a finite dry ground slab, coarse land coverage and a simplified radiative boundary. It leaves ocean heat forcing, seasonal validation, terrain-driven rainfall shadow, and sustained regional storms open.
Bounded display pacing
Commit 37cd5f67 services a supplied physical horizon in whole 10 s quanta. It leaves any fractional time as debt, updates the compositor from newly accepted cloud data and uses the accepted calendar to light the cloud volume.
Guarded build042 and pace002 used a freshly generated world, one 42-column mixed-phase crop with land radiation, and 1920 × 1080 Godot Forward+ on RTX 2070 Super. The paced window accepted 100 physical seconds in 12.533 wall seconds at a requested 8×. Peak debt was 9.997 seconds and end debt was zero. Across 754 frames, p95 was 16.909 ms and p99 was 17.076 ms. Across 750 GPU samples inside the window, cloud p95 was 2.939 ms. The longest environment service call in the window was 0.451 ms. A distinct Godot process reopened the earlier 60 s airborne checkpoint and reproduced the same water and cloud state at 3,600 s.
The window covers one active weather crop with streamed terrain and cloud rendering. The frame p95 exceeded 16.67 ms. This measurement leaves production colony integration and its sustained resource and rate targets open.
100 km moving warm weather
Commit 45058453 admits a larger saved grid on the geological lattice with a 14 km initial moisture anomaly. It uses the existing cut-cell circulation, common weather, CFE and COARE clock and finite pending rain. The two connected CFE footprints still occupy 800 m² combined. Rain outside that coverage stays in the weather owner’s ground stock.
Guarded build045 and regional001 opened a fresh 128 km terrain with 2 km geological and atmospheric spacing. The closed 100 × 100 km weather window had 2,500 columns and eight altitude layers. In one physical hour, 286 columns accumulated at least 0.01 mm of uncovered rain and the largest column depth was 0.870 mm. Off-footprint rain totalled 361,070 m³. The two actual land footprints received 679.4 L, including 610.7 L of accepted infiltration and 33.4 L of accepted runoff. Open water evaporated 10.83 L. Peak wind reached 40.24 m/s and cumulative horizontal rain transport was 73,367 m³, including repeat crossings. Native water and heat residuals were −4.78 × 10⁻⁷ m³ and −60.21 kJ across the entire window.
Two independent Godot processes matched their 60 s in-flight water and cloud records and their one-hour continued records. The first process spent 24.06 wall seconds accepting the last 3,540 physical seconds headlessly. The whole native and Godot guard took 102.05 s and peaked at 154.75 MiB. The local mixed-phase and radiation regression on the same build reproduced its prior endpoint exactly.
The regional fixture is a closed finite initial event with sparse land receivers and light rain. The large off-footprint stock establishes atmospheric rainfall and finite custody. It leaves severe rainfall, broad flood routing, recession, rendered regional pacing, and normal gameplay scale open.
Accepted clouds in the normal colony scene
Commit 6827168c uploads the accepted atmospheric field to the pinned SunshineClouds2 compositor in the normal colony scene. The volume uses the current horizontal render origin. The compositor stays outside the draw when the camera frustum cannot intersect occupied air. Initial render setup runs before the wall-time admission starts. A diagnostic sky view in the same scene looks at the accepted meteorology after the paired save has captured the environment.
Guarded build046 and colony011 ran the normal entry at 1920 × 1080 on the RTX 2070 Super. Sixteen actors reached 64 simulated seconds in 8.002 s. Frame p95 was 16.821 ms and p99 was 19.850 ms over 320 frames in the starting terrain view, where the cloud was out of view. A separate in-scene sky view gave 2.835 ms compositor GPU p95 across 39 timings. The fixed-camera image changed in 15,528 of 32,400 stride-eight samples when the compositor was enabled. The accepted atmosphere at the save was at 60 s, and the distinct headless reopen reached 120 s. The whole guard took 30.57 s and peaked at 2,040 MiB.
The attempted embark close to the weather footprint recorded about 66 ms frame p95, including in the same-site control with the compositor disabled. The accepted run kept the measured colony start and used the separate view for real cloud rendering. The capture shows the finite cloud’s bright layered extent. Sustained performance with the storm in view, cloud art acceptance, seasonal solar integration and broader precipitation routing remain open.

Source snapshot: published November 24 architecture-review commit b6003fe9f89d90b59bb9c847096c558f86e9fb71. This describes actual checked code, not a benchmark, current unpublished checkout or target architecture.

sources/src-water-upstream.title: Upstream water solver execution and regional source screen
sources/src-water-upstream.content:
Upstream hydraulic qualification, 26 November 2026
User requests continued research until water and terrain compatibility, scale and gameplay are confirmed. No runtime code changed. Historical failed water architecture remains replacement target. No unconditional new technology selection.
Actual FluxCell execution
Pin c62d8118839831529399b33815bac52a94738f55. The fetched upstream JS numerical module bodies were executed in V8 with ES module import/export bindings adapted to the execution harness. No flux equation was reimplemented. Source blob IDs: model 402bdd0f3f812cb482b7cdcca26326d8fdb64862; reference 69d2af9b2b2d49f172a937880174888e262ac74b; MUSCL reference 062f462d29b90106fb7bee2d4164d18b86e5ba27; analytical f5eb3840cb7c0d7bf571dfd99dcd13aa4e230edc; scenarios 65b4cdd000358d6b8bac83a709ba760321b36bb5.

Upstream exactScenario/cellAverages/depthErrors, 128 cells, t=2 seconds, wet dam mean absolute depth error (m): Rusanov 0.0219555, MUSCL-Hancock 0.00431223. Dry dam: 0.0214413 and 0.00500012. Max relative water residual 3.64e-16.
Rounded lake rest unchanged for 40 steps; dry rain at 2s depth 0.00002m; obstacle/dry dam volume conserved within about 2.27e-13 m³ absolute in these fixtures.
Custom fixture using actual CPU API: 24x8 one-metre cells, two-metre transverse ridge, initial left depth 0.8m, water 76.8m³, passive tracer amount 53.76 concentration*m³. Closed ridge to t=5s (141 steps): right remains dry. Reconstruct CPU solver with identical conserved state and one one-metre gate lowered, then run 8s (239 steps): left 69.2337948m³, gate 0.49515875m³, right 7.07104649m³, total 76.8m³, tracer 53.76. Negative setSources([112],[-0.2]) rejected. Withdraw 0.2m³ from cell via setState, preserving concentration and scaling momentum: stateEditVolume -0.2, water residual 1.39e-13m³, tracer residual -3.61e-14.
CPU reference does not expose GPU setBed. GPU setBed retains depth and changes bed/stage, accepts existing nonsolid cells, has fixed solid mask, and uses per-cell writes. Sparse sourceUpdates rejects negative rates. Need actual withdrawal, moving-solid, topology repair, parent/local exchange and target GPU tests. No claim of live GPU gate, cave or full game integration.
Broader attempt at seven upstream Node suites timed out; do not report full-suite pass. No target performance result, no GPU execution. CPU candidate earns priority on bounded correctness, not universal adoption.

Regional comparison
Wflow pin: surface_staggered_scheme.jl lines 674-758 and 1388-1515 merge river/floodplain storage, use entire land area for excess volume in 2D, clip negative stock and record error. Domain/network constructed from input at initialization; BMI get/set arrays not demonstrated mutable topology API. FAQ. Published v0.7.3 benchmark Rhine roughly 1km/daily forcing, 36 min CPU wall on single Xeon Gold 6144 thread per physical year excluding I/O: 2160/(36586400)144*1000 = 9.86 CPU-ms/game-s at historic 144 clock. Different version/hardware, not a current target result. Whole-model extrapolation is not a proof. Maintain candidate for catchment/soil water; do not lock stock surface hydraulics.
SFINCS 2025 peer-reviewed subgrid study: 100m subgrid comparable to 25m conventional in selected cases with 35-50x speedup, but 500m unresolved idealized meander overestimates discharge ~51%, 500m Houston water-level skill NSE near zero. High-resolution preprocessing, correct channel length and connected barriers matter. GPL-3.0 reference; no embedding/license commitment.
ADCIRC v56.2.1 source pin, LGPL-3.0-or-later core. VEW+condensed nodes relax across-channel CFL and preserve narrow river/embankment features; only lumped explicit modes. Source shared-library target and ADCIRC_Init/Run/Final found; module global and output dependencies remain. Subgrid plus condensed channel compatibility not established by source presence. VEW documentation, channel paper, 2025 subgrid resolution. Add regional contender, not accepted. No regional solver execution here: no Julia/installed regional binaries, full upstream checkout unavailable in execution environment. ANUGA flexible full SWE mesh is secondary candidate, not demonstrated subgrid narrow-channel CFL or mutable large-world fit. D-Flow FM attractive integrated 1D2D but AGPL distribution implications and full runtime requirements mean no priority over above absent license review.
Proposed decisive next gates (not approved thresholds)
Lock common physical clock scenario(s), closed ledger, barrier and geometry fixtures before selecting. Compare actual upstream regional candidates using same 1m creek in coarse land, meandering channel of known actual length, disconnected low basin behind crest, gate/dam open-close/reversal, finite rainfall/extraction and recession, offscreen 100x100km severe storm. Record solver accuracy/arrivals, water/sediment/heat accounting as applicable, peak work, inclusive CPU/GPU/memory (including setup and edits, queries, transfers, presentation). Example proposed trial targets, not changed requirements: exact no flow across sealed barrier, stage error <=0.05m in controlled geometry, arrival within 10% and flood footprint IoU >=0.90 where fine reference appropriate, closed relative residual <=1e-6 with absolute tolerance and no systematic water source. Historical 25 CPU-ms/game-s entire environment and 0.5ms water GPU/frame are starting gates; illustrative surface allocation <=8 CPU-ms/game-s not approved. Test physical-time policy explicitly; 1m cells over 100x100km are 10 billion cells/40GB per float32 field, world 16 trillion/64TB per field. 250m cells in storm 160k; must not assume that cell count alone proves throughput. Use source feature-aware storage curves and actual channel length/crest connectivity, not coarse mean heights or scanning global metre grids. A 1km trapezoidal channel, 1m bottom width, 1:1 side slopes and 0.5m depth has volume 750m³ and top area 2000m²; use as one known-answer geometry test. Gate cold/loaded terrain agreement and wet edits/erosion. Do not expand to full runtime until narrow solver, geometry and scaling evidence earns it.

spatial-architecture-selection.title: Spatial architecture selection
spatial-architecture-selection.content:
Spatial architecture selection
Status: provisional engineering selection, source-qualified only (25 November 2026). Read accepted LOD requirement, world scale, authority, performance targets, terrain contract, navigation contract, water contract and prior qualification plan. No runtime implementation or performance acceptance.
1. Current implementation and replacement delta
The published source at b6003fe9f89d90b59bb9c847096c558f86e9fb71 has a working conceptual separation between Zylann rendering/residency and native navigation. It does not establish inexpensive coarse simulation of all distant effects. Pinned source audit.





























ExistingDispositionZylann VoxelLodTerrain, Clipbox, SQLite modified-block persistenceRetain provisionally, replace generator inputRegionWorld, explicit offscreen terrain leases and current edit stampsRetain semantics for exact local queries; no routine lease for coarse domainsNavigation 16 m leaf, 4x axis hierarchy, 64 child reduction; retained fine-derived certificatesKeep useful coordinate and revision logic; replace long-range full-detail proof requirementSDF floor/crest and legacy channel preparationReplace routine geographical derivation; exact local sampling only for dirty edits or exceptional interactionsCurrent native periodic max circumference 1,024 kmConfigurable bounded world pilot; qualify 4,000 km wrapping separately, never imply existing periodic implementation already scales
The pinned VoxelGenerator header supplies multithread-safe block generation with integer origin and LOD, optional series query, and a caller-owned voxel buffer. VoxelViewer allows visual/collision/data-notification needs to differ. SQLite stream format supports string and wider binary block keys. These already cover much of fine residency; avoid a new general-purpose voxel cache or per-colonist viewer. The pinned tree already includes FastNoise2; use existing graph/noise facilities where useful, do not import another noise package by default.
2. Select the simple structure for the pilot
Shared metric integer X/Z coordinates and local Y-up metre geometry, not a universal scene-tree hierarchy. One world identity/configuration. Existing checked 64-bit coordinates can be retained if verified; render relative to a local origin. Use a bounded rectangular world initially. Optional periodic topology must preserve actual extent, wrap intersections and seam identities; never silently pad the world. Arbitrary world dimensions use exact partial-edge area and boundary handling.
Logical addressing: a 16 km region/page, integer page coordinate and domain/field/level identifier; globally dense macro row-major arrays and a compact direct page directory. Region keys locate data, not ownership. Dense hot indices are not durable IDs. Use checked floor division for negative coordinates; local float coordinates only after origin subtraction. No pointer-rich octree for ordinary horizontal cells. Existing 16 m/32 m voxel blocks remain an independent 3D lattice. 250 m horizontal samples need not align to every voxel block. Where domains differ, exact overlap weights and feature contacts link them. Optional Morton sorting is a later measured optimization, not a prerequisite.
Pilot sizes (configurable, not hard requirements):















































RepresentationScale at 256 km baseline4,000 km candidateResidency / useMacro geological and geographic fields1 km (256²)approximately 4 km (1,000², or supported GeoGenesis sample count with explicit physical spacing)Whole world, cold formation and permanent compressed baselineRegional geographic/land refinement250 m1 km and 250 m only where meaningfulBounded page access and compact summary/latent recipe; actual land-water stores chosen by solverAdministrative page16 km16 kmDirect lookup; descriptor references optional field payloads and topology revisionsRiver/valley/lake/barrier featurePhysical coordinates and width/depth, independent of rasterSame principleCompact persistent network and sparse detailed profiles; latent detail if provable from recipeVolumetric terrain1 m base sample, adjustable; extra local fidelity if neededSameZylann request-driven generation and durable editsAtmosphere / soil / navigationIndependent field scales and intervalsIndependently qualifyMay share page/index coordinates without sharing representation
Do not require all 250 m pages to exist simultaneously. A region may have persistent coarse water, vegetation or human activity when its fine payload is absent. If an authoritative state has been refined or edited, keep its actual state/delta in memory or storage and ensure due events are applied; evict derived cache first, not physical consequences. Persist unresolved incoming amounts/time horizons until processed. No every-page catchup that silently stalls large active worlds. Base geometry and current edit layers are distinct; a coarse surface cannot be used as exact cave occupancy. A narrow stream must remain a feature even below the regional sample spacing.
Resource arithmetic, not measurements

4,000 km at 16 km gives 250 x 250 = 62,500 page descriptors. At an illustrative 32 B each: 1.91 MiB, before payloads.
4 km global samples: 1,000,000 cells. At 64 B/cell: 61.04 MiB.
1 km global samples: 16,000,000 cells. At 16 B/cell: 244.14 MiB; at 64 B/cell: 976.56 MiB.
250 m global: 256,000,000 cells, 15.26 GiB at 64 B/cell. A single 16 km page is 64² samples, 256 KiB at that stride; a 1024-page working set is 256 MiB. Not a mandated cache cap.
1 m global 2D footprint: 16 trillion samples, about 931 TiB at 64 B/sample, excluding vertical geometry.

Birth/age, derived geometry, scratch, active owners, caches, snapshots, edit journal and autosave must each be measured; a packed illustrative byte stride is not a memory estimate for GeoGenesis or any real solver. Bound total work with domain-specific cadence and active partitions. A storage page is not a simulation unit and must not force every owner to tick together.
3. Geographic data flow

Birth and age: run the accepted provisional GeoGenesis single-shot connected coarse simulation. Export final original surface, soil/sediment/geology, drainage area/receiver/order and refreshed climate/diagnostic runoff in explicit units. Use hydrology::route after age; lake fill depth is capacity diagnostic, not finite inventory. Preserve terminal basins; do not discard water at the root. Do not use the initial-only tiled path as if it aged regions. One-time field handoff; no second mutable formation world.
Coarse topology and boundaries: retain stable downstream contacts, closed-basin/spill identities, crossing positions and profiles, catchment extent and region revisions. Each region uses agreed physical boundary data derived once from the parent geography; arbitrary tile boundaries are not outlets. A region with no explicit drain is not automatically sea. Persist a resolved topology change when a dam or incision changes a crossing. Evaluate narrower drainage-aware refinement algorithms for tributaries before selecting them.
Detail realization: pilot the MIT Procedural World Generation donor. Its CPU channel and slope-conditioned detail routines accept supplied coarse/river inputs. Use or port only the reusable numerical pieces after license notices and source equivalence tests. Stable bed/bank geometry, not current water stage, constrains terrain. Sample globally keyed deterministic detail; bounded halo with canonical constraints; if drainage depends beyond halo, request/reconcile the affected parent/basin summary, not a new arbitrary border outlet. A render-dependent blend is not physical terrain authority. Additional source review found a deterministic local creek/trunk generator; its authoritative parent-outlet and closed-basin consistency remains open. See formation comparison.
Current geometry: Zylann renders/generates from the canonical region recipe and edit overlay. Coarse consumers derive geometry from the same recipe, feature profiles, and durable edits. Provide direct native block/batch evaluation without requesting scene nodes, voxel viewers or GPU readbacks on routine coarse queries. A mesh may approximate but cannot alter true bank/barrier or cave occupancy. Fine SDF acquisition is for local edits, exact interactions and exceptional corrections.
Process state: each solver owns its evolving quantities. Coarse surface stores retain distinct connected partitions, stage-volume and connections; channel geometry is a constraint, not water inventory. At promotion partition volume and constituent mass to children; at restriction aggregate accepted amounts; reconcile cross-boundary flux over the same interval. A camera movement alone must not change where water flows, how long travel takes or resource totals. Live erosion commits terrain deltas from actual forcing; do not recarve geometry each time a river rises.

A newly generated fine tributary may not contradict previously simulated parent runoff/route/basin outcomes. Its latent recipe or aggregate partition must constrain the prior simulation. If unresolved, label precision and require reconciliation before claiming exact topology, not a fictional fully resolved network. Closed depressions and narrow streams cannot be represented solely by average height. Large regional reroutes may require wider topology repair; local cost guarantee is limited to genuinely local edits.
4. Reuse selection













































ComponentRecommendationWhyGeoGenesisRetain provisional formation choiceConnected coarse geological age; flat fields, existing drainage kernel; no aged fine-tile refinerZylannRetain provisional fine terrain choiceExisting streaming/meshing/editing, no new volume engineProcedural World GenerationFirst refinement geometry donor to qualifyMIT, CPU routines exist for profiles, bounded carving and coarse-conditioned height; includes local trunk/creek generation; authoritative topology remains unqualifiedterrain-generator, flowing-terrainSecondary small donorsUseful isolated primitives, border and closed-basin limitationsMAIForge, hydrological construction trees, procedural planet river networksAlgorithm referencesClosely relevant regional outlet constraints; no permissive fully qualified implementation of complete refinementAMReX, OpenVDBNot the foundationScientific adaptive grids/volume storage add another layer; no need unless a particular qualified solver requires themlibmortonOptional after profilingNot needed for simple page lookup
Minimum custom code: field handoff/versioning, checked keys and page residency boundary, existing numerical-kernel adapter, feature-to-current-terrain contract, boundary reconciliation and dirty publication. Not a new custom renderer, sparse volume format, terrain erosion engine or navigation runtime. The outstanding tributary construction is real engineering risk, not hidden behind the term ‘hierarchy’.
5. First bounded qualification package
See spatial qualification. First run should be limited to formation plus geometry/refinement; no water runtime replacement, atmosphere, ECS migration or massive game build yet.

Confirm actual checkout, dependency pins and current Zylann generator extension boundary. Use the existing build tools and separate scratch lineage. Test negative coordinates, region boundaries, arbitrary edge extents and 4,000 km indexing without fine allocations.
Build the pinned GeoGenesis core with a minimal export, age one 256 km seed, refresh drainage, measure birth, age and field handoff separately. First use a small known two-region topological fixture to validate the donor, then use actual naturally generated terrain; do not present a manually placed creek fixture as a natural river generation pass.
Exercise the source donor CPU routines with a predeclared pair of adjacent regions, crossing channel profile, terminal depression, slope and spill control. Measure source baseline and native integration separately. Compare same sample positions from both evaluation orders, with neighbor absent/present, after eviction and after independent restart. Parent outlets, shared bank/bed profiles and basin identities must agree; no false drain or inserted water. For a roughly 1 m stream verify continuous feature geometry at finer local measurement resolution, and validate what the selected voxel/mesher resolution can actually represent.
Demonstrate an edit (dam or excavation) changes the relevant topology/summary and persists, including an offscreen edit. Track affected pages, requested voxel blocks and bytes. Invalidated data returns pending/coarse until its actual dependency is resolved; unrelated pages do not rebuild.
Measure complete small-world startup to macro-ready, feature-ready, and interactive terrain-ready. Then scale the macro/address/page directory probe to 4,000 km, not a fake fine-world test. Track inclusive CPU time, peak memory, generated/resident blocks and per-page latency. Compare images in the normal Godot host if integration reaches that point. Use historical 1 s 256 km macro/initial target and few seconds large-world macro separately from aging; record misses without altering physical clocks or excluding prep.

Pass criteria for qualification: no dense fine-world allocation; deterministic same-revision shared authoritative samples (within declared numeric precision), feature/closed-basin continuity, durable edit and bounded resident work independent of camera; agreed geometric error thresholds frozen before tests; actual measured cost and rendered quality. Failure returns to candidate research, not a mandate to build an entire new terrain engine. Broad storm, conservative transfers and 800 km travel are the subsequent consumer gates, not proven by the spatial fixture.
Open: Q-GRID exact domain resolutions; Q-REFINE fine tributary/saddle construction and topology summaries; hydraulic and atmosphere algorithm selection. This record selects a structure and a first permissive refinement donor to test, not finished solver implementation.
Formation review supplement
The spatial structure remains proposed unchanged. The subsequent formation comparison supersedes the earlier assumption that only GeoGenesis should be evaluated for birth. Test Procedural World Generation as a full alternative before committing to the source of the macro fields. The existing GeoGenesis-only fixture remains a comparison path, not a mandate.

spatial-qualification.title: Spatial qualification plan
spatial-qualification.content:
Spatial qualification plan
Status: proposed research and implementation qualification sequence. No runtime execution authorized. Read DEC-SPATIAL-PILOT, Q-GRID, Q-REFINE and REQ-BUDGET.
A. Shared field and topology contract
For every candidate record: upstream commit/license/dependencies, actual input/output storage, ownership, units, supported topology, required initialization, per-step/repair complexity, clock, thread count, CPU/GPU traffic, scratch, snapshot and persistence cost. Identify whether an implementation or only a paper is available. Do not invent a custom solver merely because an algorithm has a familiar name.
A region key identifies world, coordinate and level, not authority. Use integer/double coordinates for giant worlds with local render transforms. Fields specify physical extent, sample convention, units, geometry/version, time interval and exact/coarse/pending/stale state. Wrapping is an explicit boundary policy.
B. Formation/refinement gate

Run GeoGenesis single-shot coarse age at 256² or 512²; export final original bed, fresh climate/receivers, material and soil descriptors, and units. Time generation, age and export separately.
Compare reusable drainage-aware refinement: coarse-to-fine feature constraints or regional evolution. Use two adjacent regions and a shared boundary crossing, one narrow creek, two distinct basins and a known spill threshold. Test with deliberately shifted fine relief, alternate generation orders, eviction and reload. Geometry and topology must agree; a nicer image alone fails.
Preserve upstream/outlet IDs and boundary elevation/profile; do not force every depression to drain. Exclude fake filled water depth from initial mass. Capture actual Godot terrain from the same source when the integration is authorized.
Scale probe macro 4,000 km without allocating all 250 m or metre geometry. Measure total bytes, source generation, topology preparation, and initial interactive readiness separately. Reject hidden global fine preprocessing.

C. Broad flood gate
A 100 x 100 km island is 160,000 cells at 250 m, 10,000 at 1 km, versus 10 billion at metre spacing. Select actual subgrid transport methods and compare coarse and finer reference results for a severe storm covering the island. Include a protected lowland behind a levee, closed lake, dam/diversion, downstream flooding, recession, soil infiltration and evaporation. No global promotion to fine solver. Quantify mass error, flood extent, duration, water level and arrival error independently; define acceptable numerical tolerances before the test. Report fine residency high-water mark and work during peak flood. An island-wide wetness overlay is not a hydraulic pass.
D. Cross-system authority gate
Demonstrate one interval of actual evaporation -> vapor advection -> condensation -> precipitation -> land runoff -> finite water storage -> actual erosion forcing. Add sparse basic contamination and representative non-water inventory when qualifying liquid transport. No double crediting water or material. Show how vegetation consumes soil moisture and weather, and how vegetation feedback changes ET and erosion resistance. Validate direction and units of current/wind fields. Save/reload pending intervals and offscreen edits.
E. Navigation/entity gate
Plan a route across 800 km without loading a continuous metre-scale corridor. Use region/portal summaries; refinement is for uncertain crossings and consequential local motion, not all distant traversals. Include a bridge or pass that closes from flooding and a cave/multifloor route. Unknown/pending/stale never equals proven blocked or exact valid. Compare travel time and arrival to a smaller fine reference, and test batched repeated work cycles with finite supplies. Evaluate a common ECS plus prebuilt local navigation/crowd candidates in 1k, 10k, 100k mixed active populations; no empty-entity benchmark.
Decision checkpoints

































QuestionDecision evidence requiredQ-REFINELicensed reusable method, deterministic seam, narrow-stream/lake geometry and actual startup costQ-GRIDDomain resolution and ownership table with complete memory/work measurements, large-world scalingQ-FLOODSigned transport law, finite storage, protected lowland and whole-island stormQ-ATMOSActual wind/moisture transport, finite precipitation cycle and severe-weather costQ-EROSIONReusable kernel with actual runtime flux/material input, bounded terrain editsQ-NAVLong-distance planning without full fine residency, dynamic hazards, crowd and refinement tests
The priority is to close formation/geometry contracts and hydraulic/atmospheric selection in parallel with the smallest cross-domain proofs, not complete every later feature now. Retain historical failures and distinguish source facts, theoretical estimates, small tests and production acceptance.
Coupled compatibility prerequisite for final formation selection
Use formation comparison as the early interface gate. Validate a newly added landform, terrain summaries, actual finite water and atmospheric exchanges together before locking the production terrain handoff. The earlier standalone formation/refinement experiment remains valuable and can run in parallel with solver qualification; its success alone must not be reported as full water/weather compatibility. The complete hydraulic, atmosphere, erosion and large-world gates remain separate, unresolved requirements.

systems/sys-atmos.title: Atmospheric dynamics and climate
systems/sys-atmos.content:
Atmospheric dynamics and climate
Select lightweight circulation and conservative transport kernel. Coarse horizontal model with vertical extension candidate; not fixed pressure-solver choice. Wind, thermal forcing, humidity, uplift, seasonal and diurnal changes, cloud transport and finite actual evaporation. Supply vector fields to clouds, vegetation, currents and fire/smoke later. Weather evolves offscreen; extreme storms remain cheap.
The bounded V1 Godot session advances eight terrain-derived air layers with Weather3D hydrostatic flow, finite warm precipitation and exact-area land overlap. Actual CFE ET and wind-driven neutral COARE exchange share the accepted clock. Independent recovery matched the continued state with rain in flight. The colder profile also preserves finite cloud ice and snow through recovery and heat-limited melt. Rendered weather, normal world integration and the wider workload remain open. Moving weather evidence
The bounded V1 dusk case includes solar heat, emitted longwave and a finite land heat slab on the accepted clock. Regional and seasonal qualification remain open. Radiation evidence

systems/sys-flood.title: Regional flooding
systems/sys-flood.content:
Regional flooding
Use subgrid stage-volume and face/sill geometry or other qualified method preserving levees and connected depressions. Coarse flooding must be real and persistent. Do not activate a metre solver on every wet region. Local refinement only if error or specific interaction warrants it. Expose approximate depth/current/duration/extent with accuracy labels. Qualify simultaneous island-wide storm and recession, dam breach, offscreen settlement impacts, memory and work bounds.
One native V1 bank corridor and lateral connection now carry finite overbank water with their own stage-volume curves. The headless Godot session matches the bounded native gate and wetting result. Whole-island coverage and timing remain open. V1 floodplain evidence
The bounded lateral face now fences time on a current voxel revision and rebuilds its surveyed cross section from the Zylann read lease. Closing the path by an earth edit and restoring it by verified terrain rollback both affected real finite transfer. The compartment storage curves still use the original survey. V1 face repair evidence
One bounded V1 floodplain restores its current-voxel wet storage and bank/lateral face geometry with the same finite owners. Excavation changed stage while preserving the original parcel through independent Godot continuation. Large capacity conflicts and wider flood routing remain open. Wet storage evidence

systems/sys-lod.title: Spatial hierarchy and residency
systems/sys-lod.content:
Spatial hierarchy and residency
Logical world always exists. Coarse authoritative stores and persistent feature summaries may be resident globally; fine procedural blocks are generated/read on demand, edited blocks durable. Separate terrain data residency, rendering LOD, simulation LOD, navigation abstraction and entity detail. A coarse cell need not represent a single river or traversable passage. Use stable coordinates, revision-stamped summaries and bounded caches. Promotion/restriction preserves volume, material, population identity and causal events; no duplicated owner. Exact spatial scales/tiling open, not fixed 1 km or 250 m.
Verified published implementation boundary
Current spatial source audit distinguishes existing camera-independent leases, fine navigation copies, summary residency and the exact remote-segment restriction. The spatial pilot is the proposed replacement qualification, not an implementation claim.

systems/sys-refine.title: Geographic refinement and drainage
systems/sys-refine.content:
Geographic refinement and drainage
The target geometry contract is unchanged. Fine regions and features must agree across tile boundaries, preserve river connectivity and downhill grades, lake boundaries, and watershed structure; not noise added independently. A narrow creek is a persistent subgrid feature, not averaged away. Investigate reusable procedural hydrology and multiresolution erosion; share deterministic generator and relevant feature geometry with terrain and hydraulic derivation. No resurrection of LandscapeChannels.
Candidate narrowed
The first permissive geometry donor is Procedural World Generation; the remaining topology question is explicitly open. See spatial architecture selection. No implementation status change.
Updated research boundary
Procedural World Generation’s creekGen is a concrete deterministic trunk and tributary-growth donor, not yet an authoritative refined drainage network. Qualify it with a fixed geometry callback, parent outlet and basin consistency, and residency-independent results. The remaining work is integration and verification, not automatically writing a tributary engine from scratch. See formation comparison.
V1 applies selected PWG channel geometry over the deterministic GeoGenesis receiver graph. One generated parcel checked a visible curved channel, a linked 1 m tributary, shared sampler cross-sections and separately distinguished marine and inland bodies. Candidate crests and unresolved contacts remain preparatory inputs to water closure. V1 terrain evidence

systems/sys-surface.title: Surface water and routing
systems/sys-surface.content:
Surface water and routing
Select actual reusable numerical method; a graph is not a solver. Store finite volume and geometry-dependent stage; explicit travel/residence, backwater, reversal, dry/wet transitions, barriers, controlled withdrawals and downstream consequences. Precomputed geometry from terrain revisions; no routine SDF reconstruction. Existing SWMM and CaMa coupling failed qualification. Subgrid flood capability mandatory, local refinement optional. Surface hydraulic queries feed gameplay and erosion; candidate clocks must not disguise physical time.
The Wflow-derived V1 owner now checks finite signed routing, explicit blocked and open gates, bounded extraction and stage-clipped display on a generated pair. The old SWMM and CaMa links retain their historical qualification failures. The new branch has no integrated performance, above-bank flood or persistence pass. V1 water evidence
A 24 × 48 FluxCell patch now advances in the V1 session with exclusive custody of one whole donor parcel. The sealed and opened gate checks match the pinned reference and the matching Godot run. Wide-area flood exchange and partial spatial transfer to an active fine boundary remain open. V1 rapid-water evidence

systems/sys-terrain.title: Editable volumetric terrain
systems/sys-terrain.content:
Editable volumetric terrain
Current documented: Zylann Voxel Tools 1.7.0, pinned 75d3c6d996ed2331c80edcd8c3ebc947afc0f041; X/Z horizontal, Y-up, metre negative-solid SDF, streaming/Transvoxel. This is a documented existing boundary, not immutable target implementation. Reassess Zylann only if evidence justifies it. Generated baseline plus durable edit overlay yields current geometry. Meshes/colliders are derived. Queries and dirty notices must support offscreen fine terrain without reconstructing globally.
V1 has a native immutable bed sampler feeding a display-backed Zylann inspection scene. LOD0 and LOD2 SDF and an actual current voxel edit were checked. V1 geological texturing, normal gameplay admission and cold edit continuation remain open. First V1 terrain evidence
The bounded V1 terrain session now maps formation soil, sediment and rock to the existing voxel material channels. A RegionWorld mine and independent cold reopen verified exact current SDF and material bytes. Broader geology and visual acceptance remain open. V1 terrain evidence

systems/sys-time.title: Time, settings and clocks
systems/sys-time.content:
Time, settings and clocks
Store settings in validated versioned configuration with defaults and permitted ranges. World day 600 s at 1x, year 60 days default. No universal fixed step. Explicit seconds, game calendar, geological years and solver intervals; track elapsed work and pending events. No compressed physical clock to pass performance. Config changes requiring regeneration or incompatible state must be explicit.

systems/sys-world.title: World formation
systems/sys-world.content:
World formation
Target: varied continents/islands, mountains, valleys, hills, cliffs, plateaus, coastlines, climate zones and strata. GeoGenesis provisional for initial coarse formation. Export final fields once to shared geography; use deterministic world seed/config. Initial macro generation and aging separately timed. No claim full volumetric caves or ore bodies supplied by a 2D formation grid. Current documented native LandscapeFormation is a replacement subject, not target architecture.
The first V1 package generates a configurable bounded parcel and serializes an immutable aged recipe with settings, climate and routing provenance. Offline 4,000 km formation and export ran on a 4 km grid. Normal fresh-world admission, fine streaming and integrated scale remain pending. First V1 terrain evidence

water-first-qualification-plan.title: Water-first integrated qualification plan
water-first-qualification-plan.content:
Water-first integrated qualification plan
26 November 2026. Proposed concrete next work package consolidating the user’s stylized-river clarification and prior negative/positive evidence. This is a qualification plan, not an approved production dependency selection or authorization to change game code. See integrated decision, water upstream evidence, pressure tests, stylized water requirement and spatial qualification.
Architecture
GeoGenesis + selected PWG morphology + Zylann remain user-stated soft lock, conditional on a shared hydraulic feature export. Generate and age a single landscape, select meaningful channels using climate/runoff/slope and adjustable channel-initiation thresholds; aggregate minor drainage into finite catchment/soil/aquifer flow. Preserve narrow creeks where useful, not maximum natural network density. A single stable geometry recipe defines terrain solids, channel paths, length/cross-section, banks, storage-volume and wetted-area curves, disconnected basins, sills, structures and cave contacts. Geometry control points, numerical reaches and rendering samples have independent resolution. No world-sized fine DEM or voxel scan.
For prehistory use GeoGenesis coarse climatology and erosion (qualify discharge-aware forcing). Runtime uses actual external hydraulic and atmosphere quantities; no second GeoGenesis water inventory or whole-world geological rerun. MeanderPy is a source-screened slow morphology candidate only; couple actual accumulated flow, sediment and material resistance, protect reinforced/rock banks, commit physical geometry changes and preserve water/constituents and navigation revisions. Initial morphology and live migration are distinct.
Ordered qualification, upstream first

Freeze fixture geometries, density/shape presets, physical clock scenarios and gameplay tolerances before execution. Use the 600-second calendar day, but declare physical seconds per game-second separately; compare illustrative multipliers 1, 12 and historical 144 to expose cost/behaviour, not as approved clock changes. Record target CPU/GPU/RAM/time debt and meaningful arrival/depth/hazard; retain historical 25 aggregate CPU-ms/game-s environmental comparator and 8x rendered 60 FPS on Ryzen 3700X/RTX 2070 SUPER/32 GB. No silent clock changes or hidden work.
Execute pinned GeoGenesis and selected PWG upstream routines on bounded adjacent areas; verify drainage continuity, retained closed basin, real 1m creek, actual meander length, cross sections, crest and storage geometry, generation order and cold/fine consistency with Zylann when host work is authorized. Compare sparse versus denser channel network and record counts, preparation and memory. No return to LandscapeChannels or scan-heavy legacy pipeline.
Start actual Wflow upstream tests for soil/runoff and one-dimensional signed river routing. Test no-loss finite water, backwater/reversal, abstraction, connection barriers, and the regional storm. Stock common-stage river/floodplain coupling and clipping are known blockers, not automatically accepted. Prefer one regional model that satisfies both river and connected flood storage. If stock Wflow regional surface coupling fails, keep land-only as a candidate and compare SFINCS for subgrid independent reference (GPL code embedding not approved), ADCIRC for integrated narrow-channel and floodplain challenger (LGPL obligations and mesh repair unresolved). mizuRoute ordinary downhill routing is conditional only if it earns extra integration complexity and preserves finite delayed stock and affected boundaries. Do not commit to all candidates or write a new numerical engine as default. FluxCell is the preferred local detailed reference following bounded CPU tests, conditional on actual GPU/CPU budget, withdrawal, dynamic obstacle repair and regional exchange. For ordinary slow water prioritize cheaper reach/connected storage; no widespread forced fine solver. Cave compartments and finite coastal/ocean stores must have explicit interfaces and their own acceptance cases.
Run actual reduced atmospheric candidates with coarse 16–32km horizontal transport and configurable layers as initial experiments, not fixed requirements. Weather3D reduced equations, JCM and CliMT are leads rather than adopted packages; compare cheap diagnostic wind/thermal uplift against reduced prognostic dynamics. MC-limited conservative transport has isolated tests, CliMA 0M/ERF and COARE are physics leads. Require actual wind and temperature responses, moisture advection, condensation and precipitation including snow/ice as appropriate, finite surface evaporation/ET and heat accounting. No prescribed wind/rain fixture can prove emergent atmospheric circulation.
Couple smallest terrain and hydrology slice first with metered rain, then replace forcing with actual selected atmosphere. Atmospheric rain (kg or m3 over explicit interval) partitions by contributing area and geometry into water/land once; land consumes finite infiltration, runoff and actual ET; channels receive runoff once; accepted evaporation debits stores and credits air moisture with consistent latent/sensible heat; cloud coverage and land feedback change energy exchange. Avoid duplicate soil/GW, rainfall, lake stocks and coarse/fine water. Derive renderer from physical coverage/base/top and motion; true bounded volumetric raymarching, SunshineClouds2 comparison, moving sun and camera on real target. Hydraulics return stage/discharge/wetted area/velocity/erosive exposure; erosion updates solid geometry, then recompute affected water and navigation connections. Require offscreen, edit, reload and conserved in-transit state. Real river migration and rendering are separate quality gates.
Escalate from one small connected valley (mountains, stream, river, lake, dam, protected settlement, cave, soil/aquifer, persistent downstream effects) to 100x100km severe storm/recession, multi-active regions and 4000km macro. Full water cycle includes ocean exchange, snow/ice, groundwater/caves, other liquids and contamination at suitable later gates; a warm-water prototype does not waive them. Test drought/rain, repeated changes, ecological and navigation consequences, actual Godot visual quality, integrated CPU/GPU/RAM/latency/save/debt. Only after evidence accept production dependency choices, not by isolated kernel correctness. If candidate fails identify physical, data-prep, topology, license or runtime cost reason and switch to the next upstream alternative rather than reconstruct failed architecture. No claim of full performance or full water/weather compatibility today.

Decision state
Architecture and prioritization concrete; regional surface solver, land/groundwater combination, atmospheric circulation and actual renderer performance remain open. No newly authorized solver, source port, budget, numeric tolerance or runtime work. User explicitly values plausible stylized channels and finite coupled effects over forecast precision. This ordering is a proposed operational consolidation, not new research evidence or a promise of qualification.
Sequencing supersession (26 November 2026)
The user agreed to implementation-first selection. Use Environmental Foundation V1 for the current plan; this earlier comparative qualification sequence is historical research context. Carry forward meaningful checks as ordinary implementation acceptance, not independent competing full-engine campaigns.

workflow.title: Working with the brain
workflow.content:
Working with the brain

Read the home, record-index.json and relevant requirements, contracts, systems and evidence. Follow typed edges in both directions.
Capture a thought, proposed requirement or question. Use a permanent uppercase ID such as THO-FLOOD-IDEA. Filenames may match case-insensitively. Do not rename existing IDs.
Pages CMS edits authored Markdown and metadata in eight collections. Generated connections are injected into the Quartz stage, never into the editor body. Do not manually edit generated views or index.
On the dedicated brain branch, validated edits trigger an automatic refresh. Agents can run python docs/brain/tools/atlas.py --write and --check; run python docs/brain/tools/test_brain.py for editor payload checks. A failed validation requires correcting the record, not bypassing the checks.
Distinguish user intent, proposal, implementation and measured validation. Capture source/version/license, API, performance/units and limitations. No engine changes follow from note edits. Validated Brain branch edits rebuild the user-approved public GitHub Pages documentation and publish only generated files to caleb-var/breachborn-brain/main/docs. All authoring stays in the private game repository; never edit the public mirror. All authored content including inbox is public by default; keep confidential notes outside content/.

Open Pages CMS after account authorization. GitHub Markdown editing remains available.
